docs.title: ECGEN
docs.text:
ECGEN is a research framework for generative modeling of 12-lead electrocardiograms, built on PyTorch Lightning. It provides model implementations, dataset loaders, one YAML-driven training command (ecgen train), evaluation metrics and visualization tools.

  • Get started

    Install the package and train your first model on MIMIC-IV-ECG.

    Installation · Quick Start

  • Models

    VAE, VQ-VAE with a PixelCNN prior, and the Pulse2Pulse GAN.

    Architecture overview

  • Training

    One command for every model: ecgen train <config.yaml> [key=value ...].

    Training with ecgen train

  • API reference

    Generated from the source docstrings.

    API reference

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vlbthambawita/ECGEN.git
cd ECGEN
pip install -e .

# Train a VQ-VAE (stage 1); overrides follow the config
ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml data.dataset.params.root=/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg

# then its prior (stage 2)
ecgen train configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml \
    model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt

from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning

model = VAELightning.load_from_checkpoint("runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt")
samples = model.sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000)

Note

See Training with ecgen train for the CLI, the config schema and the run directory layout. The Lightning wrappers rebuild their config from the flat hyperparameters stored in the checkpoint, so load_from_checkpoint(path) needs no extra arguments. See VAE for details.

docs.title: v1.1.0 - Generative Training Library, Phases 1–8
docs.text:
Phases 1–8 of PLAN_TRAINING_LIBRARY.md, on top of Phase 0 below.

  • Conditioning (Phase 1). ecgen.conditioning: field encoders (categorical, multilabel, numeric, fourier, masked_signal, later text_hash, text) → ConditionOutput(vector, tokens, dense); per-field dropout with learned null embeddings; zero-initialised injection layers (FiLM, AdaGN, AdaLNZero, AddToTimeEmb, CrossAttention1d); observation masks (data.masks); checkpoints carry the training data contract so sample(cond=...) takes raw units.
  • Conditional families (Phase 2). Conditional VAE (FiLM, learned prior, latent_type: global), conditional / paired Pulse2Pulse (projection critic, lead reconstruction with L1, output_scale), conditional PixelCNN prior with classifier-free guidance. Fix: the Pulse2Pulse critic's final layer was never in its optimizer.
  • Diffusion (Phase 3) and flow matching (Phase 4) in one ContinuousGenerativeModule: DDPM (ε/v/x₀, cosine/linear, min-SNR, DDIM/ancestral) and rectified flow (logit-normal t, OT coupling, Euler/Heun); unet1d backbone; EMA; CFG; SSSD-style partial-ECG training; training-free replace / RePaint inpainting.
  • Latent models and backbones (Phase 5). latent_diffusion, latent_flow_matching on frozen VAE / VQ-VAE; dit1d, ssm (S4D), mamba backbones.
  • PTB-XL and text (Phase 6). ptbxl dataset (SCP vocabularies, demographics, sex, reports, PTB-XL+ features, recommended folds); report text conditioning.
  • Evaluation and sampling (Phase 7). ecgen.evaluation (distribution metrics, HR and label adherence, TSTR classifier, reconstruction, inter-lead correlation, Einthoven residual, memorisation); ecgen.sample / ecgen sample / ecgen evaluate; checkpoints record their family.
  • Docs and packaging (Phase 8). Concepts, Extending ECGEN, conditioning, sampling, diffusion & flow, PTB-XL pages; Visual Guide pages for diffusion and flow matching; extras text, ssm, eval.

docs.title: v1.1.0 - Training Moved Into the ecgen Package (Phase 0)
Overview
docs.text:
Phase 0 of PLAN_TRAINING_LIBRARY.md. Training is now part of the published ecgen package, with one YAML-driven runner for every model family: ecgen train <config.yaml> [dotted.key=value ...] [--resume ckpt] [--print-config] (also python -m ecgen train), plus ecgen list. See Training with ecgen train.

  • One runner, honoured config. model/data.dataset/callbacks entries are built from a registry name or an import-path target, with params passed to the constructor. The callbacks: and checkpoint: sections now take effect; the old visualization: section is gone and unknown sections are rejected. Command-line overrides are applied after the YAML, so they always win (previously YAML values overrode CLI flags).
  • Run directory. Every run writes checkpoints/, samples/, metrics/train_val_metrics.json, tb/, config_resolved.yaml and metadata.json under runs/<name>/seed_<seed>/. Checkpoints also store the datamodule state (lead_names, fs, seq_length, feature_normalizer) under the ECGDataModule key.
  • Compatibility check. The run fails before training if the model's channel count or seq_length disagrees with the dataset.
  • Data. New dict-returning MIMICIVECG (mimic_iv_ecg) with lead selection (leads: independent8, standard12 or a list), scale, measurements and missing options; a SyntheticECG (synthetic) dataset for smoke runs; a generic ECGDataModule with split_params; batches are ecgen.types.ECGBatch. With default parameters MIMICIVECG reproduces the legacy dataset's records, splits and signals exactly, and VAE, VQ-VAE and prior training through the runner reproduced the old scripts' logged metrics bit-for-bit on a 256-record subset.
  • Fix: measurement normalization. The measurement statistics are always fit on the train split (previously each split, after max_samples truncation, used its own statistics).
  • Behaviour change: Pulse2Pulse leads. pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml uses leads: independent8 (I, II, V1–V6), matching the CSV columns written by ecgen.generate. The old script fed the first 8 file leads (I, II, III, aVR, aVF, aVL, V1, V2), and z-scored all 12 leads before dropping 4; the z-score is now computed over the selected leads. run_train_pulse2pulse_mimic.sh works again (it passed --config to a script that did not accept it).

docs.title: Changes Summary - PixelCNN Prior Alignment and Receptive Field
Overview
docs.text:
Two fixes to the VQ-VAE stage-2 prior. Prior checkpoints from before this change use the old architecture and must be retrained; stage-1 VQ-VAE checkpoints are unaffected.

  • Off-by-one: the mask-A layer already excluded the current position, and training also shifted the targets (logits[:, :, :-1] vs indices[:, 1:]), so logit t learned code t+1 while sampling drew code t from logit t. Logits at t now predict code t from codes < t in both training and sampling.
  • Receptive field: the prior used undilated kernel-3 masked convolutions, so each code saw only the previous num_layers codes (3 codes, about 48 ms). It now uses WaveNet-style residual gated causal convolutions with dilations 1, 2, 4, ..., 512, a receptive field of 1024 codes, which covers the 625 codes of a 5000-sample ECG.

docs.title: Changes Summary - Prior Sample Length Fix
Overview
docs.text: PriorLightning.sample() computed the latent length as seq_length // 16, but the VQ-VAE downsamples by 2 ** (len(channel_multipliers) - 1) (8 by default), so samples came out 2496 long instead of 5000. Sampling now derives the latent length from the VQ-VAE and returns the requested length.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
ECGEN trains every generative model through one runner (ecgen train) by splitting a model into independent, swappable parts. Each part talks to the others only through a small contract, so a new method, network, condition, or dataset is one new class — not a new training script.

Part Owns Contract Registry Built-ins Dataset Reading records, splits, condition fields, normalizers Dict samples {signal [C,T], cond, cond_missing, meta} + lead_names, fs, seq_length, field_normalizers DATASETS mimic_iv_ecg, ptbxl, synthetic Masks Which part of an ECG is observed (partial-ECG tasks) obs_mask [C,T], 1 = observed MASKS lead_subset, time_span, forecast, random_points, none, unobserved, mixture Batch Collation ECGBatch(signal, lead_names, fs, cond, cond_missing, obs_mask, meta) — ECGDataModule Condition encoders One field → one slot vector [B,D], tokens [B,N,D] + mask, or dense [B,C',T] CONDITION_ENCODERS categorical, multilabel, numeric, fourier, masked_signal, text_hash, text Conditioner Combining fields, dropout, null embeddings ConditionOutput(vector, tokens, tokens_mask, dense) — CompositeConditioner Family The training objective and sampler GenerativeModule: __init__(config=None, **kw), training_step, sample(n, cond=, obs=, …), supports, accepts FAMILIES vae, vqvae, vqvae_prior, pulse2pulse, diffusion, flow_matching, latent_diffusion, latent_flow_matching Process (continuous families) corruption + integration training_pair(x0, noise), sample(model_fn, shape, steps, …) PROCESSES ddpm, rectified_flow Backbone (continuous families) the network forward(x, t, cond), accepts BACKBONES unet1d, dit1d, ssm, mamba Callbacks Plots, early stopping, … Lightning callbacks CALLBACKS vae_visualization, ecg_visualization, generated_samples, early_stopping, lr_monitor, model_checkpoint Runner Run dirs, loggers, checkpoints, compatibility checks YAML config → pl.Trainer.fit — ecgen train

Every registry also accepts target: package.module.Class, so code outside the library plugs in without registration.

docs.title: What travels with a checkpoint
docs.text:
• the family's config (flat hyperparameters → Family.load_from_checkpoint(path) works);
  • ecgen_family: the registry name, so ecgen.sample(path) needs nothing else;
  • ecgen_data_info: lead names, sampling rate, length, scaling, and one normalizer per numeric condition field, so sample(cond={...}) takes raw units;
  • the ECGDataModule state, and EMA weights for continuous families;
  • for two-stage models (PixelCNN prior, latent diffusion/flow) the frozen stage-1 config and weights, so stage 1 is not needed again.

docs.title: Checks before training
docs.text: The runner refuses a config when the model's channel count or fixed length disagrees with the dataset, a family that cannot be conditioned gets a conditioning block, an encoder produces a slot the family or backbone cannot consume, a condition field is not in the data, or an observation encoder is configured without data.masks.

docs.title: Extending ECGEN
docs.text: Each extension point is a class plus one registration line. Code outside the package can skip registration and be referenced with target: my_pkg.MyClass.

docs.title: A new family
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Optional

from ecgen.families.base import Capabilities, GenerativeModule
from ecgen.registry import FAMILIES
from ecgen.utils.config import resolve_config


@dataclass
class MyConfig:
    in_channels: int = 12
    lr: float = 1e-4
    conditioning: Optional[dict] = None


@FAMILIES.register("my_model")
class MyModel(GenerativeModule):
    supports = Capabilities(conditional=True)
    accepts = frozenset({"vector"})

    def __init__(self, config: Any = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        config = resolve_config(MyConfig, config, kwargs)   # checkpoint-safe
        self.save_hyperparameters(config.__dict__)
        self.config = config
        self.init_conditioning(config.conditioning)
        ...

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        x = self.get_signal(batch)          # [B, C, T]
        c = self.condition(batch)           # ConditionOutput or None
        ...

    def sample(self, n_samples=16, cond=None, **kwargs):
        c = self.encode_condition(n_samples, cond)   # raw values -> ConditionOutput
        ...

Then a config with model: {name: my_model, params: {...}}, a smoke test with the synthetic dataset, and a docs page. Data, conditioning, the runner, callbacks, ecgen sample and the evaluation tools work unchanged.

docs.title: A new diffusion / flow method
docs.text: Subclass ecgen.processes.Process — training_pair(x0, noise) returns TrainingPair(xt, t, target, weight), sample(model_fn, shape, steps, device, generator, inpaint) integrates — and register it with @PROCESSES.register("name"). Use it with model: {name: diffusion, params: {process: {name: name}}}. No family code.

docs.title: A new backbone
docs.text: Implement forward(x, t, cond) (cond is a ConditionOutput or None), set accepts to the slots it consumes, take in_channels, cond_dim, context_dim, dense_channels in __init__, and register it with @BACKBONES.register("name"). Zero-initialise the output layer so training starts from a neutral prediction.

docs.title: A new kind of condition
docs.text: Dataset side: emit cond["field"] (and cond_missing["field"] if values can be missing) in every sample; numeric fields should expose a FeatureNormalizer in field_normalizers so raw values work at sampling time. Model side: subclass ecgen.conditioning.FieldEncoder, set slot (vector, tokens, or dense) and out_dim, implement forward(value, missing), and register it with @CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("name").

docs.title: A new dataset
docs.text: Subclass ecgen.data.datasets.BaseECGDataset: return the dict contract from __getitem__, set lead_names, fs, seq_length, accept split=, fit normalizers on the training split, and register it with @DATASETS.register("name"). See Adding a dataset.

docs.title: A new mask, guidance, or callback
docs.text: Masks subclass ecgen.data.masks.MaskGenerator (@MASKS.register); guidance is a function of model outputs like ecgen.processes.cfg_model_fn; callbacks are Lightning callbacks registered in CALLBACKS (a save_dir argument defaults to the run's samples/ folder).

docs.title: Project Structure

docs.title: ecgen.conditioning.composite
docs.text: Combining several field encoders into one :class:~ecgen.types.ConditionOutput, with per-field condition dropout (for classifier-free guidance).

docs.title: CompositeConditioner
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Encodes condition fields into the vector / tokens / dense slots.

  • vector encoders are projected to vector_dim and summed;
  • token encoders are projected to token_dim and concatenated along N;
  • dense encoders are concatenated along channels.

Config (also stored in model hyperparameters)::

conditioning:
  vector_dim: 256
  token_dim: 256
  encoders:
    - {field: measurements, name: numeric, params: {num_features: 9}}
    - {field: obs, name: masked_signal, params: {num_leads: 12}}
  dropout: {measurements: 0.1}      # per-field drop probability in training

A dropped or absent field is replaced by a learned null embedding (vector: one [vector_dim] row per field; tokens: one null token; dense: everything unobserved). The same null is used for the unconditional pass of classifier-free guidance (drop="all").

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default encoders Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]

Specs {field, name | target, params}.

required vector_dim int

Size of the combined global vector.

256 token_dim int

Size of each token.

256 dropout Optional[Mapping[str, float]]

Per-field drop probability during training.

None Source code in src/ecgen/conditioning/composite.py 
class CompositeConditioner(nn.Module):
    """
    Encodes condition fields into the ``vector`` / ``tokens`` / ``dense`` slots.

    - vector encoders are projected to ``vector_dim`` and summed;
    - token encoders are projected to ``token_dim`` and concatenated along N;
    - dense encoders are concatenated along channels.

    Config (also stored in model hyperparameters)::

        conditioning:
          vector_dim: 256
          token_dim: 256
          encoders:
            - {field: measurements, name: numeric, params: {num_features: 9}}
            - {field: obs, name: masked_signal, params: {num_leads: 12}}
          dropout: {measurements: 0.1}      # per-field drop probability in training

    A dropped or absent field is replaced by a learned *null* embedding
    (vector: one ``[vector_dim]`` row per field; tokens: one null token;
    dense: everything unobserved). The same null is used for the
    unconditional pass of classifier-free guidance (``drop="all"``).

    Args:
        encoders: Specs ``{field, name | target, params}``.
        vector_dim: Size of the combined global vector.
        token_dim: Size of each token.
        dropout: Per-field drop probability during training.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        encoders: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
        vector_dim: int = 256,
        token_dim: int = 256,
        dropout: Optional[Mapping[str, float]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        if not encoders:
            raise ValueError("conditioning.encoders is empty")
        self.vector_dim = vector_dim
        self.token_dim = token_dim
        self.dropout = dict(dropout or {})

        self.fields: List[str] = []
        self.encoders = nn.ModuleDict()
        self.proj = nn.ModuleDict()
        self.null_vector = nn.ParameterDict()
        self.null_token = nn.ParameterDict()
        dense_channels = 0
        for spec in encoders:
            field = spec["field"]
            if field in self.encoders:
                raise ValueError(f"Field {field!r} has two encoders")
            enc = CONDITION_ENCODERS.build(
                {k: v for k, v in spec.items() if k != "field"}
            )
            self.fields.append(field)
            self.encoders[field] = enc
            if enc.slot == "vector":
                self.proj[field] = nn.Linear(enc.out_dim, vector_dim)
                self.null_vector[field] = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(vector_dim))
            elif enc.slot == "tokens":
                self.proj[field] = nn.Linear(enc.out_dim, token_dim)
                self.null_token[field] = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(token_dim) * 0.02)
            elif enc.slot == "dense":
                dense_channels += enc.out_dim
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Encoder for {field!r} has unknown slot {enc.slot!r}")
        unknown = set(self.dropout) - set(self.fields)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"dropout names fields without encoders: {sorted(unknown)}"
            )
        self.dense_channels = dense_channels

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ properties

    @property
    def slots(self) -> set[str]:
        return {self.encoders[f].slot for f in self.fields}

    @property
    def uses_obs(self) -> bool:
        return OBS_FIELD in self.fields

    @property
    def cond_fields(self) -> List[str]:
        """Fields read from ``cond`` (everything except ``obs``)."""
        return [f for f in self.fields if f != OBS_FIELD]

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- forward

    def _drop_masks(
        self, batch_size: int, device: torch.device, drop: Drop
    ) -> Dict[str, Tensor]:
        """Per-field ``[B]`` bool masks, True = replace with null."""
        masks = {
            f: torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
            for f in self.fields
        }
        if self.training:
            for f, p in self.dropout.items():
                if p > 0:
                    masks[f] = torch.rand(batch_size, device=device) < p
        if drop is None:
            return masks
        if isinstance(drop, Mapping):
            for f, m in drop.items():
                masks[f] = masks[f] | m.to(device).bool()
            return masks
        names = (
            self.fields
            if drop == "all"
            else ([drop] if isinstance(drop, str) else list(drop))
        )
        for f in names:
            masks[f] = torch.ones(batch_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
        return masks

    def forward(
        self,
        cond: Optional[Mapping[str, Tensor]] = None,
        cond_missing: Optional[Mapping[str, Tensor]] = None,
        obs: Optional[Tensor] = None,
        obs_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
        batch_size: Optional[int] = None,
        drop: Drop = None,
    ) -> ConditionOutput:
        """
        Args:
            cond: Normalized condition fields; a missing key means "not given".
            cond_missing: Per-field missing masks.
            obs: Partially observed ECG ``[B, C, T]``.
            obs_mask: Mask of ``obs`` (1 = observed).
            batch_size: Needed when no field is given at all.
            drop: ``"all"``, field name(s), or ``{field: [B] bool}`` to force nulls
                (e.g. the unconditional half of classifier-free guidance).
        """
        cond = dict(cond or {})
        cond_missing = dict(cond_missing or {})
        b = batch_size or _infer_batch(cond, obs)
        device = _infer_device(self, cond, obs)
        drops = self._drop_masks(b, device, drop)

        vector: Optional[Tensor] = None
        tokens: List[Tensor] = []
        token_masks: List[Tensor] = []
        dense: List[Tensor] = []
        for field in self.fields:
            enc = self.encoders[field]
            dropped = drops[field]
            if field == OBS_FIELD:
                given = obs is not None and obs_mask is not None
            else:
                given = field in cond
            if not given:
                dropped = torch.ones_like(dropped)

            if enc.slot == "dense":
                dense.append(self._dense(field, enc, obs, obs_mask, dropped, b, device))
                continue

            null_rows = dropped[:, None]
            # Given fields are always encoded, so a fully dropped batch keeps the
            # same token count as a conditional one (CFG can batch both passes).
            out = enc(cond[field], cond_missing.get(field)) if given else None

            if enc.slot == "vector":
                null = self.null_vector[field].expand(b, -1)
                v = (
                    null
                    if out is None
                    else torch.where(null_rows, null, self.proj[field](out))
                )
                vector = v if vector is None else vector + v
            else:
                null_tok = self.null_token[field].view(1, 1, -1).expand(b, 1, -1)
                if out is None:
                    tok, tmask = (
                        null_tok,
                        torch.ones(b, 1, dtype=torch.bool, device=device),
                    )
                else:
                    raw_tok, raw_mask = out
                    tok = self.proj[field](raw_tok)
                    # dropped rows: only the null token (in slot 0) is valid
                    tok = torch.where(
                        null_rows[..., None], null_tok.expand_as(tok), tok
                    )
                    tmask = raw_mask.bool() & ~null_rows
                    tmask[:, 0] |= dropped
                tokens.append(tok)
                token_masks.append(tmask)

        return ConditionOutput(
            vector=vector,
            tokens=torch.cat(tokens, dim=1) if tokens else None,
            tokens_mask=torch.cat(token_masks, dim=1) if token_masks else None,
            dense=torch.cat(dense, dim=1) if dense else None,
        )

    def _dense(self, field, enc, obs, obs_mask, dropped, b, device) -> Tensor:
        if obs is None or obs_mask is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Dense encoder for {field!r} needs obs/obs_mask; configure data.masks "
                "for training or pass obs= and obs_mask= when sampling"
            )
        keep = (~dropped).to(obs.dtype).view(-1, *([1] * (obs.dim() - 1)))
        return enc((obs * keep, obs_mask.to(obs.dtype) * keep))

A missing label (mask True, or value < 0) maps to a learned "unknown" embedding.

Source code in src/ecgen/conditioning/encoders.py 
@CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("categorical")
class CategoricalEncoder(FieldEncoder):
    """
    Single class label ``[B]`` (int) → embedding ``[B, dim]``.

    A missing label (mask ``True``, or value ``< 0``) maps to a learned
    "unknown" embedding.
    """

    def __init__(self, num_classes: int, dim: int = 128) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.out_dim = dim
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(num_classes + 1, dim)  # last row = unknown

    def forward(self, value: Tensor, missing: Optional[Tensor] = None) -> Tensor:
        idx = value.long().reshape(-1)
        unknown = idx < 0
        if missing is not None:
            unknown = unknown | missing.reshape(-1).bool()
        idx = torch.where(unknown, torch.full_like(idx, self.num_classes), idx)
        return self.embed(idx)

@CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("multilabel")
class MultiLabelEncoder(FieldEncoder):
    """
    Multi-hot labels ``[B, L]`` → ``[B, dim]`` (linear projection, SSSD-ECG style),
    or with ``as_tokens=True`` one token per *present* label for cross-attention.
    Missing labels (mask ``[B, L]``) are treated as absent.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, num_labels: int, dim: int = 128, as_tokens: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.num_labels = num_labels
        self.out_dim = dim
        self.as_tokens = as_tokens
        self.slot = "tokens" if as_tokens else "vector"
        if as_tokens:
            self.label_emb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(num_labels, dim) * 0.02)
        else:
            self.proj = _mlp(num_labels, dim, None)

    def forward(self, value: Tensor, missing: Optional[Tensor] = None):
        y = value.float()
        if missing is not None:
            y = y * (~missing.bool()).float()
        if not self.as_tokens:
            return self.proj(y)
        tokens = self.label_emb[None] * y[..., None]  # [B, L, D]
        return tokens, y > 0.5

Bases: FieldEncoder

Normalized numeric features [B, F] with a missing mask → [B, dim].

The MLP sees (value * observed, missing), so missingness is explicit. With as_tokens=True each feature becomes one token value * w_f + b_f (or a learned missing token), for cross-attention.

Source code in src/ecgen/conditioning/encoders.py 
@CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("numeric")
class NumericEncoder(FieldEncoder):
    """
    Normalized numeric features ``[B, F]`` with a missing mask → ``[B, dim]``.

    The MLP sees ``(value * observed, missing)``, so missingness is explicit.
    With ``as_tokens=True`` each feature becomes one token
    ``value * w_f + b_f`` (or a learned missing token), for cross-attention.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_features: int,
        dim: int = 128,
        hidden: Optional[int] = None,
        as_tokens: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.num_features = num_features
        self.out_dim = dim
        self.as_tokens = as_tokens
        self.slot = "tokens" if as_tokens else "vector"
        if as_tokens:
            self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(num_features, dim) * 0.02)
            self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(num_features, dim) * 0.02)
            self.missing_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(num_features, dim) * 0.02)
        else:
            self.mlp = _mlp(2 * num_features, dim, hidden)

    def forward(self, value: Tensor, missing: Optional[Tensor] = None):
        x = value.float()
        m = torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.bool) if missing is None else missing.bool()
        x = torch.where(m, torch.zeros_like(x), x)
        if not self.as_tokens:
            return self.mlp(torch.cat([x, m.float()], dim=-1))
        tokens = x[..., None] * self.weight + self.bias
        tokens = torch.where(m[..., None], self.missing_token.expand_as(tokens), tokens)
        return tokens, torch.ones_like(m)

Numeric features [B, F] → random Fourier features → MLP [B, dim].

Source code in src/ecgen/conditioning/encoders.py 
@CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("fourier")
class FourierScalarEncoder(FieldEncoder):
    """Numeric features ``[B, F]`` → random Fourier features → MLP ``[B, dim]``."""

    def __init__(
        self, num_features: int, dim: int = 128, n_freqs: int = 16, sigma: float = 1.0
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.out_dim = dim
        self.fourier = FourierFeatures(num_features, n_freqs, sigma)
        self.mlp = _mlp(self.fourier.out_dim + num_features, dim, None)

    def forward(self, value: Tensor, missing: Optional[Tensor] = None) -> Tensor:
        x = value.float()
        m = torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.bool) if missing is None else missing.bool()
        x = torch.where(m, torch.zeros_like(x), x)
        feats = self.fourier(x) * (~m).float().repeat_interleave(
            self.fourier.out_dim // x.shape[1], dim=1
        )
        return self.mlp(torch.cat([feats, m.float()], dim=-1))

Reads obs / obs_mask (not a cond field). With channels set, a 1x1 conv projects to that many channels.

@CONDITION_ENCODERS.register("masked_signal")
class MaskedSignalEncoder(FieldEncoder):
    """
    Partially observed ECG → dense ``[B, 2C, T]`` = ``[x * mask, mask]``.

    Reads ``obs`` / ``obs_mask`` (not a ``cond`` field). With ``channels`` set,
    a 1x1 conv projects to that many channels.
    """

    slot = "dense"

    def __init__(self, num_leads: int, channels: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.num_leads = num_leads
        self.proj = nn.Conv1d(2 * num_leads, channels, 1) if channels else None
        self.out_dim = channels or 2 * num_leads

    def forward(self, value: Tensor, missing: Optional[Tensor] = None) -> Tensor:
        obs, mask = value
        mask = mask.to(obs.dtype)
        dense = torch.cat([obs * mask, mask], dim=1)
        return self.proj(dense) if self.proj is not None else dense

class FiLM(nn.Module):
    """``h * (1 + gamma(c)) + beta(c)`` per channel."""

    def __init__(self, cond_dim: int, channels: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.proj = _zero(nn.Linear(cond_dim, 2 * channels))

    def forward(self, h: Tensor, c: Optional[Tensor]) -> Tensor:
        if c is None:
            return h
        gamma, beta = self.proj(c).chunk(2, dim=-1)
        shape = (h.shape[0], -1) + (1,) * (h.dim() - 2)
        return h * (1 + gamma.view(shape)) + beta.view(shape)

class AdaGN(nn.Module):

class AdaLNZero(nn.Module):
    """
    DiT-style adaptive LayerNorm for ``[B, N, D]`` tokens.

    ``forward`` returns ``(modulated_x, gate)``; the block adds
    ``gate * f(modulated_x)`` to its residual. Gates start at 0.
    """

    def __init__(self, cond_dim: int, dim: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(dim, elementwise_affine=False, eps=1e-6)
        self.proj = _zero(nn.Linear(cond_dim, 3 * dim))

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, c: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
        shift, scale, gate = self.proj(F.silu(c)).unsqueeze(1).chunk(3, dim=-1)
        return self.norm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift, gate

Residual: x + out(attn(norm(x), tokens)), with out zero-initialised.

Source code in src/ecgen/nn/injection.py 
class CrossAttention1d(nn.Module):
    """
    Feature map ``[B, C, T]`` attends to condition tokens ``[B, N, D]``.

    Residual: ``x + out(attn(norm(x), tokens))``, with ``out`` zero-initialised.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, channels: int, context_dim: int, heads: int = 4, groups: int = 8
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        if channels % heads:
            raise ValueError(f"channels={channels} must be divisible by heads={heads}")
        self.heads = heads
        self.norm = nn.GroupNorm(groups, channels)
        self.q = nn.Linear(channels, channels)
        self.kv = nn.Linear(context_dim, 2 * channels)
        self.out = _zero(nn.Linear(channels, channels))

    def forward(
        self, x: Tensor, tokens: Optional[Tensor], mask: Optional[Tensor] = None
    ) -> Tensor:
        if tokens is None:
            return x
        b, c, t = x.shape
        h = self.norm(x).transpose(1, 2)  # [B, T, C]
        q = self.q(h).view(b, t, self.heads, -1).transpose(1, 2)
        k, v = self.kv(tokens).chunk(2, dim=-1)
        k = k.view(b, -1, self.heads, c // self.heads).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.view(b, -1, self.heads, c // self.heads).transpose(1, 2)
        attn_mask = None
        if mask is not None:
            attn_mask = mask[:, None, None, :].to(torch.bool)  # True = attend
            # rows with no valid token would give NaN; let them attend to everything
            attn_mask = attn_mask | ~attn_mask.any(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=attn_mask)
        out = out.transpose(1, 2).reshape(b, t, c)
        return x + self.out(out).transpose(1, 2)

def concat_dense(x: Tensor, dense: Optional[Tensor]) -> Tensor:
    """``ConcatInput``: stack time-aligned conditions onto the input channels."""
    if dense is None:
        return x
    if dense.shape[-1] != x.shape[-1]:
        dense = F.interpolate(
            dense, size=x.shape[-1], mode="linear", align_corners=False
        )
    return torch.cat([x, dense], dim=1)

class TimestepEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """Sinusoidal embedding followed by a 2-layer MLP (DDPM / ADM style)."""

    def __init__(self, dim: int, hidden: int | None = None, scale: float = 1.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        hidden = hidden or 4 * dim
        self.dim = dim
        self.scale = scale
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(dim, hidden), nn.SiLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, hidden)
        )
        self.out_dim = hidden

    def forward(self, t: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        return self.mlp(sinusoidal_embedding(t * self.scale, self.dim))

class FourierFeatures(nn.Module):
    """
    Random Fourier features of scalars: ``[B, F] -> [B, F * 2 * n_freqs]``.

    Frequencies are fixed (a buffer), drawn once with a fixed seed so models
    built twice from the same config are identical.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, num_features: int, n_freqs: int = 16, sigma: float = 1.0
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
        self.register_buffer(
            "freqs", torch.randn(num_features, n_freqs, generator=gen) * sigma
        )
        self.out_dim = num_features * 2 * n_freqs

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        args = 2 * math.pi * x[..., None] * self.freqs  # [B, F, n]
        return torch.cat([torch.cos(args), torch.sin(args)], dim=-1).flatten(1)

def sinusoidal_embedding(t: Tensor, dim: int, max_period: float = 10000.0) -> Tensor:
    """
    Transformer-style sinusoidal embedding of (possibly fractional) positions.

    Args:
        t: ``[B]`` time steps or noise levels.
        dim: Embedding size.

    Returns:
        ``[B, dim]``
    """
    half = dim // 2
    freqs = torch.exp(
        -math.log(max_period)
        * torch.arange(half, device=t.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        / half
    )
    args = t.float()[:, None] * freqs[None]
    emb = torch.cat([torch.cos(args), torch.sin(args)], dim=-1)
    if dim % 2:
        emb = torch.cat([emb, torch.zeros_like(emb[:, :1])], dim=-1)
    return emb

docs.title: ecgen.data.masks
docs.text:
Observation masks for partial-ECG conditioning (lead reconstruction, imputation, forecasting).

A mask generator is called once per sample with the signal shape and returns an obs_mask [C, T] float tensor, 1 = observed. The data module attaches it to the batch (ECGBatch.obs_mask); models condition on signal * obs_mask and (optionally) compute the loss on the unobserved part.

Config (data.masks)::

masks: {name: lead_subset, params: {keep: [[I], [I, II], [II, V1]]}}
masks:
  name: mixture
  params:

@MASKS.register("lead_subset")
class LeadSubset(MaskGenerator):
    """
    Observe whole leads.

    Args:
        keep: List of lead-name lists; one is chosen uniformly per sample
            (e.g. ``[[I], [I, II]]`` = "single lead I" or "leads I and II").
            If omitted, a random subset of ``min_leads..max_leads`` leads is kept.
        min_leads: Smallest random subset.
        max_leads: Largest random subset.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        lead_names: Sequence[str],
        keep: Optional[Sequence[Sequence[str]]] = None,
        min_leads: int = 1,
        max_leads: int = 3,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(lead_names)
        self.keep: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None
        if keep is not None:
            self.keep = []
            for names in keep:
                unknown = [n for n in names if n not in self.lead_names]
                if unknown:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"lead_subset keeps unknown leads {unknown}; data has {self.lead_names}"
                    )
                self.keep.append([self.lead_names.index(n) for n in names])
        self.min_leads, self.max_leads = min_leads, max_leads

    def __call__(self, num_leads, length, generator=None):
        mask = torch.zeros(num_leads, length)
        if self.keep is not None:
            idx = self.keep[_randint(0, len(self.keep) - 1, generator)]
        else:
            k = _randint(self.min_leads, min(self.max_leads, num_leads), generator)
            idx = torch.randperm(num_leads, generator=generator)[:k].tolist()
        mask[idx] = 1.0
        return mask

@MASKS.register("time_span")
class TimeSpan(MaskGenerator):
    """
    Hide ``n_spans`` contiguous segments (all leads) covering ``min_frac..max_frac``
    of the record in total — imputation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        lead_names: Sequence[str],
        min_frac: float = 0.1,
        max_frac: float = 0.5,
        n_spans: int = 1,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(lead_names)
        self.min_frac, self.max_frac, self.n_spans = min_frac, max_frac, n_spans

    def __call__(self, num_leads, length, generator=None):
        mask = torch.ones(num_leads, length)
        frac = self.min_frac + (self.max_frac - self.min_frac) * _rand(generator)
        span = max(1, int(round(frac * length / self.n_spans)))
        for _ in range(self.n_spans):
            start = _randint(0, length - span, generator)
            mask[:, start : start + span] = 0.0
        return mask

@MASKS.register("mixture")
class Mixture(MaskGenerator):
    """Pick one component per sample with probability proportional to ``weight``."""

    def __init__(
        self, lead_names: Sequence[str], components: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(lead_names)
        if not components:
            raise ValueError("mixture needs at least one component")
        self.components = [build_mask(c, lead_names) for c in components]
        w = torch.tensor([float(c.get("weight", 1.0)) for c in components])
        self.probs = w / w.sum()

    def __call__(self, num_leads, length, generator=None):
        i = int(torch.multinomial(self.probs, 1, generator=generator))
        return self.components[i](num_leads, length, generator)

def build_mask(
    spec: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]], lead_names: Sequence[str]
) -> Optional[MaskGenerator]:
    """Build a mask generator from ``{name | target, params}`` (``weight`` is ignored)."""
    if not spec:

def get_signal(batch: Any) -> Tensor:
    """
    Return the ``[B, C, T]`` ECG tensor from any supported batch format.

    Accepts an :class:`ECGBatch`, a dict with ``"signal"`` or the legacy
    ``"ecg_signals"`` key, or a legacy ``(ecg, features)`` tuple.
    """
    if isinstance(batch, ECGBatch):
        return batch.signal
    if isinstance(batch, dict):
        if "signal" in batch:
            return batch["signal"]
        if "ecg_signals" in batch:
            return batch["ecg_signals"]
        raise KeyError(
            f"Batch dict has no 'signal' or 'ecg_signals' key: {sorted(batch)}"
        )
    if isinstance(batch, (tuple, list)):
        return batch[0]
    if isinstance(batch, Tensor):
        return batch
    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported batch type: {type(batch).__name__}")

class BaseECGDataset(Dataset, ABC):
    """
    Base class for ECG datasets.

    ``__getitem__`` returns a dict::

        {
            "signal": FloatTensor [C, T],
            "cond": {field_name: Tensor},          # may be empty
            "cond_missing": {field_name: BoolTensor},
            "meta": {...},                         # ids; not fed to models
        }

    and the dataset exposes :attr:`lead_names` and :attr:`fs`, which
    :class:`ecgen.data.collate.ECGCollate` attaches to every batch.
    """

    lead_names: List[str]
    fs: int
    seq_length: int
    feature_normalizer: Optional[FeatureNormalizer] = None

    @abstractmethod
    def __len__(self) -> int: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, Any]: ...

    @property
    def num_leads(self) -> int:
        return len(self.lead_names)

    @property
    def field_normalizers(self) -> Dict[str, FeatureNormalizer]:
        """Normalizers of numeric ``cond`` fields, by field name.

        Saved in checkpoints so a model can normalize raw values at sampling
        time. Default: :attr:`feature_normalizer` for the ``measurements`` field.
        """
        if self.feature_normalizer is None or not self.feature_normalizer.columns:
            return {}
        return {"measurements": self.feature_normalizer}

def scale_signal(ecg: np.ndarray, scale: Scale, eps: float = 1e-6) -> np.ndarray:
    """Apply the dataset-level amplitude scaling to a ``[C, T]`` record."""
    if scale == "none":
        return ecg.astype(np.float32)
    mean = ecg.mean()
    if scale == "zscore":
        divisor = max(float(np.std(ecg)), eps)
    elif isinstance(scale, (int, float)) and not isinstance(scale, bool):
        divisor = float(scale)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown scale {scale!r}; use 'zscore', 'none', or a number")
    return ((ecg.astype(np.float32) - mean) / divisor).astype(np.float32)

@DATASETS.register("mimic_iv_ecg")
class MIMICIVECG(BaseECGDataset):
    """
    MIMIC-IV-ECG records with machine measurements as a numeric condition field.

    Samples are dicts (see :class:`~ecgen.data.datasets.base.BaseECGDataset`) with
    ``cond["measurements"]`` = the normalized ``measurements`` columns.

    The train/val/test split is by subject and seeded, and matches the legacy
    ``MIMICIVECGDataset`` when ``missing="drop"`` (the default). The measurement
    normalizer is always fit on the *train* split, whichever split is loaded.

    Args:
        root: MIMIC-IV-ECG directory (contains ``files/`` and ``machine_measurements.csv``).
        split: ``"train"``, ``"val"``, or ``"test"``.
        val_split: Fraction of subjects in the validation split.
        test_split: Fraction of subjects in the test split.
        seed: Split seed.
        max_samples: Keep only the first N rows of the split (for quick runs).
        skip_missing_check: Skip the check that each record's ``.hea`` exists.
        leads: ``None`` (file order, padded/truncated to ``num_leads``), an alias
            (``"standard12"``, ``"independent8"``), or a list of lead names.
        num_leads: Channel count when ``leads`` is ``None``.
        seq_length: Samples per record (padded/truncated).
        scale: ``"zscore"`` (per record, legacy), ``"none"`` (mV), or a number
            (subtract record mean, divide by it).
        measurements: Columns for ``cond["measurements"]``; ``[]`` for none.
        missing: ``"drop"`` rows with any missing measurement (legacy) or
            ``"mask"`` to keep them and report the gaps in ``cond_missing``.
            ``"mask"`` keeps more subjects, so its split differs from ``"drop"``.
        feature_normalizer: Use these statistics instead of fitting on train
            (e.g. those stored in a checkpoint).
        report: Add ``cond["report"]``: the machine report lines joined by ". ".
    """

    fs = 500

    def __init__(
        self,
        root: str,
        split: str = "train",
        val_split: float = 0.1,
        test_split: float = 0.1,
        seed: int = 42,
        max_samples: Optional[int] = None,
        skip_missing_check: bool = False,
        leads: LeadSpec = None,
        num_leads: int = 12,
        seq_length: int = 5000,
        scale: Scale = "zscore",
        ecg_norm_eps: float = 1e-6,
        measurements: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        missing: str = "drop",
        feature_normalizer: Optional[FeatureNormalizer | Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        report: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        if split not in ("train", "val", "test"):
            raise ValueError(f"split must be train/val/test, got {split!r}")
        if missing not in ("drop", "mask"):
            raise ValueError(f"missing must be 'drop' or 'mask', got {missing!r}")

        self.root = root
        self.split = split
        self.seed = seed
        self.seq_length = seq_length
        self.scale = scale
        self.ecg_norm_eps = ecg_norm_eps
        self.use_report = report
        self.measurement_columns: List[str] = list(
            MEASUREMENT_COLUMNS if measurements is None else measurements
        )

        self._leads_spec = leads
        if leads is None:
            self.lead_names = list(MIMIC_LEAD_ORDER[:num_leads]) + [
                f"pad{i}" for i in range(max(0, num_leads - len(MIMIC_LEAD_ORDER)))
            ]
        else:
            self.lead_names = resolve_leads(leads, MIMIC_LEAD_ORDER)

        table = self._load_measurements(missing)
        table["split"] = self._assign_splits(table, val_split, test_split)

        if feature_normalizer is None:
            self.feature_normalizer = FeatureNormalizer.fit(
                table[table["split"] == "train"], self.measurement_columns
            )
        elif isinstance(feature_normalizer, dict):
            self.feature_normalizer = FeatureNormalizer.from_dict(feature_normalizer)
        else:
            self.feature_normalizer = feature_normalizer

        self.records = table[table["split"] == split].reset_index(drop=True)

        if skip_missing_check:
            warnings.warn(
                "Skipping missing file check. Some samples may fail during loading.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        else:
            self._filter_missing_files()

        if max_samples is not None:
            self.records = self.records.head(max_samples).reset_index(drop=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ setup

    def _load_measurements(self, missing: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        path = os.path.join(self.root, "machine_measurements.csv")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"machine_measurements.csv not found at {path}. "
                "Download from https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/"
            )
        table = pd.read_csv(path, low_memory=False)

        # The legacy loader always required (and dropped NaNs in) the 9 standard
        # columns, which also decides which subjects enter the split.
        required = (
            ["subject_id", "study_id"]
            + list(MEASUREMENT_COLUMNS)
            + self.measurement_columns
        )
        missing_cols = sorted({c for c in required if c not in table.columns})
        if missing_cols:
            raise ValueError(
                f"machine_measurements.csv missing columns: {missing_cols}"
            )

        if missing == "drop":
            subset = list(
                dict.fromkeys(list(MEASUREMENT_COLUMNS) + self.measurement_columns)
            )
            table = table.dropna(subset=subset)
        return table.reset_index(drop=True)

    def _assign_splits(
        self, table: pd.DataFrame, val_split: float, test_split: float
    ) -> pd.Series:
        subjects = table["subject_id"].unique()
        train_subjects, test_subjects = train_test_split(
            subjects, test_size=test_split, random_state=self.seed
        )
        train_subjects, val_subjects = train_test_split(
            train_subjects,
            test_size=val_split / (1 - test_split),
            random_state=self.seed,
        )
        split = pd.Series("train", index=table.index)
        split[table["subject_id"].isin(set(val_subjects))] = "val"
        split[table["subject_id"].isin(set(test_subjects))] = "test"
        return split

    def record_path(self, subject_id: int, study_id: int) -> str:
        sub = str(subject_id)
        return os.path.join(
            self.root, "files", f"p{sub[:4]}", f"p{sub}", f"s{study_id}", str(study_id)
        )

    def _filter_missing_files(self) -> None:
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(self.root, "files")):
            return
        exists = [
            os.path.isfile(self.record_path(s, t) + ".hea")
            for s, t in zip(self.records["subject_id"], self.records["study_id"])
        ]
        self.records = self.records[np.asarray(exists, dtype=bool)].reset_index(
            drop=True
        )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- samples

    def load_ecg(self, idx: int) -> np.ndarray:
        """Raw ``[C, T]`` signal in mV, with the configured leads and length."""
        row = self.records.iloc[idx]
        record = wfdb.rdrecord(self.record_path(row["subject_id"], row["study_id"]))
        signal = record.p_signal.T.astype(np.float32)  # (leads, time)

        if self._leads_spec is None:
            n = len(self.lead_names)
            if signal.shape[0] < n:
                signal = np.vstack(
                    [
                        signal,
                        np.zeros(
                            (n - signal.shape[0], signal.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32
                        ),
                    ]
                )
            signal = signal[:n]
        else:
            signal = signal[lead_indices(self.lead_names, record.sig_name)]

        if signal.shape[1] < self.seq_length:
            pad = np.zeros(
                (signal.shape[0], self.seq_length - signal.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32
            )
            signal = np.hstack([signal, pad])
        return signal[:, : self.seq_length]

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.records)

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        ecg = scale_signal(self.load_ecg(idx), self.scale, self.ecg_norm_eps)
        row = self.records.iloc[idx]
        sample: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "signal": torch.from_numpy(ecg),
            "cond": {},
            "cond_missing": {},
            "meta": {
                "subject_id": int(row["subject_id"]),
                "study_id": int(row["study_id"]),
            },
        }
        if self.use_report:
            lines = [row.get(f"report_{i}") for i in range(18)]
            sample["cond"]["report"] = ". ".join(
                str(x).strip() for x in lines if isinstance(x, str) and x.strip()
            )
        if self.measurement_columns:
            raw = pd.to_numeric(
                row[self.measurement_columns], errors="coerce"
            ).to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            values, missing = self.feature_normalizer.transform(raw)
            sample["cond"]["measurements"] = torch.from_numpy(values)
            sample["cond_missing"]["measurements"] = torch.from_numpy(missing)
        return sample

def load_ecg(self, idx: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Raw ``[C, T]`` signal in mV, with the configured leads and length."""
    row = self.records.iloc[idx]
    record = wfdb.rdrecord(self.record_path(row["subject_id"], row["study_id"]))
    signal = record.p_signal.T.astype(np.float32)  # (leads, time)

    if self._leads_spec is None:
        n = len(self.lead_names)
        if signal.shape[0] < n:
            signal = np.vstack(
                [
                    signal,
                    np.zeros(
                        (n - signal.shape[0], signal.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32
                    ),
                ]
            )
        signal = signal[:n]
    else:
        signal = signal[lead_indices(self.lead_names, record.sig_name)]

    if signal.shape[1] < self.seq_length:
        pad = np.zeros(
            (signal.shape[0], self.seq_length - signal.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32
        )
        signal = np.hstack([signal, pad])
    return signal[:, : self.seq_length]

@DATASETS.register("synthetic")
class SyntheticECG(BaseECGDataset):
    """
    Deterministic periodic "beats" with per-record heart rate and amplitude.

    Every record carries the ground truth that produced it, so conditional
    models can be tested against known targets:

    - ``cond["measurements"]``: ``[heart_rate (bpm), amplitude (mV)]``, normalized
      with :attr:`feature_normalizer` (fixed statistics of the sampling ranges);
    - ``cond["rhythm"]``: class 0 = brady (< 60 bpm), 1 = normal, 2 = tachy (> 100 bpm);
    - ``cond["labels"]``: multi-hot ``[brady, tachy, high_amplitude (> 1.25 mV)]``;
    - ``cond["report"]``: a templated text, e.g. ``"sinus tachycardia, high voltage"``.

    Args:
        split: ``"train"``, ``"val"``, or ``"test"`` (different records per split).
        num_samples: Records in this split.
        leads: Lead spec (see :func:`ecgen.data.leads.resolve_leads`); default all 12.
        seq_length: Samples per record.
        fs: Sampling rate in Hz.
        scale: As in :func:`ecgen.data.datasets.base.scale_signal`; default ``"none"``
            keeps the amplitude, which ``"zscore"`` would normalize away.
        seed: Base seed; record ``i`` of a split is always the same signal.
    """

    HR_RANGE = (45.0, 150.0)
    AMP_RANGE = (0.5, 2.0)
    MEASUREMENTS = ("heart_rate", "amplitude")
    RHYTHMS = ("brady", "normal", "tachy")
    LABELS = ("brady", "tachy", "high_amplitude")

    def __init__(
        self,
        split: str = "train",
        num_samples: int = 64,
        leads: LeadSpec = None,
        seq_length: int = 5000,
        fs: int = 500,
        scale: Scale = "none",
        seed: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        if split not in _SPLIT_OFFSET:
            raise ValueError(f"split must be train/val/test, got {split!r}")
        self.split = split
        self.num_samples = num_samples
        self.lead_names = resolve_leads(leads, STANDARD_12)
        self.seq_length = seq_length
        self.fs = fs
        self.scale = scale
        self.seed = seed
        ranges = (self.HR_RANGE, self.AMP_RANGE)
        self.feature_normalizer = FeatureNormalizer(
            columns=list(self.MEASUREMENTS),
            mean={c: float(np.mean(r)) for c, r in zip(self.MEASUREMENTS, ranges)},
            std={
                c: float(np.ptp(r) / np.sqrt(12))
                for c, r in zip(self.MEASUREMENTS, ranges)
            },
        )

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return self.num_samples

    @classmethod
    def render(
        cls, hr: float, amp: float, num_leads: int, seq_length: int, fs: int, rng
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        The ``[C, T]`` signal for a heart rate (bpm) and R amplitude (mV).

        Each beat has P, Q, R, S and T waves with fixed widths in seconds (the
        QT interval shortens with the RR interval, Bazett-style); every lead is
        the same beat train times a random gain and sign, plus white noise.
        """
        rr = 60.0 / hr
        t = np.arange(seq_length) / fs - rng.uniform(0, rr)

        def wave(center: float, width: float) -> np.ndarray:
            dt = (t - center + rr / 2) % rr - rr / 2  # time to the nearest wave
            return np.exp(-(dt**2) / (2 * width**2))

        beat = (
            0.12 * wave(-0.16, 0.025)  # P
            - 0.15 * wave(-0.03, 0.008)  # Q
            + wave(0.0, 0.012)  # R
            - 0.25 * wave(0.03, 0.010)  # S
            + 0.30 * wave(0.30 * np.sqrt(rr), 0.045)  # T
        )
        gains = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.0, size=(num_leads, 1)) * rng.choice(
            [-1.0, 1.0], size=(num_leads, 1)
        )
        noise = 0.02 * rng.standard_normal((num_leads, seq_length))
        return (amp * gains * beat[None, :] + noise).astype(np.float32)

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(self.seed + _SPLIT_OFFSET[self.split] + idx)
        hr = rng.uniform(*self.HR_RANGE)
        amp = rng.uniform(*self.AMP_RANGE)
        ecg = self.render(hr, amp, len(self.lead_names), self.seq_length, self.fs, rng)

        features, missing = self.feature_normalizer.transform([hr, amp])
        rhythm = 0 if hr < 60 else (2 if hr > 100 else 1)
        labels = np.array([hr < 60, hr > 100, amp > 1.25], dtype=np.float32)
        rhythm_text = ("sinus bradycardia", "sinus rhythm", "sinus tachycardia")[rhythm]
        report = rhythm_text + (", high voltage" if amp > 1.25 else "")
        return {
            "signal": torch.from_numpy(scale_signal(ecg, self.scale)),
            "cond": {
                "measurements": torch.from_numpy(features),
                "rhythm": torch.tensor(rhythm, dtype=torch.long),
                "labels": torch.from_numpy(labels),
                "report": report,
            },
            "cond_missing": {"measurements": torch.from_numpy(missing)},
            "meta": {"index": idx, "heart_rate": float(hr), "amplitude": float(amp)},
        }

def resolve_leads(spec: LeadSpec, available: Sequence[str]) -> List[str]:
    """
    Turn a lead spec into a list of lead names.

    Args:
        spec: ``None`` keeps ``available`` in its stored order; a string is an
            alias from :data:`LEAD_ALIASES`; a sequence lists lead names.
        available: Leads the dataset stores, in file order.

    Returns:
        Lead names in output channel order.
    """
    if spec is None:
        return list(available)
    if isinstance(spec, str):
        if spec not in LEAD_ALIASES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown lead alias {spec!r}; known: {sorted(LEAD_ALIASES)}"
            )
        names = list(LEAD_ALIASES[spec])
    else:
        names = list(spec)
    missing = [n for n in names if n not in available]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Leads {missing} are not available; dataset has {list(available)}"
        )
    return names

def derive_standard12(x: Any, lead_names: Sequence[str]) -> Any:
    """
    Complete 8 independent leads (I, II, V1–V6, any order) to the standard 12
    using Einthoven / Goldberger: III = II − I, aVR = −(I + II)/2,
    aVL = I − II/2, aVF = II − I/2.

    Args:
        x: ``[..., C, T]`` tensor or array with leads ``lead_names``.

    Returns:
        ``[..., 12, T]`` in :data:`STANDARD_12` order (same type as ``x``).
    """
    import numpy as np

    idx = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(lead_names)}
    missing = [n for n in INDEPENDENT_8 if n not in idx]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"derive_standard12 needs leads {list(INDEPENDENT_8)}; missing {missing}"
        )
    i, ii = x[..., idx["I"], :], x[..., idx["II"], :]
    derived = {
        "III": ii - i,
        "aVR": -(i + ii) / 2,
        "aVL": i - ii / 2,
        "aVF": ii - i / 2,
    }
    leads = [derived[n] if n in derived else x[..., idx[n], :] for n in STANDARD_12]
    try:
        import torch

        if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
            return torch.stack(leads, dim=-2)
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
        pass
    return np.stack(leads, axis=-2)

@dataclass
class FeatureNormalizer:
    """
    Per-column standardization, ``(x - mean) / std``, with missing values.

    Fit it on the training split only and reuse it for validation, test, and
    sampling; :meth:`to_dict` / :meth:`from_dict` make it storable in a checkpoint.
    Missing values (NaN) are ignored when fitting and come out of
    :meth:`transform` as 0 with ``missing=True``.
    """

    columns: List[str]
    mean: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    std: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    eps: float = 1e-6

    @classmethod
    def fit(
        cls, df: pd.DataFrame, columns: Sequence[str], eps: float = 1e-6
    ) -> "FeatureNormalizer":
        norm = cls(columns=list(columns), eps=eps)
        for name in norm.columns:
            vals = pd.to_numeric(df[name], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            vals = vals[~np.isnan(vals)]
            if vals.size == 0:
                norm.mean[name], norm.std[name] = 0.0, 1.0
            else:
                norm.mean[name] = float(np.mean(vals))
                norm.std[name] = float(np.std(vals)) + eps
        return norm

    def transform(self, values: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Normalize one row of raw values (ordered as :attr:`columns`).

        Returns:
            ``(normalized float32 [F], missing bool [F])``
        """
        raw = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
        missing = np.isnan(raw)
        mean = np.array([self.mean[c] for c in self.columns])
        std = np.array([self.std[c] for c in self.columns])
        out = np.where(missing, 0.0, (raw - mean) / std)
        return out.astype(np.float32), missing

    def inverse_transform(self, values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        mean = np.array([self.mean[c] for c in self.columns])
        std = np.array([self.std[c] for c in self.columns])
        return np.asarray(values) * std + mean

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "columns": list(self.columns),
            "mean": dict(self.mean),
            "std": dict(self.std),
            "eps": self.eps,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict[str, Any]) -> "FeatureNormalizer":
        return cls(
            columns=list(d["columns"]),
            mean=dict(d["mean"]),
            std=dict(d["std"]),
            eps=d.get("eps", 1e-6),
        )

def transform(self, values: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Normalize one row of raw values (ordered as :attr:`columns`).

    Returns:
        ``(normalized float32 [F], missing bool [F])``
    """
    raw = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    missing = np.isnan(raw)
    mean = np.array([self.mean[c] for c in self.columns])
    std = np.array([self.std[c] for c in self.columns])
    out = np.where(missing, 0.0, (raw - mean) / std)
    return out.astype(np.float32), missing

class ECGCollate:
    """
    ``collate_fn`` that stacks dict samples into an :class:`ECGBatch`.

    Tensors under ``signal``, ``cond``, ``cond_missing`` and ``obs_mask`` are
    stacked; ``meta`` values are gathered into lists. With a ``mask_generator``,
    each sample without its own ``obs_mask`` gets one drawn from it.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        lead_names: Sequence[str],
        fs: int,
        mask_generator: Optional[MaskGenerator] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.lead_names = list(lead_names)
        self.fs = int(fs)
        self.mask_generator = mask_generator

    def __call__(self, samples: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> ECGBatch:
        if self.mask_generator is not None:
            for s in samples:
                if s.get("obs_mask") is None:
                    c, t = s["signal"].shape
                    s["obs_mask"] = self.mask_generator(c, t)
        first = samples[0]
        cond = {
            k: _stack([s["cond"][k] for s in samples]) for k in first.get("cond", {})
        }
        cond_missing = {
            k: torch.stack([s["cond_missing"][k] for s in samples])
            for k in first.get("cond_missing", {})
        }
        obs_mask = (
            torch.stack([s["obs_mask"] for s in samples])
            if first.get("obs_mask") is not None
            else None
        )
        meta = {k: [s["meta"][k] for s in samples] for k in first.get("meta", {})}
        return ECGBatch(
            signal=torch.stack([s["signal"] for s in samples]),
            lead_names=list(self.lead_names),
            fs=self.fs,
            cond=cond,
            cond_missing=cond_missing,
            obs_mask=obs_mask,
            meta=meta,
        )

class ECGDataModule(pl.LightningDataModule):
    """
    Builds train/val/test splits of one dataset and yields :class:`~ecgen.types.ECGBatch`.

    Args:
        dataset: Dataset spec, ``{"name" | "target": ..., "params": {...}}``; the
            ``split`` argument is filled in per split.
        batch_size: Batch size for all splits.
        num_workers: DataLoader workers.
        pin_memory: Defaults to ``torch.cuda.is_available()``.
        split_params: Per-split overrides of ``dataset.params``, e.g.
            ``{"val": {"max_samples": 1000}}``.
        masks: Observation-mask spec (see :mod:`ecgen.data.masks`); adds
            ``obs_mask`` to every batch for partial-ECG conditioning.

    The train split's ``feature_normalizer`` (if any) is passed to the val/test
    datasets that accept one, and saved in checkpoints via :meth:`state_dict`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        dataset: Mapping[str, Any],
        batch_size: int = 32,
        num_workers: int = 4,
        pin_memory: Optional[bool] = None,
        split_params: Optional[Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]] = None,
        masks: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.dataset_spec = dict(dataset)
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.num_workers = num_workers
        self.pin_memory = (
            torch.cuda.is_available() if pin_memory is None else pin_memory
        )
        self.split_params = {k: dict(v) for k, v in (split_params or {}).items()}
        self.mask_spec = dict(masks) if masks else None

        self.datasets: Dict[str, BaseECGDataset] = {}

    def build_dataset(self, split: str) -> BaseECGDataset:
        cls = DATASETS.resolve(self.dataset_spec)
        params = {
            **dict(self.dataset_spec.get("params") or {}),
            **self.split_params.get(split, {}),
            "split": split,
        }
        train = self.datasets.get("train")
        if (
            split != "train"
            and "feature_normalizer" not in params
            and train is not None
            and getattr(train, "feature_normalizer", None) is not None
            and "feature_normalizer" in inspect.signature(cls).parameters
        ):
            params["feature_normalizer"] = train.feature_normalizer
        return cls(**params)

    def setup(self, stage: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        splits = {
            "fit": ("train", "val"),
            "validate": ("val",),
            "test": ("test",),
            "predict": ("test",),
        }
        wanted = (
            splits.get(stage, ("train", "val", "test"))
            if stage
            else ("train", "val", "test")
        )
        for split in wanted:
            if split not in self.datasets:
                self.datasets[split] = self.build_dataset(split)

    def _loader(self, split: str, shuffle: bool) -> DataLoader:
        if split not in self.datasets:
            self.datasets[split] = self.build_dataset(split)
        ds = self.datasets[split]
        return DataLoader(
            ds,
            batch_size=self.batch_size,
            shuffle=shuffle,
            num_workers=self.num_workers,
            pin_memory=self.pin_memory,
            collate_fn=ECGCollate(
                ds.lead_names, ds.fs, build_mask(self.mask_spec, ds.lead_names)
            ),
        )

    def train_dataloader(self) -> DataLoader:
        return self._loader("train", shuffle=True)

    def val_dataloader(self) -> DataLoader:
        return self._loader("val", shuffle=False)

    def test_dataloader(self) -> DataLoader:
        return self._loader("test", shuffle=False)

    @property
    def reference_dataset(self) -> BaseECGDataset:
        """Any built split (train preferred), for lead names, fs, etc."""
        for split in ("train", "val", "test"):
            if split in self.datasets:
                return self.datasets[split]
        raise RuntimeError("No dataset built yet; call setup() first.")

    def state_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not self.datasets:
            return {}
        ds = self.reference_dataset
        train = self.datasets.get("train", ds)
        norm = getattr(train, "feature_normalizer", None)
        return {
            "lead_names": list(ds.lead_names),
            "fs": ds.fs,
            "seq_length": ds.seq_length,
            "scale": getattr(ds, "scale", None),
            "feature_normalizer": norm.to_dict() if norm is not None else None,
            "normalizers": {f: n.to_dict() for f, n in train.field_normalizers.items()},
        }

docs.title: ecgen.evaluation
docs.text:
Measurements on (generated) ECGs, e.g. to check that a model follows the heart rate it was asked for.

Feature extractors for distribution metrics (Fréchet distance, MMD, precision/recall, nearest neighbours).

There is no single pretrained ECG encoder that every user has, so the default is a set of interpretable hand-crafted features; any torch.nn.Module that maps [B, C, T] to [B, D] (e.g. the penultimate layer of an ECG classifier, see :mod:ecgen.evaluation.classifier) can be used instead.

Metrics for generated ECGs (plan §8): distribution fidelity and diversity, condition adherence, partial-ECG reconstruction, lead consistency, and memorisation.

Arrays are [N, C, T] (NumPy or torch). Distribution metrics work on feature vectors from an extractor (:mod:ecgen.evaluation.features).

A small 1D-ResNet ECG classifier for condition adherence ("does a classifier trained on real ECGs recognise the requested labels in generated ones?") and for TSTR / TRTR (train on synthetic / real, test on real).

Train it on data separate from the generator's training split, otherwise adherence scores are optimistic.

def detect_r_peaks(
    signal: ArrayLike,
    fs: int,
    lead: Optional[int] = None,
    method: str = "simple",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    R-peak sample indices of one ECG ``[C, T]`` (or ``[T]``).

    Args:
        signal: One ECG.
        fs: Sampling rate in Hz.
        lead: Lead to use; default = the lead with the largest QRS energy.
        method: ``"simple"`` (band-pass + peak picking, no extra dependency) or
            ``"neurokit"`` (``neurokit2.ecg_peaks``; needs ``ecgen[eval]``).
    """
    x = _as_numpy(signal)
    if x.ndim == 1:
        x = x[None]
    if x.shape[-1] < int(0.5 * fs):
        return np.array([], dtype=int)

    nyq = fs / 2
    b, a = butter(2, [5 / nyq, min(30 / nyq, 0.99)], btype="band")
    filtered = filtfilt(b, a, x, axis=-1)
    if lead is None:
        lead = int(np.argmax(np.percentile(np.abs(filtered), 99, axis=-1)))
    sig = filtered[lead]

    if method == "neurokit":
        import neurokit2 as nk

        _, info = nk.ecg_peaks(x[lead], sampling_rate=fs)
        return np.asarray(info["ECG_R_Peaks"], dtype=int)
    if method != "simple":
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown method {method!r}")

    # QRS polarity varies by lead: use the dominant sign
    if np.abs(sig.min()) > np.abs(sig.max()):
        sig = -sig
    height = 0.4 * np.percentile(sig, 99.5)
    peaks, _ = find_peaks(sig, height=height, distance=int(0.25 * fs))
    return peaks

def heart_rate(
    signals: ArrayLike,
    fs: int,
    method: str = "simple",
    lead: Optional[int] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Heart rate (bpm) per ECG from the median RR interval; NaN when fewer than
    two beats are found.

    Args:
        signals: ``[N, C, T]``, ``[C, T]``, or ``[T]``.
        fs: Sampling rate in Hz.
    """
    x = _as_numpy(signals)
    if x.ndim == 1:
        x = x[None, None]
    elif x.ndim == 2:
        x = x[None]
    rates: List[float] = []
    for ecg in x:
        peaks = detect_r_peaks(ecg, fs, lead=lead, method=method)
        if len(peaks) < 2:
            rates.append(np.nan)
        else:
            rates.append(60.0 * fs / float(np.median(np.diff(peaks))))
    return np.asarray(rates)

How well measured values follow requested ones (NaNs ignored).

Returns {"mae", "pearson_r", "n_valid", "n"}.

def adherence(requested: Sequence[float], measured: Sequence[float]) -> dict:
    """
    How well measured values follow requested ones (NaNs ignored).

    Returns ``{"mae", "pearson_r", "n_valid", "n"}``.
    """
    req = np.asarray(requested, dtype=np.float64)
    mea = np.asarray(measured, dtype=np.float64)
    ok = ~(np.isnan(req) | np.isnan(mea))
    out = {
        "n": int(len(req)),
        "n_valid": int(ok.sum()),
        "mae": float("nan"),
        "pearson_r": float("nan"),
    }
    if ok.sum() >= 2:
        out["mae"] = float(np.mean(np.abs(req[ok] - mea[ok])))
        if np.std(req[ok]) > 0 and np.std(mea[ok]) > 0:
            out["pearson_r"] = float(np.corrcoef(req[ok], mea[ok])[0, 1])
    return out

handcrafted_features(x: ArrayLike, fs: int = 500) -> np.ndarray

Per-ECG feature vector [N, D]:

  • heart rate (bpm, NaN → batch median);
  • per lead: standard deviation, 1st/99th percentile, and the relative power in the bands 0.5–5, 5–15, 15–40, 40–100 Hz;
  • the upper triangle of the inter-lead correlation matrix.
Source code in src/ecgen/evaluation/features.py 
def handcrafted_features(x: ArrayLike, fs: int = 500) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Per-ECG feature vector ``[N, D]``:

    - heart rate (bpm, NaN → batch median);
    - per lead: standard deviation, 1st/99th percentile, and the relative power
      in the bands 0.5–5, 5–15, 15–40, 40–100 Hz;
    - the upper triangle of the inter-lead correlation matrix.
    """
    x = _as_numpy(x)
    if x.ndim == 2:
        x = x[None]
    n, c, t = x.shape
    hr = heart_rate(x, fs)
    hr = np.where(np.isnan(hr), np.nanmedian(hr) if np.isfinite(hr).any() else 0.0, hr)

    std = x.std(axis=-1)
    p1, p99 = np.percentile(x, 1, axis=-1), np.percentile(x, 99, axis=-1)
    freqs, psd = welch(x, fs=fs, nperseg=min(t, 2 * fs), axis=-1)
    total = psd.sum(-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12
    bands = (
        np.stack(
            [
                psd[..., (freqs >= lo) & (freqs < min(hi, fs / 2))].sum(-1)
                for lo, hi in BANDS
            ],
            axis=-1,
        )
        / total
    )
    iu = np.triu_indices(c, k=1)
    corr = (
        np.stack([np.nan_to_num(np.corrcoef(e))[iu] for e in x])
        if c > 1
        else np.zeros((n, 0))
    )
    feats = [hr[:, None], std, p1, p99, bands.reshape(n, -1), corr]
    return np.concatenate(feats, axis=1).astype(np.float64)

def module_features(
    model: torch.nn.Module, batch_size: int = 64, device: Optional[str] = None
) -> Extractor:
    """Wrap a ``[B, C, T] -> [B, D]`` network as an extractor."""
    device = device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

    def extract(x: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
        xt = torch.as_tensor(_as_numpy(x), dtype=torch.float32)
        model.eval().to(device)
        out = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i in range(0, len(xt), batch_size):
                out.append(
                    model(xt[i : i + batch_size].to(device)).float().cpu().numpy()
                )
        return np.concatenate(out)

    return extract

docs.text:
frechet_distance(feats_a: ndarray, feats_b: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-06) -> float

Fréchet distance between Gaussians fitted to two feature sets (FID-style).

Source code in src/ecgen/evaluation/metrics.py 
def frechet_distance(
    feats_a: np.ndarray, feats_b: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-6
) -> float:
    """Fréchet distance between Gaussians fitted to two feature sets (FID-style)."""
    mu_a, mu_b = feats_a.mean(0), feats_b.mean(0)
    sa, sb = (
        np.atleast_2d(np.cov(feats_a, rowvar=False)),
        np.atleast_2d(np.cov(feats_b, rowvar=False)),
    )
    covmean, _ = linalg.sqrtm(sa @ sb, disp=False)
    if not np.isfinite(covmean).all():
        off = np.eye(sa.shape[0]) * eps
        covmean = linalg.sqrtm((sa + off) @ (sb + off))
    covmean = covmean.real
    return float(
        ((mu_a - mu_b) ** 2).sum() + np.trace(sa) + np.trace(sb) - 2 * np.trace(covmean)
    )

mmd_rbf(feats_a: ndarray, feats_b: ndarray, bandwidth: Optional[float] = None) -> float

Unbiased squared MMD with an RBF kernel (bandwidth = median heuristic).

Source code in src/ecgen/evaluation/metrics.py 
def mmd_rbf(
    feats_a: np.ndarray, feats_b: np.ndarray, bandwidth: Optional[float] = None
) -> float:
    """Unbiased squared MMD with an RBF kernel (bandwidth = median heuristic)."""
    x, y = np.asarray(feats_a, float), np.asarray(feats_b, float)
    z = np.concatenate([x, y])
    d2 = ((z[:, None] - z[None]) ** 2).sum(-1)
    if bandwidth is None:
        bandwidth = np.sqrt(0.5 * np.median(d2[d2 > 0])) if (d2 > 0).any() else 1.0
    k = np.exp(-d2 / (2 * bandwidth**2))
    n, m = len(x), len(y)
    kxx, kyy, kxy = k[:n, :n], k[n:, n:], k[:n, n:]
    return float(
        (kxx.sum() - np.trace(kxx)) / (n * (n - 1))
        + (kyy.sum() - np.trace(kyy)) / (m * (m - 1))
        - 2 * kxy.mean()
    )

k-NN manifold precision / recall (Kynkäänniemi et al., 2019): precision = share of generated samples inside the real manifold, recall = share of real samples inside the generated manifold.

Source code in src/ecgen/evaluation/metrics.py 
def precision_recall(
    real: np.ndarray, fake: np.ndarray, k: int = 3
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    k-NN manifold precision / recall (Kynkäänniemi et al., 2019): precision = share
    of generated samples inside the real manifold, recall = share of real samples
    inside the generated manifold.
    """

    def radii(a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        d = np.sqrt(((a[:, None] - a[None]) ** 2).sum(-1))
        return np.sort(d, axis=1)[:, min(k, len(a) - 1)]

    def inside(points: np.ndarray, ref: np.ndarray, r: np.ndarray) -> float:
        d = np.sqrt(((points[:, None] - ref[None]) ** 2).sum(-1))
        return float((d <= r[None]).any(axis=1).mean())

    return {
        "precision": inside(fake, real, radii(real)),
        "recall": inside(real, fake, radii(fake)),
    }

def distribution_metrics(
    real: ArrayLike,
    fake: ArrayLike,
    fs: int = 500,
    extractor: Optional[Callable[[ArrayLike], np.ndarray]] = None,
    k: int = 3,
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Fréchet distance, MMD and precision/recall between real and generated ECGs on
    (standardized) features; default features: :func:`handcrafted_features`.
    """
    extract = extractor or (lambda x: handcrafted_features(x, fs))
    fr, ff = extract(real), extract(fake)
    fr, ff = _standardize(fr, ff)
    out = {"frechet_distance": frechet_distance(fr, ff), "mmd": mmd_rbf(fr, ff)}
    out.update(precision_recall(fr, ff, k))
    return out

def inter_lead_correlation_error(real: ArrayLike, fake: ArrayLike) -> float:
    """Mean |corr_real − corr_fake| over lead pairs, using mean correlation matrices (MIDT-ECG)."""

    def mean_corr(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.nanmean(np.stack([np.corrcoef(e) for e in x]), axis=0)

    r, f = mean_corr(_as_numpy(real)), mean_corr(_as_numpy(fake))
    iu = np.triu_indices(r.shape[0], k=1)
    return float(np.abs(r[iu] - f[iu]).mean())
