docs.title: Adding a Dataset
docs.text:
This guide covers adding a new ECG dataset (PTB-XL, a private cohort, pre-extracted NumPy arrays, ...) and training an existing model on it with ecgen train. There are three steps:

  1. Subclass BaseECGDataset and return the dict sample contract.
  2. Make it reachable from YAML: register a name with @DATASETS.register("name"), or refer to it by import path with target:.
  3. Point the data: section of an experiment YAML at it.

No DataModule or training script is needed: the generic ecgen.data.datamodule.ECGDataModule builds the train/val/test splits of any dataset and the runner does the rest. See MIMIC-IV-ECG for the reference implementation (ecgen.data.datasets.MIMICIVECG), ecgen.data.datasets.SyntheticECG for a minimal one, and the Data API reference for signatures.

docs.title: 1. The BaseECGDataset contract
docs.text:
ecgen.data.datasets.base.BaseECGDataset (torch.utils.data.Dataset + abc.ABC):

class BaseECGDataset(Dataset, ABC):
    lead_names: List[str]          # names of the C output channels, in order
    fs: int                        # sampling rate in Hz
    seq_length: int                # samples per record (T)
    feature_normalizer: Optional[FeatureNormalizer] = None

    @abstractmethod
    def __len__(self) -> int: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, Any]: ...

    @property
    def num_leads(self) -> int:    # len(self.lead_names)
        ...

__getitem__ returns a dict:

Key Type Notes "signal" FloatTensor [C, T] C == len(lead_names), T == seq_length "cond" {field: Tensor} Condition fields, e.g. "measurements": [F]; {} for none "cond_missing" {field: BoolTensor} Same keys as cond, True = missing; {} for none "meta" dict Record ids etc.; collected into lists, never fed to a model

ECGCollate stacks the samples into an ecgen.types.ECGBatch (signal [B, C, T], lead_names, fs, cond, cond_missing, meta), taking lead_names and fs from the dataset. Every family reads the signal with get_signal(batch), so a dataset that follows this contract works with all of them.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
These are not enforced, but ECGDataModule and the runner rely on them:

  • The constructor takes split ("train", "val", "test"); ECGDataModule fills it in for each split, and all other data.dataset.params are passed as keyword arguments.
  • A deterministic, seeded split computed inside the dataset. MIMIC splits by subject, so if your data has patient IDs, split on them to avoid leakage.
  • lead_names, fs and seq_length set in __init__. The runner compares len(lead_names) and seq_length with the model before training, and ECGDataModule stores them in every checkpoint. Use names from ecgen.data.leads (STANDARD_12, INDEPENDENT_8, resolve_leads) where they apply.
  • Output float32. The VAE/VQ-VAE encoders downsample by 2 ** (len(channel_multipliers) - 1), so seq_length must divide evenly (5000 / 8 = 625).
  • Amplitude scaling via ecgen.data.datasets.base.scale_signal(ecg, scale) ("zscore" per record, "none", or a number), the same as MIMIC.
  • If you provide numeric conditions, fit a FeatureNormalizer on the train split and accept a feature_normalizer argument: ECGDataModule passes the train dataset's normalizer to val/test when the constructor takes one.

docs.title: 2. Implement the dataset
docs.text:
The example reads one (leads, time) .npy file per record:

my_project/data/npy_ecg.py
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch

from ecgen.data.datasets.base import BaseECGDataset, Scale, scale_signal
from ecgen.data.leads import STANDARD_12, LeadSpec, resolve_leads
from ecgen.registry import DATASETS


@DATASETS.register("npy_ecg")
class NpyECGDataset(BaseECGDataset):
    """One ``.npy`` file of shape (12, time) per record, leads in standard order."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        root: str,
        split: str = "train",
        val_split: float = 0.1,
        test_split: float = 0.1,
        max_samples: Optional[int] = None,
        seed: int = 42,
        leads: LeadSpec = None,
        seq_length: int = 5000,
        fs: int = 500,
        scale: Scale = "zscore",
    ) -> None:
        if split not in ("train", "val", "test"):
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown split: {split}")
        self.lead_names = resolve_leads(leads, STANDARD_12)
        self._idx = [STANDARD_12.index(n) for n in self.lead_names]
        self.seq_length = seq_length
        self.fs = fs
        self.scale = scale

        files = sorted(Path(root).glob("*.npy"))
        if not files:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"No .npy files in {root}")

        # Deterministic split; the same seed gives disjoint train/val/test
        perm = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(len(files))
        n_test = int(round(len(files) * test_split))
        n_val = int(round(len(files) * val_split))
        idx = {
            "test": perm[:n_test],
            "val": perm[n_test:n_test + n_val],
            "train": perm[n_test + n_val:],
        }[split]
        self.files = [files[i] for i in sorted(idx)]
        if max_samples is not None:
            self.files = self.files[:max_samples]

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.files)

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        ecg = np.load(self.files[idx]).astype(np.float32)[self._idx]   # (C, time)
        ecg = ecg[:, : self.seq_length]
        if ecg.shape[1] < self.seq_length:
            ecg = np.pad(ecg, ((0, 0), (0, self.seq_length - ecg.shape[1])))
        return {
            "signal": torch.from_numpy(scale_signal(ecg, self.scale)),
            "cond": {},
            "cond_missing": {},
            "meta": {"file": self.files[idx].name},
        }

Check it quickly:

import torch
from my_project.data.npy_ecg import NpyECGDataset

ds = NpyECGDataset("data/raw/npy_ecg", split="val")
x = ds[0]["signal"]
assert x.shape == (ds.num_leads, ds.seq_length) and x.dtype == torch.float32

Write a test

Add a test that writes a few random arrays to tmp_path, then checks split disjointness, output shape and dtype, and that ECGDataModule(dataset={"target": ..., "params": {...}}, batch_size=2) yields an ECGBatch. Run it with pytest tests/.

docs.title: 3. Make it reachable from YAML
docs.text:
Two options:

target: (no registration)Registered name

Refer to the class by import path. The module only has to be importable (installed, or on PYTHONPATH):

data:
  dataset:
    target: my_project.data.npy_ecg.NpyECGDataset
    params: {root: data/raw/npy_ecg}

@DATASETS.register("npy_ecg") adds the class to ecgen.registry.DATASETS when its module is imported. Built-in datasets live in src/ecgen/data/datasets/ and are imported by ecgen/data/datasets/__init__.py, which ecgen.registry.load_builtins() imports; add yours there to make name: npy_ecg work everywhere (ecgen list shows it):

data:
  dataset:
    name: npy_ecg
    params: {root: data/raw/npy_ecg}

docs.title: 4. Experiment YAML
docs.text:
Copy an existing experiment (for example configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml) to configs/experiments/vqvae_npy_ecg.yaml and replace the data: section:

experiment:
  name: vqvae_npy_ecg
  seed: 42
  runs_root: runs

data:
  dataset:
    name: npy_ecg                        # or target: my_project.data.npy_ecg.NpyECGDataset
    params:
      root: data/raw/npy_ecg
      max_samples: null
      val_split: 0.1
      test_split: 0.1
      leads: null                        # 12 leads
      seq_length: 5000
  split_params:                          # optional per-split overrides
    val: {max_samples: 500}
  batch_size: 32
  num_workers: 4

Run it:

ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_npy_ecg.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml \
    data.dataset.name=npy_ecg 'data.dataset.params={root: data/raw/npy_ecg}'   # without a new file

Outputs go to runs/<experiment.name>/seed_<seed>/, as described in Training with ecgen train.

Model compatibility checklist

  • The model's in_channels (VAE, VQ-VAE) or num_channels (Pulse2Pulse) must equal len(lead_names); the runner fails early otherwise.
  • seq_length must be divisible by the encoder's total downsampling factor (8 with the default channel_multipliers: [1, 2, 4, 4]), and equal Pulse2Pulse's seq_length (a multiple of 2500).
  • Pulse2Pulse uses 8 leads (num_channels: 8, leads: independent8). See Pulse2Pulse GAN.

configs/dataset/*.yaml fragments are reference values only; the runner reads the experiment YAML.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• BaseECGDataset subclass implementing __len__ and __getitem__, setting lead_names, fs and seq_length
  • __getitem__ returns {"signal", "cond", "cond_missing", "meta"}
  • Constructor takes split; split is seeded and leakage-free
  • Registered with @DATASETS.register("<name>") (imported by ecgen.data.datasets) or referenced with target:
  • configs/experiments/<model>_<name>.yaml with a data.dataset section
  • A test under tests/

docs.title: MIMIC-IV-ECG Dataset
docs.text:
MIMIC-IV-ECG (the Diagnostic Electrocardiogram Matched Subset) is a large collection of 10-second, 12-lead diagnostic ECGs with automated machine measurements. It is the main training dataset in ECGEN.

The loader is ecgen.data.datasets.MIMICIVECG (src/ecgen/data/datasets/mimic.py), registered as mimic_iv_ecg. It follows the BaseECGDataset dict contract and is wrapped by the generic ecgen.data.datamodule.ECGDataModule, which the training runner builds from the data: section of an experiment YAML. API details are in the Data API reference.

Legacy loader

The older tuple-returning ecgen.data.mimic_dataset.MIMICIVECGDataset and ecgen.data.pulse2pulse_mimic are still present for legacy scripts such as scripts/utils/test_pulse2pulse_setup.py, but no training path uses them. With default parameters MIMICIVECG reproduces the legacy dataset's records, splits and signals exactly.

docs.title: Directory layout
docs.text:
MIMICIVECG expects the PhysioNet release unpacked as-is. The directory you pass as root must contain:

<root>/
├── machine_measurements.csv        # required
└── files/
    └── p{first 4 digits of subject_id}/
        └── p{subject_id}/
            └── s{study_id}/
                ├── {study_id}.hea  # WFDB header
                └── {study_id}.dat  # WFDB signal

For example, subject 10000032, study 40689238 resolves to files/p1000/p10000032/s40689238/40689238 (the WFDB record name without extension).

machine_measurements.csv must contain at least these columns, or the constructor raises ValueError:

  • subject_id, study_id
  • rr_interval, p_onset, p_end, qrs_onset, qrs_end, t_end, p_axis, qrs_axis, t_axis

Where to put the data

Any location works. Pass it as root (Python) or data.dataset.params.root (experiment YAML or override). The shipped experiment configs in configs/experiments/ point to a hard-coded cluster path, so change that value for your setup. data/raw/mimic/ is the conventional location in this repo (and is gitignored).

docs.title: Getting the data
docs.text:
MIMIC-IV-ECG v1.0 is open access on PhysioNet under the ODC Open Database License (ODbL), so no credentialing is required:

wget -r -N -c -np https://physionet.org/files/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/

Then set root to the directory that contains machine_measurements.csv and files/.

No preprocessing step is needed. The dataset reads the raw WFDB files directly.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
from ecgen.data.datasets import MIMICIVECG

train_ds = MIMICIVECG(
    root="/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg-diagnostic-electrocardiogram-matched-subset-1.0",
    split="train",
    max_samples=1000,          # small subset for a smoke test
)

sample = train_ds[0]           # a dict
sample["signal"].shape         # torch.Size([12, 5000]), float32
sample["cond"]["measurements"].shape          # torch.Size([9]), z-scored with train statistics
sample["cond_missing"]["measurements"]        # bool [9], True = missing
sample["meta"]                 # {"subject_id": ..., "study_id": ...}
train_ds.lead_names, train_ds.fs, train_ds.seq_length   # ['I', 'II', 'III', 'aVR', 'aVF', 'aVL', 'V1', ...], 500, 5000

With ECGDataModule the samples are collated into an ecgen.types.ECGBatch (signal [B, C, T], lead_names, fs, cond, cond_missing, meta). All families read the signal with get_signal(batch), which also accepts the legacy dict and tuple formats.

docs.title: Dataset parameters
docs.text:
Argument Default Meaning root required Root of the MIMIC-IV-ECG release (see layout). split "train" "train", "val" or "test"; filled in by ECGDataModule. val_split / test_split 0.1 / 0.1 Fractions of subjects in the validation / test split. seed 42 random_state for the subject split. max_samples None Keep only the first N records of the selected split, after filtering. Does not affect the measurement normalizer. skip_missing_check False If True, skip the check that each record's .hea file exists (and emit a UserWarning). leads None None: the file's leads in file order I, II, III, aVR, aVF, aVL, V1–V6 (aVF before aVL), padded/truncated to num_leads. An alias, "standard12" (clinical order, aVL before aVF) or "independent8" (I, II, V1–V6), or a list of lead names, selects leads by name. num_leads 12 Channel count when leads is None. seq_length 5000 Output length in samples (zero-padded at the end or truncated). scale "zscore" "zscore": per record, (x - mean) / max(std, eps) over all selected leads (legacy default); "none": physical units (mV); a number: (x - mean) / number. ecg_norm_eps 1e-6 Lower bound on the std for "zscore". measurements None Columns of machine_measurements.csv returned in cond["measurements"]; None = the 9 standard measurements below; [] = none. missing "drop" "drop": drop rows with a NaN in any measurement column (legacy). "mask": keep them; NaNs become 0 and are flagged in cond_missing. "mask" keeps more subjects, so its split differs from "drop". report false Add cond["report"]: the non-empty report_0…report_17 machine statements joined by ". " (for text conditioning). feature_normalizer None Use these measurement statistics (a FeatureNormalizer or its dict) instead of fitting them on the train split.

In an experiment YAML these go under data.dataset.params; data.split_params overrides them per split:

data:
  dataset:
    name: mimic_iv_ecg
    params:
      root: /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg-...-1.0
      max_samples: 1000          # null = full split
      skip_missing_check: false
      val_split: 0.1
      test_split: 0.1
      leads: null                # or independent8, standard12, [I, II, V1]
      seq_length: 5000
      scale: zscore
  split_params:
    val: {max_samples: 1000}
  batch_size: 32
  num_workers: 4

The model's channel count (in_channels / num_channels) must equal the number of selected leads; the runner checks this before training.

docs.title: What the constructor does
docs.text:
1. Load measurements. Reads machine_measurements.csv and checks the required columns. With missing="drop" it drops every row with a NaN in the 9 standard measurement columns (and in any extra measurements columns).
  2. Subject-level split. Takes the unique subject_ids and runs two sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split calls with random_state=seed: first test_size=test_split → test subjects, then test_size=val_split / (1 - test_split) on the remainder → validation subjects. No subject appears in more than one split, and the split sizes are fractions of subjects, not of records.
  3. Measurement normalizer. Fits a per-column z-score (FeatureNormalizer) on the train split's rows, whichever split is being loaded, unless feature_normalizer is given. ECGDataModule also passes the train dataset's normalizer to val/test and stores it in every checkpoint (under the ECGDataModule key, with lead_names, fs and seq_length).
  4. Filter to split, then the missing-file check (unless skip_missing_check=True): keep only rows whose <record>.hea exists. If <root>/files does not exist, the check is skipped. This scans every record in the split, which can take a while on the full dataset.
  5. max_samples. Truncates to the first N rows.

Changed from the legacy loader

The legacy dataset computed the measurement statistics on whichever split it loaded, after max_samples truncation, so val/test features were normalized with different statistics from train. They now always come from the full train split.

docs.title: Per-sample processing (__getitem__)
docs.text:
1. Read the record with wfdb.rdrecord(...) and take p_signal (mV), transposed to (leads, time).
  2. Select leads (by name, or the first num_leads in file order) and pad/truncate time to seq_length.
  3. Scale according to scale (default: one mean and std over all selected leads, so relative amplitudes between leads are kept).
  4. Normalize the measurement columns with the train-split statistics; missing values become 0 with cond_missing=True.

There is no NaN handling for the waveform itself, and an unreadable record raises from wfdb.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
Key Shape dtype Notes signal (C, seq_length), default (12, 5000) float32 Scaled per record cond["measurements"] (F,), default (9,) float32 Z-scored machine measurements cond_missing["measurements"] (F,) bool True = missing (only with missing="mask") meta — — subject_id, study_id

Signal properties of the release: 500 Hz (fs), 10 s (5000 samples).

docs.title: Conditioning features
docs.text:
Default measurements, in order:

# Feature # Feature # Feature 0 rr_interval 3 qrs_onset 6 p_axis 1 p_onset 4 qrs_end 7 qrs_axis 2 p_end 5 t_end 8 t_axis

The current models are unconditional and ignore them. They are returned for conditional models.

docs.title: Configuration fragment
docs.text:
configs/dataset/mimic.yaml documents defaults under a top-level dataset: key (data_dir, num_leads, seq_length, sampling_rate, normalize, ...).

Not consumed by the runner

The runner does not load configs/dataset/mimic.yaml, and its key names differ from the MIMICIVECG parameters (data_dir vs root, normalize vs scale). Set dataset parameters in data.dataset.params of the experiment YAML. configs/dataset/ptbxl.yaml is an empty placeholder.

docs.title: Data preparation and validation scripts
docs.text:
scripts/data/ has two CLI entry points. Both are stubs right now. They parse their arguments, print a "to be implemented" message and exit.

prepare_mimic.pyvalidate_dataset.py 
python scripts/data/prepare_mimic.py \
    --raw_dir data/raw/mimic \
    --output_dir data/processed/mimic \
    [--validate]
Flag Required Description --raw_dir yes Path to raw MIMIC data --output_dir yes Output directory --validate no Flag: validate data integrity

Output: prints MIMIC data preparation - to be implemented. No files are written.

python scripts/data/validate_dataset.py \
    --data_dir data/raw/mimic \
    --dataset mimic
Flag Required Description --data_dir yes Dataset root --dataset yes mimic or ptbxl

Output: prints Validating mimic dataset - to be implemented.

Checking a download today

For a real check of the directory layout, CSV columns and WFDB readability, use single_file/test_data_loading.py --data-dir <root> (see Standalone VQ-VAE), or build a dataset with max_samples set:

python -c "from ecgen.data.datasets import MIMICIVECG as D; \
d = D('/path/to/mimic', split='val', max_samples=10); s = d[0]; print(len(d), s['signal'].shape, d.lead_names)"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix FileNotFoundError: machine_measurements.csv not found root should point at the directory that contains the CSV, not at files/. ValueError: machine_measurements.csv missing columns Wrong CSV (for example record_list.csv), or a measurements column that does not exist. ValueError: Leads [...] are not available A name in leads is misspelled; MIMIC uses I, II, III, aVR, aVF, aVL, V1–V6. ValueError: Model expects N channels but the dataset yields M leads Set leads / num_leads or the model's in_channels / num_channels so they agree. num_samples should be a positive integer value, but got num_samples=0 The split is empty: no .hea files were found, or max_samples=0. Slow startup on the full dataset The missing-file check stats every record. Use skip_missing_check: true once you know the download is complete. NaN losses The dataset does not clean NaNs in p_signal. If some records contain them, filter those records or apply np.nan_to_num in a subclass.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text: If you use MIMIC-IV-ECG, cite the dataset and PhysioNet using the citation text on the dataset page (Gow et al., "MIMIC-IV-ECG: Diagnostic Electrocardiogram Matched Subset", version 1.0, PhysioNet, 2023).

docs.title: PTB-XL
docs.text:
PTBXL (registry name ptbxl) loads PTB-XL (Wagner et al., 2020; PhysioNet ptb-xl 1.0.x): 21,799 ten-second 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz (records500/) and 100 Hz (records100/), with diagnostic statements, demographics, and reports. Optionally it joins PTB-XL+ (Strodthoff et al., 2023) 12SL measurements.

data:
  dataset:
    name: ptbxl
    params:
      root: /path/to/ptb-xl/1.0.1
      sampling_rate: 500        # or 100
      leads: standard12         # stored order: I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1–V6
      scale: zscore
      labels: all               # scp vocabulary, or null
      ptbxl_plus_root: /path/to/ptb-xl-plus/1.0.1   # optional: adds "features"

docs.title: Splits
docs.text: The recommended stratified folds: strat_fold 1–8 train, 9 val, 10 test (override with folds: {train: [...], val: [...], test: [...]}). All normalizers are fit on the training folds.

docs.title: Condition fields
docs.text:
Field Value Encoder to use Switch scp multi-hot statements multilabel (num_labels = vocabulary size) labels: all, superclass, subclass, diagnostic, form, rhythm, or null demographics normalized [age, height, weight] + missing mask numeric (num_features: 3) demographics: true sex class (0 male, 1 female) categorical (num_classes: 2) sex: true report report text (mostly German) text or text_hash report: true features normalized PTB-XL+ 12SL measurements + missing mask numeric / fourier ptbxl_plus_root, feature_columns

Vocabulary sizes: all 71, superclass 5 (NORM, MI, STTC, CD, HYP), subclass 23, rhythm 12; the order is dataset.label_names. min_likelihood drops statements below a likelihood (PTB-XL stores 0–100; the default 0 keeps every listed statement, as SSSD-ECG does). Height and weight are often missing — the numeric encoder sees the mask.

Default PTB-XL+ features: HR_Ventr_Global, PR_Int_Global, QRS_Dur_Global, QT_Int_Global, QT_IntBazett_Global, P_AxisFront_Global, R_AxisFrontal_Global, T_AxisFront_Global.

docs.title: Example configs
docs.text:
• configs/experiments/ptbxl_sssd_ecg.yaml — SSSD-ECG-style: 100 Hz, 8 independent leads, 71 statements, S4D diffusion backbone.
  • configs/experiments/ptbxl_text_demographics.yaml — flow matching conditioned on the report (frozen multilingual BERT), demographics and sex.

docs.title: Evaluation Metrics
docs.text:
The evaluation package provides metrics for judging generated ECGs: signal quality, diversity and fidelity. It also has a model benchmark helper and plotting utilities for metric results. A small set of torch-based metrics for training-time monitoring lives separately in training/metrics/.

evaluation/
├── metrics/
│   ├── __init__.py         # re-exports the 10 public metric functions
│   ├── signal_quality.py   # SNR, baseline wander, powerline interference
│   ├── diversity.py        # pairwise distance, per-class diversity, mode coverage
│   └── fidelity.py         # FID / Fréchet distance, reconstruction error, correlation
├── benchmark.py            # ModelBenchmark: params, latency, GPU memory
└── visualize.py            # bar chart and model×metric heat map

All evaluation metrics accept either a torch.Tensor (moved to CPU and converted) or a NumPy array, and return plain Python floats or dicts. They are NumPy/SciPy/scikit-learn code and are not differentiable.

from evaluation.metrics import (
    signal_to_noise_ratio, baseline_wander, powerline_interference, calculate_quality_metrics,
    pairwise_distance_diversity, intra_class_diversity, mode_coverage,
    calculate_fid, reconstruction_error, structural_similarity,
)
from evaluation.metrics.fidelity import frechet_distance   # not re-exported

Python ≥ 3.10 required at import time

signal_quality.py, diversity.py, fidelity.py and visualize.py use X | Y type hints without from __future__ import annotations. Those hints are evaluated when the module is imported, so importing evaluation.metrics or evaluation.visualize fails on Python 3.8/3.9, even though pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.8".

docs.title: ecgen.evaluation (packaged metrics)
docs.text:
The ecgen package ships the metrics from the training plan (§8). They take [N, C, T] arrays or tensors.

Function What it measures distribution_metrics(real, fake, fs, extractor=None) Fréchet distance, MMD (RBF, median bandwidth) and k-NN precision / recall on standardized features — hand-crafted by default (handcrafted_features: heart rate, per-lead amplitude percentiles and band powers, inter-lead correlations), or any network via module_features(model) heart_rate(x, fs, method="simple" \| "neurokit"), adherence(requested, measured) Requested vs. measured heart rate (MAE, Pearson r) — condition adherence for measurement conditioning fit_classifier, label_adherence, tstr A small 1D-ResNet: train it on real labelled ECGs (separate from the generator's training data), then score generated ECGs against the labels they were generated for (macro AUROC), or train on synthetic and test on real (TSTR) reconstruction_metrics(pred, true, unobserved) MAE, RMSE, Pearson r on the unobserved part (lead reconstruction, imputation) inter_lead_correlation_error(real, fake) Mean absolute difference of the average lead-correlation matrices (MIDT-ECG) einthoven_residual(x, lead_names) Relative violation of III = II − I, aVR, aVL, aVF identities (≈0 for real 12-lead ECGs) memorization_ratio(fake, train, real_holdout) Nearest-neighbour distance of generated ECGs to the training set relative to held-out real ECGs (≪ 1 suggests copying) 
ecgen sample runs/.../last.ckpt -n 256 -o gen/ --format npy
ecgen evaluate gen/samples.npy configs/experiments/diffusion_mimic.yaml --split test -n 256
python scripts/evaluate/condition_adherence.py <ckpt> --family diffusion --target rr_interval
python scripts/evaluate/lead_reconstruction.py <ckpt> --family diffusion --keep I

The sections below document the older research-layout metrics in evaluation/.

docs.title: Signal quality (evaluation/metrics/signal_quality.py)
docs.text:
These are reference-free metrics computed on a single signal.

Function Signature Returns signal_to_noise_ratio (ecg) -> float SNR in dB baseline_wander (ecg, sampling_rate: int = 500) -> float Std of the < 0.5 Hz component powerline_interference (ecg, sampling_rate: int = 500) -> float Fraction of spectral power at 50 Hz + 60 Hz calculate_quality_metrics (ecg, sampling_rate: int = 500) -> dict {"snr", "baseline_wander", "powerline_interference"}

signal_to_noise_ratio(ecg) computes 10·log10(mean(ecg²) / (std(diff(ecg))² + 1e-8)). It estimates "noise" as the spread of sample-to-sample differences along the last axis, which is a smoothness proxy rather than a true noise measurement. It works on any shape. For (C, L) or (B, C, L) inputs it returns one pooled value.

baseline_wander(ecg, sampling_rate=500) applies a 4th-order Butterworth high-pass at 0.5 Hz (scipy.signal.filtfilt along the last axis). It returns the standard deviation of the removed low-frequency part, ecg - filtered, in the same units as the input. It works on 1-D or multi-dimensional input (pooled std). The input must be longer than the filter's padding length (more than 15 samples for this order-4 filter).

powerline_interference(ecg, sampling_rate=500) takes the FFT and returns (P(50 Hz) + P(60 Hz)) / ΣP, using the nearest FFT bins to 50 and 60 Hz.

1-D input only

powerline_interference uses len(ecg) for the frequency axis and indexes power[idx] on the first axis. It is only correct for a single-lead 1-D signal of shape (L,). With a (C, L) array it raises TypeError: only length-1 arrays can be converted to Python scalars. Since calculate_quality_metrics calls it, calculate_quality_metrics is also limited to 1-D input. Loop over leads yourself:

ecg = samples[0]                      # (C, L)
per_lead = [calculate_quality_metrics(ecg[c], sampling_rate=500) for c in range(ecg.shape[0])]

docs.title: Diversity (evaluation/metrics/diversity.py)
docs.text:
These metrics take a set of samples. Every sample is flattened to a vector, so (N, C, L) becomes (N, C·L).

Function Signature Returns pairwise_distance_diversity (samples, metric: str = "euclidean") -> float Mean pairwise distance intra_class_diversity (samples, labels: np.ndarray) -> dict {str(label): mean pairwise distance} mode_coverage (samples, real_samples, n_clusters: int = 10) -> float Fraction of real-data clusters hit, in [0, 1]

pairwise_distance_diversity(samples, metric="euclidean") computes the mean of scipy.spatial.distance.pdist(samples.reshape(N, -1), metric=metric). metric can be any pdist metric ("euclidean", "cosine", "correlation", …). Higher values mean more diverse samples. Cost is O(N²·C·L).

intra_class_diversity(samples, labels) calls pairwise_distance_diversity (Euclidean) on samples[labels == label] for each unique label and skips classes with fewer than 2 samples. labels must be a NumPy array of length N, because it is used as a boolean mask.

mode_coverage(samples, real_samples, n_clusters=10) fits sklearn.cluster.KMeans(n_clusters, random_state=42) on the flattened real samples, assigns each generated sample to its nearest centroid, and returns #distinct clusters hit / n_clusters. A value of 1.0 means every real-data mode received at least one generated sample. You need at least n_clusters real samples.

docs.title: Fidelity (evaluation/metrics/fidelity.py)
docs.text:
These metrics compare generated (or reconstructed) data against real data.

Function Signature Returns frechet_distance (mu1, sigma1, mu2, sigma2, eps: float = 1e-6) -> float Fréchet distance between two Gaussians calculate_fid (real_features, generated_features) -> float FID reconstruction_error (real, reconstructed, metric: str = "mse") -> float MSE / MAE / RMSE structural_similarity (real, generated) -> float Global normalised correlation

calculate_fid(real_features, generated_features) expects 2-D feature matrices (N, D) and (M, D). It computes the mean and covariance of each (np.cov(..., rowvar=False)) and calls frechet_distance:

\[ \mathrm{FD} = \lVert \mu_1-\mu_2\rVert^2 + \mathrm{Tr}\big(\Sigma_1+\Sigma_2-2(\Sigma_1\Sigma_2)^{1/2}\big) \]

If sqrtm is not finite, frechet_distance retries with eps·I added to both covariances. It raises ValueError if the result has a significant imaginary part.

No feature extractor is included

The package has no pretrained ECG encoder. You need to supply the embeddings yourself, for example the VAE/VQ-VAE encoder output or a classifier's penultimate layer. Passing raw flattened ECGs (D = 12·5000) is technically possible but builds 60000×60000 covariance matrices, and needs N ≫ D samples for a meaningful estimate. Lower is better.

reconstruction_error(real, reconstructed, metric="mse") computes the element-wise "mse", "mae" or "rmse" averaged over all elements. Any other value raises ValueError. Shapes must match or broadcast. Use it for autoencoder reconstructions, for example VAE / VQ-VAE.

structural_similarity(real, generated) z-normalises each array with its global mean and std, then returns mean(real_norm * generated_norm), i.e. a Pearson-style correlation over all elements. Despite the name, it is not SSIM. It needs paired, same-shaped inputs (such as reconstructions) and returns a value of roughly 1.0 for identical signals.

docs.title: Example: evaluating generated samples
docs.text:
import torch
from evaluation.metrics import (
    calculate_quality_metrics, pairwise_distance_diversity, mode_coverage, calculate_fid,
)

generated = model.generate_samples(256).cpu()      # e.g. Pulse2Pulse: (256, 8, 5000)
real = torch.stack([ds[i][0][:8] for i in range(256)])  # matching real ECGs

results = {
    **calculate_quality_metrics(generated[0, 1]),  # lead II of sample 0 (1-D!)
    "diversity": pairwise_distance_diversity(generated),
    "mode_coverage": mode_coverage(generated, real, n_clusters=10),
    "fid": calculate_fid(encoder(real), encoder(generated)),   # encoder = your feature extractor
}

docs.title: Benchmarking (evaluation/benchmark.py)
docs.text:
ModelBenchmark measures size and speed for any nn.Module whose forward accepts a single torch.randn(input_shape) tensor.

ModelBenchmark(model, device: str = "cuda")
Method What it records in self.results count_parameters() total_parameters, trainable_parameters, total_parameters_millions measure_inference_time(input_shape, n_runs=100, warmup=10) inference_time_ms (mean per forward), throughput_samples_per_sec (input_shape[0] / mean time) measure_memory_usage(input_shape) memory_allocated_mb, memory_reserved_mb (peak); no-op unless device == "cuda" run_full_benchmark(input_shape, save_path=None) Runs all of the above, optionally writes JSON to save_path, returns results print_results() Pretty-prints results 
from evaluation.benchmark import ModelBenchmark
from ecgen.families.gan.pulse2pulse import Pulse2PulseGAN, Pulse2PulseConfig

model = Pulse2PulseGAN(Pulse2PulseConfig()).netG.to("cuda")   # move it yourself
bench = ModelBenchmark(model, device="cuda")
bench.run_full_benchmark(input_shape=(32, 8, 5000), save_path="benchmark_results.json")
bench.print_results()

Note

ModelBenchmark does not move the model to device; it only moves the dummy input. CUDA synchronisation and memory measurement only happen when device is exactly the string "cuda", so "cuda:1" skips both.

docs.title: Visualisation (evaluation/visualize.py)
docs.text:
Function Signature Output plot_evaluation_results (metrics: dict, save_path=None, figsize=(12, 8)) -> plt.Figure Bar chart of {name: value} with value labels plot_comparison_matrix (models: list[str], metrics: dict[str, list[float]], save_path=None, figsize=(12, 8)) -> plt.Figure Metrics × models heat map (RdYlGn_r) with annotations

For plot_comparison_matrix, each metrics[name] must be a list with one value per model, in the order of models. When save_path is given, both functions save the figure at 300 dpi with bbox_inches="tight". Bar colours in plot_evaluation_results form a fixed gradient by position and do not reflect the values. For ECG waveform plots, see Visualization.

from evaluation.visualize import plot_evaluation_results, plot_comparison_matrix

plot_evaluation_results({"snr": 24.0, "diversity": 40.4, "fid": 4.6}, save_path="eval.png")
plot_comparison_matrix(
    models=["VAE", "VQ-VAE", "Pulse2Pulse"],
    metrics={"fid": [12.1, 8.3, 9.7], "diversity": [35.2, 41.0, 40.4]},
    save_path="comparison.png",
)

docs.title: Evaluation scripts (scripts/evaluate/)
docs.text:
Placeholders

Both scripts only parse their arguments and print a "to be implemented" message. They do not load checkpoints or compute any metrics yet. Use the Python API above instead.

Script Flags Current behaviour evaluate_model.py --checkpoint (required), --data_dir (required), --output_dir (default evaluation_results) Prints Model evaluation - to be implemented benchmark_models.py --checkpoints (required, one or more), --data_dir (required), --output_dir (default benchmark_results) Prints Model benchmarking - to be implemented 
python scripts/evaluate/evaluate_model.py --checkpoint path/to/model.ckpt --data_dir /path/to/data
python scripts/evaluate/benchmark_models.py --checkpoints a.ckpt b.ckpt --data_dir /path/to/data

These scripts use underscore flags (--data_dir), while the training scripts use hyphens (--data-dir). Each script adds the repo root to sys.path, so they run from any working directory.

docs.title: Training-time metrics (training/metrics/)
docs.text:
These are torch functions that return tensors, intended for use inside training/validation steps. training/metrics/__init__.py re-exports nothing, so import from the submodules.

Module Function Description training.metrics.reconstruction reconstruction_mse(pred, target) -> Tensor mean((pred - target)²) training.metrics.reconstruction reconstruction_mae(pred, target) -> Tensor mean(|pred - target|) training.metrics.generation signal_to_noise_ratio(signal, noise) -> Tensor 10·log10(mean(signal²) / (mean(noise²) + 1e-8)), given an explicit noise tensor training.metrics.clinical wasserstein_distance(d_real, d_fake) -> Tensor d_real.mean() - d_fake.mean(), the WGAN critic estimate (higher means the critic separates real from fake better) training.metrics.clinical gradient_penalty_loss(discriminator, real_data, fake_data, lmbda=10.0) -> Tensor WGAN-GP penalty on random interpolates of (B, C, L) tensors; same as calc_gradient_penalty in the Pulse2Pulse GAN

Two different signal_to_noise_ratios

training.metrics.generation.signal_to_noise_ratio(signal, noise) takes an explicit noise tensor. evaluation.metrics.signal_to_noise_ratio(ecg) estimates noise from first differences. Despite its name, training/metrics/clinical.py contains only GAN critic metrics, not clinical ones such as intervals or heart rate.

None of the current Lightning modules import training.metrics. Pulse2PulseGAN computes its Wasserstein estimate and gradient penalty inline.

docs.text:
• API reference: Evaluation, Training
  • Pulse2Pulse GAN, VAE

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Training is driven by YAML experiment files in configs/experiments/, all run by the same command, ecgen train <config.yaml> [key=value ...].

File model.name Model vae_mimic.yaml vae VAE vqvae_mimic.yaml vqvae VQ-VAE (stage 1) prior_mimic.yaml vqvae_prior PixelCNN prior (stage 2) pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml pulse2pulse Pulse2Pulse GAN

Training with ecgen train has the full schema, an annotated example, the registry names and the run-directory layout. This page summarises how a config is applied.

docs.title: How configs are applied
docs.text:
1. The YAML is loaded, then each command-line override dotted.key=value is applied on top (values parsed as YAML). Overrides always win.
  2. Unknown top-level sections are rejected. The allowed sections are experiment, model, data, checkpoint, callbacks, trainer, wandb and resume; model and data are required.
  3. Defaults are filled in and ${run_dir}, ${name} and ${seed} are substituted in strings.
  4. The model is built from model: {name | target, params}, the dataset from data.dataset: {name | target, params}, and each callbacks: entry the same way. params are passed to the constructor as keyword arguments, so every constructor argument is configurable without editing code.
  5. The resolved config is written to runs/<name>/seed_<seed>/config_resolved.yaml.
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml --print-config        # inspect the result
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml model.params.kl_weight=1e-3 'trainer.devices=[1]'

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
experiment:     # name, seed, runs_root
model:          # name | target, params (flat config-dataclass fields)
data:           # dataset: {name | target, params}, batch_size, num_workers, pin_memory, split_params
checkpoint:     # ModelCheckpoint: monitor, mode, save_top_k, save_last, filename
callbacks:      # list of {name | target, params}
trainer:        # pl.Trainer keyword arguments
wandb:          # optional Weights & Biases logging
resume:         # checkpoint to resume from

docs.title: model.params per family
docs.text:
model.params holds the fields of the family's config dataclass, flat. The legacy nested form params: {config: {...}} is still accepted.

model.name Config dataclass Fields vae VAEConfig in_channels, base_channels, latent_channels, channel_multipliers, num_res_blocks, lr, kl_weight, b1, b2 vqvae VQVAEConfig in_channels, base_channels, latent_channels, channel_multipliers, num_res_blocks, num_embeddings, commitment_cost, lr, b1, b2 vqvae_prior PriorConfig num_embeddings, hidden_dim, num_layers, kernel_size, dilation_cycle, lr, b1, b2, vqvae_checkpoint pulse2pulse Pulse2PulseConfig model_size, num_channels, seq_length, lr, b1, b2, lmbda, n_critic

The model's channel count must equal the number of leads the dataset yields; the runner checks this before training.

docs.title: data.dataset.params for MIMIC-IV-ECG
docs.text: root, val_split, test_split, seed, max_samples, skip_missing_check, leads, num_leads, seq_length, scale, measurements, missing, feature_normalizer. See MIMIC-IV-ECG. split is filled in by the datamodule; data.split_params overrides params for one split, e.g. split_params: {val: {max_samples: 1000}}.

docs.title: callbacks
docs.text:
Built in order after the runner's own ModelCheckpoint. Registered names: vae_visualization, ecg_visualization, generated_samples, early_stopping, lr_monitor, model_checkpoint. A callback that takes save_dir defaults to ${run_dir}/samples. See Callbacks.

Removed: the visualization: section

Plot settings used to live in a top-level visualization: section read by the old VAE/VQ-VAE scripts. They are now the params of a vae_visualization callback, e.g. {name: vae_visualization, params: {log_every_n_epochs: 1, num_samples: 4}}. A config that still has visualization: fails with Unknown config sections.

docs.title: Reusable fragments
docs.text: configs/model/, configs/dataset/ and configs/training/ hold YAML fragments (model/vae/vae_1d_base.yaml, model/vae/vae_1d_large.yaml, model/vqvae/vqvae_1d_base.yaml, model/vqvae/prior_base.yaml, model/gan/pulse2pulse.yaml, dataset/mimic.yaml, dataset/ptbxl.yaml, training/fast_dev.yaml, training/production.yaml, ...). The runner does not load these files; they are reference values only. To use them, copy the values into an experiment file.

docs.title: Creating a custom experiment
docs.text:
cp configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml
# edit experiment.name, data.dataset.params.root, model.params.*, trainer.max_epochs, ...
ecgen train configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml

Change experiment.name so the run does not overwrite runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/. For one-off changes, prefer overrides to a new file:

ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml experiment.name=vae_kl1e-3 model.params.kl_weight=1e-3

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
pyproject.toml declares:

  • Python >= 3.8
  • torch>=1.10, pytorch-lightning>=1.5
  • pyyaml, pandas, scikit-learn, wfdb, matplotlib, tensorboard
  • extras: [hf] (huggingface_hub, python-dotenv), [plot] (cairosvg), [all], [dev] (pytest, black, flake8, mypy)

Python version

Several modules (for example visualization/ecg_plots.py) use X | Y type hints at runtime without from __future__ import annotations, so in practice Python 3.10+ is required to import every package.

Optional: wandb is imported lazily by the runner and callbacks only when Weights & Biases logging is enabled. It is not a declared dependency; install it yourself if you need it.

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vlbthambawita/ECGEN.git
cd ECGEN

docs.title: 2. Install the package
docs.text:
pip install -e .            # the ecgen package + the `ecgen` command
pip install -e ".[dev]"     # + pytest, black, flake8, mypy

Only the ecgen package in src/ecgen/ is installed. It contains the model families (ecgen.families.*), datasets (ecgen.data.*), the training runner (ecgen.training.runner) and the ecgen console script. The research packages at the repository root (training, evaluation, visualization) are not installed: run code that imports them from the repo root (pytest adds the root via pythonpath = ["."]). The old root packages models, data and utils were removed in 1.2; import from ecgen.* instead (see the migration table).

docs.title: 3. Verify the installation
docs.text:
ecgen list
# family: pulse2pulse, vae, vqvae, vqvae_prior
# dataset: mimic_iv_ecg, synthetic
# callback: early_stopping, ecg_visualization, generated_samples, lr_monitor, model_checkpoint, vae_visualization

python -c "from ecgen.families import VAELightning, VQVAELightning, PriorLightning, Pulse2PulseGAN; print('ok')"

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text: pytest tests/

docs.title: Dataset setup
docs.text: See MIMIC-IV-ECG Dataset for dataset setup instructions.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This page gets a VAE training on MIMIC-IV-ECG with the config-driven workflow. For the other model families see VQ-VAE training and Pulse2Pulse training.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install -e .

See Installation for details.

docs.title: 2. Point the config at your data
docs.text:
Edit configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml or pass overrides on the command line:

data:
  dataset:
    name: mimic_iv_ecg
    params:
      root: /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg   # directory containing machine_measurements.csv and files/
      max_samples: 1000             # small value for a smoke run; null for the full dataset

For a short run also lower trainer.max_epochs.

No data yet?

Add data.dataset.name=synthetic 'data.dataset.params={num_samples: 64}' to the command below to train on generated ECG-like signals. See Smoke runs.

docs.title: 3. Train
docs.text:
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml \
    data.dataset.params.root=/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg \
    data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000 trainer.max_epochs=10
# or the shell wrapper (same command, run from the repo root)
./scripts/shell/run_train_vae_mimic_config.sh configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml trainer.max_epochs=10

Command-line overrides are applied after the YAML, so they always win.

W&B is on by default

vae_mimic.yaml ships with wandb.enabled: true and log_to_wandb: true on its vae_visualization callback. Pass wandb.enabled=false if you do not have wandb installed/configured.

docs.title: 4. Monitor
docs.text:
tensorboard --logdir runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/tb
ls runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/samples/      # epoch_NNNN.png reconstruction plots

Tip

With the shipped vae_mimic.yaml (trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, log_every_n_epochs: 5 on vae_visualization) the plot and validation epochs never coincide, so no images are written. Add callbacks.2.params.log_every_n_epochs=1 to get a plot after every validation run. See Visualization.

Outputs:

runs/<experiment.name>/seed_<seed>/
├── config_resolved.yaml
├── metadata.json
├── checkpoints/   # epochNNN-stepNNNNNN.ckpt (top-3 by val_loss) + last.ckpt
├── samples/       # reconstruction plots from VAEVisualizationCallback
├── metrics/       # train_val_metrics.json
└── tb/            # TensorBoard logs

docs.title: 5. Use the trained model
docs.text:
from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning

model = VAELightning.load_from_checkpoint("runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu")
model.eval()

samples = model.sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000)   # (16, 12, 5000)

Note

The checkpoint stores the flattened VAEConfig fields as hyper-parameters, and VAELightning rebuilds its config from them, so no config= argument is needed. Passing one explicitly (load_from_checkpoint(path, config=VAEConfig(...))) still works and takes precedence.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
ECGEN models operate on multi-lead ECG tensors of shape (batch, num_leads, seq_length); the MIMIC-IV-ECG pipeline produces 12 × 5000 by default (10 s at 500 Hz).

Visual guide

The Visual Guide shows every model as animated, interactive diagrams.

Family Package Status Main classes Details VAE src/ecgen/families/vae/ Implemented VAE1D, VAELightning, VAEConfig VAE VQ-VAE + PixelCNN prior src/ecgen/families/vqvae/ Implemented VQVAE1D, VectorQuantizer, VQVAELightning, PixelCNNPrior, PriorLightning, VQVAEConfig, PriorConfig VQ-VAE GAN (Pulse2Pulse) src/ecgen/families/gan/ Implemented WaveGANGenerator, WaveGANDiscriminator, Pulse2PulseGAN, Pulse2PulseConfig GAN Diffusion models/diffusion/ Placeholder (empty __init__.py + README) — — State space models models/ssm/ Placeholder (empty __init__.py + README) — —

The families live in the ecgen package under src/ecgen/families/ and register themselves with the training runner as vae, vqvae, vqvae_prior and pulse2pulse (see Training with ecgen train). The old root import paths models.vae, models.vqvae, models.gan.pulse2pulse and models.components were removed in 1.2.

docs.title: Package pattern
docs.text:
The VAE and VQ-VAE packages follow the same layout:

  • config.py — a @dataclass holding architecture and optimiser hyper-parameters (VAEConfig, VQVAEConfig, PriorConfig).
  • *_1d.py — a plain nn.Module (VAE1D, VQVAE1D).
  • *_lightning.py — a pl.LightningModule wrapper (VAELightning, VQVAELightning, PriorLightning) that owns the loss, logging, configure_optimizers() and sample(). The constructor takes either the dataclass or an equivalent dict, or the fields as keyword arguments, so load_from_checkpoint(path) works from the saved hyperparameters.
  • losses.py — the family's loss functions.

Every wrapper subclasses ecgen.families.base.GenerativeModule, which fixes the shared contract: batches are read with get_signal(batch) (an ECGBatch, a {"signal"} / legacy {"ecg_signals"} dict, or an (ecg, features) tuple), sample() returns [n, C, T], and class attributes family and supports (Capabilities) describe the model.

Losses live next to each family: ecgen.families.vae.losses.vae_loss, ecgen.families.vqvae.losses.vqvae_loss / prior_loss, and WGAN / LSGAN helpers in ecgen.families.gan.losses.

Pulse2Pulse is a single module, src/ecgen/families/gan/pulse2pulse.py, containing the networks, the config dataclass, calc_gradient_penalty() and the Pulse2PulseGAN LightningModule.

docs.title: Shared components (src/ecgen/nn/)
docs.text: Exported from ecgen.nn: ResidualBlock1D, Encoder1D, Decoder1D. Both the VAE and the VQ-VAE are built from these.

docs.title: ResidualBlock1D(in_channels, out_channels)
docs.text: Conv1d(k=3) → GroupNorm(8) → SiLU → Conv1d(k=3) → GroupNorm(8) → SiLU, plus a residual shortcut (1×1 conv when the channel count changes, identity otherwise). Because of GroupNorm(8, ·), every channel width used in the encoder/decoder must be divisible by 8.

docs.title: Encoder1D
docs.text:
Arguments (defaults): in_channels=12, base_channels=64, latent_channels=8, channel_multipliers=(1, 2, 4, 4), num_res_blocks=2.

  1. Conv1d(in_channels → base_channels, k=7)
  2. For each multiplier m: num_res_blocks × ResidualBlock1D(→ base_channels·m); after every stage except the last, a strided Conv1d(k=4, stride=2) halves the length.
  3. Two middle ResidualBlock1Ds, GroupNorm, SiLU.
  4. Conv1d(→ 2·latent_channels, k=3), split into (mean, logvar).

With S = len(channel_multipliers) the temporal downsampling factor is 2**(S-1); the default (1, 2, 4, 4) gives 8×, so a 5000-sample input yields a latent of length 625.

docs.title: Decoder1D
docs.text: Mirror image of the encoder (multipliers reversed): Conv1d(latent_channels → ·, k=3), two middle residual blocks, per-stage residual blocks with ConvTranspose1d(k=4, stride=2) upsampling between stages, then GroupNorm → SiLU → Conv1d(→ out_channels, k=7). There is no output activation.

docs.title: VAE
docs.text: VAE1D = Encoder1D → reparameterisation → Decoder1D. Loss = MSE reconstruction + kl_weight × KL (KL normalised by B·C·L). See VAE.

docs.title: VQ-VAE + PixelCNN prior (two stages)
docs.text:
Stage 1 — VQVAE1D / VQVAELightning. The same Encoder1D is used, but only its mean output is kept (default latent_channels=64). VectorQuantizer(num_embeddings=512, embedding_dim=latent_channels, commitment_cost=0.25) snaps every latent vector to its nearest codebook entry (L2), with vq_loss = ||sg[z_q] - z||² + commitment_cost·||z_q - sg[z]||² and a straight-through estimator. forward() returns (recon, vq_loss, indices) with indices of shape (B, L_latent). Total loss = MSE reconstruction + vq_loss (ecgen.families.vqvae.losses.vqvae_loss).

Stage 2 — PixelCNNPrior / PriorLightning. PriorLightning loads a frozen stage-1 checkpoint (PriorConfig.vqvae_checkpoint), encodes each batch to code indices, and trains a WaveNet-style autoregressive prior: an embedding of the codes shifted right by one position, num_layers (default 10) CausalGatedBlocks (causal dilated convs with kernel size 2, dilations 2 ** (i % dilation_cycle), gated tanh·sigmoid activations, residual and skip 1×1 convs), and a ReLU/1×1-conv head over the summed skips that outputs num_embeddings logits. The default receptive field is 1024 codes, which covers the full 625-code sequence. Logit t predicts code t from codes < t, in training and in sampling. Loss is cross-entropy (ecgen.families.vqvae.losses.prior_loss).

Sampling. PriorLightning.sample() draws code indices autoregressively from the prior and decodes them with the frozen VQ-VAE (decode_from_indices). VQVAELightning.sample() exists too, but picks indices uniformly at random and is only a sanity check.

See VQ-VAE and VQ-VAE training.

docs.title: Pulse2Pulse GAN
docs.text:
A WaveGAN-derived, U-Net-style 1-D GAN trained with WGAN-GP:

  • WaveGANGenerator(model_size=50, num_channels=8, ...) maps a noise tensor of the same shape as the ECG ((B, num_channels, seq_length), uniform in [-1, 1]) through six strided Conv1d(k=25) layers and six upsampling layers, four of which concatenate encoder skip connections, ending in tanh.
  • WaveGANDiscriminator stacks seven Conv1d(k=25) layers with LeakyReLU(0.2) and phase shuffle, and lazily creates its final Linear layer from the observed input length.
  • Pulse2PulseGAN uses manual optimisation: one critic step per batch (Wasserstein loss + gradient penalty weighted by lmbda=10), and a generator step every n_critic=5 batches; Adam with b1=0.5, b2=0.9, lr=1e-4. It defaults to 8 leads (num_channels=8).

Note

All wrappers, including Pulse2PulseGAN, read the signal with get_signal(batch), so they train on the ECGBatch objects produced by ECGDataModule as well as on the legacy dict and tuple batch formats.

See GAN and Pulse2Pulse training.

docs.title: Placeholders: diffusion and SSM
docs.text: models/diffusion/ and models/ssm/ contain only a docstring __init__.py and a README stating they are reserved for future work (the SSM README mentions Mamba and S4). VAE1D.encode_to_latent() / decode_from_latent() are provided with a future latent-diffusion stage in mind.

docs.title: Adding a new model
docs.text:
1. Create src/ecgen/families/<family>/ with config.py (dataclass), the nn.Module, losses.py and a GenerativeModule wrapper taking config=None, **kwargs; export them from the package __init__.py and import that from src/ecgen/families/__init__.py.
  2. Reuse ecgen.nn blocks where they fit.
  3. Register the wrapper with @FAMILIES.register("<name>") (or reference it with model.target) and add an experiment YAML under configs/experiments/; no training script is needed. See Extending.

docs.title: Diffusion and flow matching
docs.text:
Visual guide

Animated diagrams of the noising process, the UNet1d backbone, guidance, the loss and sampling: Diffusion (DDPM) and Flow Matching.

DiffusionModule (registry name diffusion) is a Gaussian diffusion model (DDPM, Ho et al., 2020) over raw 12-lead ECGs. It is one instance of ContinuousGenerativeModule, which separates three choices:

Choice Config key Built-in Process — how training pairs are corrupted and how samples are integrated model.params.process ddpm Backbone — the network f(x_t, t, cond) model.params.backbone unet1d Conditioning — what the model is conditioned on model.params.conditioning see Conditioning

FlowMatchingModule (registry name flow_matching) is the same module with the rectified_flow process as its default — see Flow matching.

docs.title: DDPM process (ddpm)
docs.text:
Param Default Meaning num_steps 1000 Diffusion steps T schedule "cosine" "cosine" (Nichol & Dhariwal) or "linear" beta schedule prediction "v" Network target: "eps", "v" (Salimans & Ho) or "x0" min_snr_gamma 5.0 Min-SNR-γ loss weighting; null = uniform clip_x0 null Clamp predicted x0 while sampling (z-scored ECGs reach about ±10)

Sampling is DDIM (Song et al., 2021) over steps evenly spaced steps; eta=0 is deterministic, eta=1 ancestral.

docs.title: Flow matching
docs.text:
Process rectified_flow (family flow_matching): time runs from noise (t = 0) to data (t = 1) along straight paths x_t = t·x1 + (1 − (1 − σ_min)·t)·x0; the network regresses the velocity x1 − (1 − σ_min)·x0, and sampling integrates the ODE with Euler or Heun steps. Typically 10–25 steps (Heun: two network calls per step) give samples comparable to 50+ DDIM steps.

Param Default Meaning t_sampling "logit_normal" Training time distribution ("uniform" or logit-normal, Esser et al. 2024) logit_mean, logit_std 0.0, 1.0 Logit-normal parameters sigma_min 0.0 Path width at t = 1 (0 = rectified flow) ot_coupling false Minibatch optimal-transport pairing of noise and data (OT-CFM) time_scale 1000.0 Network time input = t · time_scale solver "euler" Default ODE solver ("euler" or "heun"); override per call with sample(solver=...)

Everything else — backbone, conditioning, CFG (on the velocity), EMA, loss_on, clean_observed — is shared with diffusion. Training-free inpainting supports replace (the observed part follows its straight path from the initial noise); RePaint is diffusion-only.

docs.title: U-Net backbone (unet1d)
docs.text:
ADM-style 1D U-Net: residual blocks with AdaGN on the time (+ condition) embedding, self-attention at attn_levels, cross-attention to condition tokens at the same levels, and dense conditions concatenated to the input. The signal length must be divisible by 2 ** (len(channel_mults) - 1) (5000 works with four levels).

Param Default base_channels 64 channel_mults [1, 2, 4, 4] num_res_blocks 2 attn_levels [3] (the lowest resolution) heads 4 dropout 0.0

docs.title: Other backbones
docs.text:
Name Idea Condition slots Notes unet1d Convolutional U-Net (above) vector, tokens, dense Default; length divisible by 2^(levels-1) dit1d Transformer over patches of patch_size samples, AdaLN-Zero modulation, cross-attention in every block (Peebles & Xie, 2023) vector, tokens, dense Length divisible by patch_size; good for latents (e.g. 625 / 5 = 125 tokens) ssm SSSD-style stack of bidirectional S4D state-space layers at full resolution (Alcaraz & Strodthoff, 2023; Gu et al., 2022), pure PyTorch vector, dense Global receptive field via FFT convolution mamba ssm with bidirectional Mamba layers (Gu & Dao, 2023) vector, dense Needs mamba-ssm (CUDA)

dit1d: patch_size (25), dim (256), depth (8), heads (8), mlp_ratio (4). ssm / mamba: channels (128), depth (8), state_size (64 / 16), bidirectional (true), dropout.

docs.title: Latent diffusion and flow matching
docs.text:
latent_diffusion and latent_flow_matching run the same processes in the latent space of a frozen stage-1 autoencoder (Rombach et al., 2022):

  • autoencoder_family: vae — a spatial, unconditional vae; the posterior mean is the latent ([latent_channels, T / 8]);
  • autoencoder_family: vqvae — the quantized embeddings are the latent; sampled latents are snapped to the codebook before decoding.

The stage-1 config is stored in the checkpoint (autoencoder_config) and its weights in the state dict, so the stage-1 file is not needed after training (the same pattern as the PixelCNN prior). Latents are multiplied by latent_scale (default: 1 / std of the first training batch, then fixed and saved). Dense conditions are pooled to the latent length; loss_on, clean_observed and training-free inpainting are signal-space options and are rejected. Example: configs/experiments/latent_diffusion_mimic.yaml.

docs.title: Module options (ContinuousConfig)
docs.text: Field Default Meaning lr, weight_decay, b1, b2 2e-4, 0, 0.9, 0.999 AdamW warmup_steps 500 Linear LR warm-up ema_decay 0.999 EMA of the weights, used for sampling (0 = off); stored in checkpoints loss_on "all" "unobserved": loss only where obs_mask is 0 clean_observed false SSSD-style: observed entries of x_t are the clean signal, in training and sampling sample_steps 50 Default sampling steps guidance 1.0 Default classifier-free guidance scale

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
from ecgen.families import DiffusionModule

model = DiffusionModule.load_from_checkpoint("runs/diffusion_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt")
x = model.sample(16, steps=50, seed=0)                       # unconditional
x = model.sample(16, cond={"measurements": [...]}, guidance=2.0)  # conditional + CFG
x = model.sample(4, obs=ecg, obs_mask=mask)                  # model trained with a masked_signal condition
x = model.sample(4, obs=ecg, obs_mask=mask, inpaint="repaint", jumps=5)  # any model, training-free

Inpainting modes: replace overwrites the observed part with the observation noised to the current level after every step; repaint additionally resamples each step jumps times (Lugmayr et al., 2022). The observed part is pasted into the output unless paste_observed=False.

docs.title: Example configs
docs.text:
• configs/experiments/diffusion_mimic.yaml — unconditional
  • configs/experiments/diffusion_mimic_conditional.yaml — conditioned on the machine measurements, CFG
  • configs/experiments/diffusion_mimic_leads.yaml — lead reconstruction / imputation
  • configs/experiments/flow_matching_mimic.yaml — conditional flow matching
  • configs/experiments/diffusion_mimic_ssm.yaml — SSSD-style S4D backbone
  • configs/experiments/latent_diffusion_mimic.yaml — latent diffusion with a DiT backbone

Evaluate lead reconstruction with python scripts/evaluate/lead_reconstruction.py <ckpt> --family diffusion --keep I (add --inpaint repaint for an unconditional model).

docs.title: Adding a process or backbone
docs.text: A process subclasses ecgen.processes.Process (training_pair, sample) and is registered with @PROCESSES.register("name"); a backbone implements forward(x, t, cond), declares accepts (condition slots) and takes in_channels, cond_dim, context_dim, dense_channels; register it with @BACKBONES.register("name"). Neither needs changes to the family.

docs.title: Pulse2Pulse GAN
docs.text:
Pulse2Pulse is a WaveGAN-style generative adversarial network for ECG synthesis, trained with the WGAN-GP objective (Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty). The generator is a 1D U-Net that turns a uniform-noise tensor with the same shape as an ECG into an ECG; the discriminator (critic) is a deep strided 1D CNN with WaveGAN phase shuffling.

Visual guide

For animated diagrams of the input, architecture, output and loss, see the visual guide.

By default it models 8 leads × 5000 samples (10 s at 500 Hz): leads I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1, V2, the first 8 channels of the 12-lead MIMIC-IV-ECG records.

For training and sample generation, see Pulse2Pulse Training.

docs.title: Where the code lives
docs.text:
src/ecgen/families/gan/pulse2pulse.py (ecgen.families.gan.pulse2pulse, also exported from ecgen.families.gan), registered with the training runner as pulse2pulse. The old import path models.gan.pulse2pulse was removed in 1.2; ecgen.models.pulse2pulse still works but is deprecated (removed in 2.0).

from ecgen.families.gan import Pulse2PulseGAN, Pulse2PulseConfig

The public names in the module are:

  • Pulse2PulseConfig: dataclass with the hyperparameters
  • Pulse2PulseGAN: the LightningModule (generator + discriminator + WGAN-GP training loop)
  • WaveGANGenerator, WaveGANDiscriminator: the plain nn.Modules
  • PhaseShuffle, Transpose1dLayer, Transpose1dLayerMultiInput: building blocks
  • calc_gradient_penalty(netD, real_data, fake_data, lmbda): the WGAN-GP penalty

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Z["noise U(-1,1)<br/>(B, C, L)"] --> G["WaveGANGenerator<br/>(1D U-Net)"]
    G -->|"tanh, (B, C, L)"| D["WaveGANDiscriminator<br/>(critic)"]
    X["real ECG<br/>(B, C, L)"] --> D
    D --> S["score (B, 1)"]

docs.title: Generator: WaveGANGenerator
docs.text:
WaveGANGenerator(
    model_size: int = 50,
    num_channels: int = 8,
    post_proc_filt_len: int = 0,
    verbose: bool = False,
    upsample: bool = True,
)

The input is noise of shape (B, num_channels, seq_length), not a latent vector. The encoder path has six Conv1d layers (kernel 25, padding=12, LeakyReLU). The decoder path upsamples with nn.Upsample followed by a Conv1d (kernel 25), and concatenates U-Net skip connections from the encoder. The output goes through tanh, so generated values are in [-1, 1].

Shapes for the defaults (model_size=50, num_channels=8, input length 5000):

Encoder layer Channels Stride Output shape conv_1 8 → 10 (ms//5) 2 (B, 10, 2500) conv_2 10 → 25 (ms//2) 5 (B, 25, 500) conv_3 25 → 50 (ms) 2 (B, 50, 250) conv_4 50 → 150 (3·ms) 5 (B, 150, 50) conv_5 150 → 250 (5·ms) 5 (B, 250, 10) conv_6 250 → 250 (5·ms) 5 (B, 250, 2) Decoder layer Skip input Upsample Output channels deconv_1 — ×5 5·ms deconv_2 conv_5 ×5 3·ms deconv_3 conv_4 ×5 ms deconv_5 conv_3 ×2 ms//2 deconv_6 conv_2 ×5 ms//5 deconv_7 — ×2 num_channels (then tanh)

With upsample=False, the layers use ConvTranspose1d (stride 4) instead. Setting post_proc_filt_len > 0 adds a final Conv1d(num_channels, num_channels, post_proc_filt_len). Pulse2PulseGAN never passes these two arguments, so it always uses the defaults (upsample=True, no post-processing filter).

Sequence length constraint

The encoder downsamples by 2·5·2·5·5·5 = 2500, so seq_length must be a multiple of 2500: 2500, 5000 and 10000 work, but 4000 fails with a shape mismatch at the skip concatenation.

With the defaults, the generator has about 10.5 M parameters.

docs.title: Discriminator: WaveGANDiscriminator
docs.text:
WaveGANDiscriminator(
    model_size: int = 64,
    num_channels: int = 8,
    shift_factor: int = 2,
    alpha: float = 0.2,
    verbose: bool = False,
)

It has seven Conv1d layers (kernel 25, padding=11) with LeakyReLU (negative_slope=alpha). A PhaseShuffle(shift_factor) follows each of the first six layers.

Layer Channels (×model_size) Stride Output for L=5000, ms=50 conv1 C → 1 2 (B, 50, 2499) conv2 1 → 2 2 (B, 100, 1249) conv3 2 → 5 2 (B, 250, 624) conv4 5 → 10 2 (B, 500, 311) conv5 10 → 20 4 (B, 1000, 78) conv6 20 → 25 4 (B, 1250, 19) conv7 25 → 100 4 (B, 5000, 5)

The output is flattened and passed to a final nn.Linear(flat_dim, 1) that is created lazily on the first forward pass (_ensure_fc) to match the sequence length. The critic returns an unbounded score of shape (B, 1), with no sigmoid.

Pulse2PulseGAN builds the discriminator with model_size=config.model_size (50 by default), not with the class default of 64. At model_size=50 it has about 204 M parameters. Most of them are in conv7, so the critic is roughly 20× larger than the generator.

PhaseShuffle shifts each sample in the batch by a random integer k ∈ [-shift_factor, shift_factor] along time and fills the gap with reflection padding. This stops the critic from relying on exact sample phase.

docs.title: Configuration: Pulse2PulseConfig
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Pulse2PulseConfig:
    model_size: int = 50
    num_channels: int = 8
    seq_length: int = 5000
    lr: float = 1e-4
    b1: float = 0.5
    b2: float = 0.9
    lmbda: float = 10.0
    n_critic: int = 5
Field Default Meaning model_size 50 Width multiplier for both generator and discriminator num_channels 8 Number of ECG leads (input and output channels) seq_length 5000 Samples per ECG; also the noise length (must be a multiple of 2500) lr 1e-4 Adam learning rate (same for G and D) b1, b2 0.5, 0.9 Adam betas (same for G and D) lmbda 10.0 Gradient-penalty weight λ n_critic 5 A generator update happens every n_critic batches

Pulse2PulseGAN(config) accepts either a Pulse2PulseConfig or a plain dict with these keys.

configs/model/gan/pulse2pulse.yaml is not used

That fragment (latent_dim, base_channels, lr_g, lr_d, b2: 0.999, ...) does not match Pulse2PulseConfig, and nothing reads it. The values that take effect are the Pulse2PulseConfig defaults overridden by model.params in configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml. See Pulse2Pulse Training.

docs.title: Training objective (WGAN-GP)
docs.text:
Pulse2PulseGAN sets automatic_optimization = False and runs a manual loop in training_step. It reads the real ECGs with get_signal(batch) (an ECGBatch's signal, or the legacy batch["ecg_signals"]), of shape (B, num_channels, seq_length).

For every batch, it updates the critic:

\[ \mathcal{L}_D = \mathbb{E}[D(\tilde x)] - \mathbb{E}[D(x)] + \lambda\,\mathbb{E}_{\hat x}\big[(\lVert\nabla_{\hat x} D(\hat x)\rVert_2 - 1)^2\big] \]

Here \(\tilde x = G(z)\) with \(z \sim U(-1,1)\) (detached), and \(\hat x\) is a random per-sample interpolation between real and fake (calc_gradient_penalty).

It updates the generator only when (batch_idx + 1) % n_critic == 0, using \(\mathcal{L}_G = -\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) with fresh noise.

Both optimizers are torch.optim.Adam(lr=config.lr, betas=(config.b1, config.b2)). configure_optimizers returns [opt_g, opt_d], [], with no LR schedulers.

docs.title: Logged metrics
docs.text:
Key When Meaning train/d_loss step + epoch (prog bar) Critic loss incl. GP train/d_wasserstein step + epoch D(real) - D(fake), the Wasserstein estimate train/g_loss step + epoch (prog bar) -D(G(z)); logged as 0.0 on steps without a G update val/d_wasserstein epoch (prog bar) Wasserstein estimate on validation batches val_loss epoch (prog bar) -val/d_wasserstein

configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml checkpoints on val/d_wasserstein with mode: max.

validation_step also stores the first real and generated sample of batch 0 in _val_real_sample / _val_fake_sample. ECGVisualizationCallback reads these (see Callbacks).

docs.title: Loss helpers in src/ecgen/families/gan/losses.py
docs.text:
The Lightning module computes its losses inline and does not import this module. The helpers are equivalent, standalone functions:

Function Returns wgan_discriminator_loss(d_real, d_fake, gp) d_fake - d_real + gp wgan_generator_loss(d_fake) -d_fake adversarial_loss(pred, target_is_real: bool) BCE-with-logits against all-ones / all-zeros targets least_squares_discriminator_loss(d_real, d_fake) 0.5 * (mean((d_real-1)^2) + mean(d_fake^2)) least_squares_generator_loss(d_fake) 0.5 * mean((d_fake-1)^2)

wgan_* do not reduce, so pass already-averaged critic outputs. The WGAN-GP penalty is also available as training.metrics.clinical.gradient_penalty_loss(discriminator, real_data, fake_data, lmbda=10.0), and the Wasserstein estimate as training.metrics.clinical.wasserstein_distance(d_real, d_fake) (see Evaluation Metrics).

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
import torch
from ecgen.families.gan.pulse2pulse import Pulse2PulseGAN, Pulse2PulseConfig

model = Pulse2PulseGAN(Pulse2PulseConfig())
samples = model.generate_samples(n_samples=16)   # (16, 8, 5000), values in [-1, 1]

# or, equivalently, with your own noise:
z = torch.empty(4, 8, 5000).uniform_(-1, 1)
with torch.no_grad():
    ecg = model(z)                                # forward() == netG(noise)

generate_samples(n_samples=16) runs under @torch.no_grad(), switches netG to eval mode, and samples noise on the generator's device.

docs.title: Loading a checkpoint
docs.text:
A plain load_from_checkpoint restores the model:

from ecgen.families.gan.pulse2pulse import Pulse2PulseGAN

model = Pulse2PulseGAN.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/pulse2pulse_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt",
    map_location="cpu",
)
samples = model.generate_samples(16)

The constructor accepts either config= or the flat Pulse2PulseConfig fields that save_hyperparameters(config.__dict__) stores in the checkpoint, so no config needs to be passed (an explicit config=Pulse2PulseConfig(...) still works). The checkpoint also holds netD.fc1.* weights for the lazily created linear layer; on_load_checkpoint creates fc1 at the saved size before the state dict is loaded, so strict loading works and strict=False is not needed. scripts/generate/generate_pulse2pulse.py uses this call.

docs.title: Conditional Pulse2Pulse
docs.text:
With conditioning in the config, Pulse2PulseGAN is a conditional WGAN-GP (see Conditioning): global conditions drive FiLM layers in the generator's decoder and a projection head in the critic; a dense masked_signal condition is concatenated to the generator's noise and to the critic's input (paired critic). l1_weight adds a pix2pix-style L1 term on the unobserved part, which makes it a lead-reconstruction model (configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_lead_reconstruction.yaml).

Field Default Meaning conditioning None Conditioning config (ecgen.conditioning) l1_weight 0.0 Weight of the L1 term to the real ECG l1_on "unobserved" L1 on the unobserved part (needs data.masks) or on "all" output_scale 1.0 Multiplies the generator's tanh output

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
• Fixed: the critic's final linear layer was never trained. fc1 used to be created on the first forward pass, after configure_optimizers() had built opt_d, so it stayed at its random initialisation. Pulse2PulseGAN now builds fc1 in __init__ (from seq_length), so it is in the critic's optimizer. Models trained before this fix had a fixed random fc1; their checkpoints still load.
  • Output range vs. data scaling. The generator ends in tanh (range [-1, 1]), but MIMICIVECG (with the default scale: zscore) z-score normalises each record (zero mean, unit std), so real ECGs regularly exceed ±1. Set output_scale (e.g. 8.0 for z-scored data) to stretch the generator's range, or scale the data into ±1 (e.g. scale: 5 = mV / 5).
  • n_critic is based on batch_idx. If an epoch has fewer than n_critic batches (for example, with a tiny max_samples), the generator is never updated. The epoch mean of train/g_loss includes the logged zeros.
