docs.title: VAE
docs.text:
A 1-D convolutional variational autoencoder for multi-lead ECG, in src/ecgen/families/vae/.

Visual guide

For animated diagrams of the input, architecture, output and loss, see the visual guide.

Class File Role VAEConfig src/ecgen/families/vae/config.py Dataclass of architecture + optimiser settings VAE1D src/ecgen/families/vae/vae_1d.py nn.Module: Encoder1D → reparameterisation → Decoder1D VAELightning src/ecgen/families/vae/vae_lightning.py LightningModule: loss, logging, Adam, reconstruct(), sample() vae_loss src/ecgen/families/vae/losses.py MSE + weighted KL 
from ecgen.families.vae import VAE1D, VAELightning, VAEConfig
from ecgen.families.vae.losses import vae_loss

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
VAE1D is built from the shared blocks in src/ecgen/nn/ (see Architecture overview):

  • Encoder (Encoder1D): Conv1d(k=7) → per stage, num_res_blocks × ResidualBlock1D (GroupNorm + SiLU, residual shortcut) with a stride-2 Conv1d(k=4) between stages → two middle residual blocks → Conv1d(k=3) producing 2·latent_channels channels, split into mean and logvar.
  • Latent: Gaussian, z = mean + exp(0.5·logvar)·ε.
  • Decoder (Decoder1D): Conv1d(k=3) → two middle residual blocks → per stage residual blocks with stride-2 ConvTranspose1d(k=4) between stages → GroupNorm → SiLU → Conv1d(k=7). No output activation.

The latent is a sequence, not a vector: shape (B, latent_channels, L / 2**(S-1)) where S = len(channel_multipliers). With the defaults, a (B, 12, 5000) input gives a (B, 8, 625) latent (8× temporal compression).

Sequence length

seq_length should be divisible by 2**(S-1) for the reconstruction to have the input length. 5000 works with the default four-stage setup (5000 / 8 = 625).

docs.title: Configuration (VAEConfig)
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning in_channels 12 Number of ECG leads (also the decoder's output channels) base_channels 64 Width of the first stage latent_channels 8 Channels of the latent sequence channel_multipliers (1, 2, 4, 4) Per-stage width multipliers; length sets the number of stages num_res_blocks 2 Residual blocks per stage lr 1e-4 Adam learning rate kl_weight 0.0001 Weight of the KL term b1, b2 0.9, 0.999 Adam betas conditioning None Conditioning config → conditional VAE (see Conditioning) learned_prior False Learn p(z \| c) instead of N(0, I) (needs conditioning) recon_on "all" "unobserved": reconstruction loss only where obs_mask is 0 latent_type "spatial" "global": one global_latent_dim vector per ECG; prior samples decode to coherent ECGs global_latent_dim 64 Size of the global latent seq_length 5000 Signal length, needed by latent_type: global

Sampling from a spatial-latent VAE

With latent_type: spatial every latent position has an independent N(0, 1) prior, so sample() draws incoherent latents and the decoder output is not a realistic ECG. The spatial VAE is a good autoencoder (e.g. the first stage of a latent diffusion model), not a sampler on its own. Use latent_type: global for sampling.

All widths (base_channels × m) must be divisible by 8 because of GroupNorm(8, ·).

Parameter counts (VAE1D, 12 leads):

Setting Parameters base_channels=32, other defaults ~1.57 M Defaults ~6.22 M configs/model/vae/vae_1d_large.yaml (base_channels=128, latent_channels=16, channel_multipliers=(1, 2, 4, 8), num_res_blocks=3) ~82.8 M

docs.title: Loss
docs.text:
total, recon, kl = vae_loss(recon, x, mean, logvar, kl_weight=0.0001)
  • recon = F.mse_loss(recon, x) (mean over all elements)
  • kl = -0.5 · Σ(1 + logvar − mean² − exp(logvar)) / (B · C · L) — summed over the latent and normalised by the input size B·C·L
  • total = recon + kl_weight · kl

kl_weight trades reconstruction fidelity against how close the latent stays to N(0, I); it matters for the quality of sample().

docs.title: Plain module
docs.text:
import torch
from ecgen.families.vae import VAE1D
from ecgen.families.vae.losses import vae_loss

model = VAE1D(in_channels=12, base_channels=64, latent_channels=8,
              channel_multipliers=(1, 2, 4, 4), num_res_blocks=2)

x = torch.randn(4, 12, 5000)
recon, mean, logvar = model(x)            # (4,12,5000), (4,8,625), (4,8,625)
total, rec, kl = vae_loss(recon, x, mean, logvar, kl_weight=1e-4)

Other VAE1D methods: encode(x) -> (mean, logvar), reparameterize(mean, logvar), decode(z), and the no-grad helpers encode_to_latent(x) (returns mean) and decode_from_latent(z), intended for a future latent-diffusion stage.

docs.title: Lightning module
docs.text:
from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning, VAEConfig

model = VAELightning(VAEConfig(latent_channels=8, kl_weight=1e-4))
# or: VAELightning({"latent_channels": 8, "kl_weight": 1e-4})

recon = model.reconstruct(x)                          # no-grad, eval mode
samples = model.sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000) # z ~ N(0, I) of shape (16, 8, 625) -> decode

Logged metrics: train/total_loss, train/recon_loss, train/kl_loss (step + epoch), val/total_loss, val/recon_loss, val/kl_loss, and val_loss (used for checkpointing / early stopping). The optimiser is a single Adam with no LR scheduler.

Batch format

VAELightning reads the signal with get_signal(batch), so it trains on the ECGBatch objects produced by ECGDataModule and also accepts legacy {"ecg_signals": ...} dicts and (ecg, features) tuples. Train it with ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml; see VAE training.

docs.title: Loading a checkpoint
docs.text:
Checkpoints from VAELightning (and from the removed train_vae_mimic.py script's VAEDataWrapper) store the flattened VAEConfig fields as hyper-parameters and the weights under vae.*, so they can be loaded into VAELightning. The constructor accepts either config= or the flat config fields as keyword arguments, so a plain load_from_checkpoint works:

from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning

model = VAELightning.load_from_checkpoint("runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu")
model.eval()

Passing config=VAEConfig(...) explicitly still works and takes precedence over the stored hyper-parameters. Unknown keyword arguments raise TypeError: Unexpected VAEConfig fields: [...].

docs.title: Latent interpolation
docs.text:
z1 = model.vae.encode_to_latent(x[:1])
z2 = model.vae.encode_to_latent(x[1:2])
frames = [model.vae.decode_from_latent((1 - a) * z1 + a * z2) for a in torch.linspace(0, 1, 10)]

docs.title: Tuning hints
docs.text:
• Blurry / over-smoothed reconstructions: lower kl_weight, or increase base_channels / num_res_blocks.
  • Good reconstructions but poor random samples: the latent is far from N(0, I); raise kl_weight.
  • Out of memory: lower the batch size, base_channels or num_res_blocks.

docs.title: VQ-VAE + PixelCNN Prior
docs.text:
ECGEN's VQ-VAE is a two-stage generative model for 12-lead ECGs:

Visual guide

For animated diagrams of the input, architecture, output and loss, see the visual guide.

  1. Stage 1 – VQ-VAE (VQVAELightning): a 1D convolutional autoencoder whose latent is snapped to the nearest entry of a learned codebook, so each ECG becomes a sequence of discrete code indices.
  2. Stage 2 – PixelCNN prior (PriorLightning): an autoregressive model over those code indices, trained while the stage-1 model stays frozen.

To generate, the prior samples a sequence of code indices and the VQ-VAE decoder turns it into an ECG.

All classes live in src/ecgen/families/vqvae/ and are exported from ecgen.families.vqvae:

from ecgen.families.vqvae import (
    VQVAEConfig, PriorConfig,            # dataclass configs
    VQVAE1D, VectorQuantizer,            # plain nn.Modules (stage 1)
    PixelCNNPrior, CausalGatedBlock,     # plain nn.Modules (stage 2)
    VQVAELightning, PriorLightning,      # LightningModule wrappers
)

For training instructions, see VQ-VAE Training. For the generated API reference, see Models API.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    X["ECG<br/>[B, 12, 5000]"] --> E["Encoder1D"]
    E -->|"z [B, 64, 625]"| VQ["VectorQuantizer<br/>codebook 512 x 64"]
    VQ -->|"z_q [B, 64, 625]"| D["Decoder1D"]
    D --> R["Reconstruction<br/>[B, 12, 5000]"]
    VQ -.->|"indices [B, 625]"| P["PixelCNNPrior<br/>(stage 2)"]
    P -.->|"sampled indices"| VQ

docs.title: Encoder and decoder
docs.text:
VQVAE1D reuses the shared Encoder1D / Decoder1D from src/ecgen/nn/, the same blocks that the VAE uses:

  • ResidualBlock1D (src/ecgen/nn/blocks.py): two Conv1d(k=3) → GroupNorm(8) → SiLU layers with a residual shortcut (a 1×1 conv when the channel count changes).
  • Encoder1D: Conv1d(k=7) stem, then for each entry in channel_multipliers, num_res_blocks residual blocks at base_channels * mult channels. A stride-2 Conv1d(k=4) follows every stage except the last. Then two mid residual blocks, GroupNorm, SiLU, and a Conv1d to 2 * latent_channels, which is split into (mean, logvar).
  • Decoder1D: the mirror image. It uses ConvTranspose1d(k=4, stride=2) upsampling and a Conv1d(k=7) output to in_channels leads.

Only the first half of the encoder output is used

Encoder1D was written for the VAE and returns (mean, logvar). VQVAE1D.encode() keeps only mean as the continuous latent z and discards logvar. It returns (z, z) so the API matches the VAE's.

docs.title: Vector quantizer
docs.text:
VectorQuantizer(num_embeddings, embedding_dim, commitment_cost) (src/ecgen/families/vqvae/vector_quantizer.py) works as follows:

  • It holds an nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) codebook, initialised uniformly in [-1/K, 1/K].
  • It finds the nearest codebook vector (L2 distance) for every latent time step.
  • It computes vq_loss = mse(sg[z_q], z) + commitment_cost * mse(z_q, sg[z]), where sg is stop-gradient. In this formula the first term updates the encoder and the second term updates the codebook. The original VQ-VAE paper does the opposite: it puts β on the encoder (commitment) term. Here β = commitment_cost scales the codebook term, even though the code comments call it the commitment loss.
  • It passes gradients to the encoder with the straight-through estimator: z_q = z + (z_q - z).detach().
  • forward(z) returns (vq_loss, quantized [B, C, L], indices [B, L]).
  • get_codebook_entry(indices) maps [B, L] indices back to [B, C, L] vectors.

embedding_dim is set to latent_channels.

docs.title: PixelCNN prior
docs.text:
PixelCNNPrior(num_embeddings=512, hidden_dim=128, num_layers=10, kernel_size=2, dilation_cycle=10) (src/ecgen/families/vqvae/pixelcnn_prior.py) is a WaveNet-style stack of causal dilated convolutions. It has these parts:

  • nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, hidden_dim) turns code indices into vectors.
  • The embedded sequence is shifted right by one position (zeros at t = 0), so position t only sees codes < t.
  • num_layers CausalGatedBlock(hidden_dim, kernel_size, dilation) blocks. Block i uses dilation 2 ** (i % dilation_cycle), so with the defaults the dilations are 1, 2, 4, …, 512. Each block left-pads its input by (kernel_size - 1) * dilation, applies a causal dilated conv with the gated activation tanh(W_f * x) * sigmoid(W_g * x), and produces a 1×1 residual output (added to the block input) and a 1×1 skip output.
  • The skip outputs of all blocks are summed and passed through a head: ReLU, 1×1 Conv1d, ReLU, 1×1 Conv1d to num_embeddings logits.
  • forward(indices [B, L]) returns logits [B, num_embeddings, L]. The logit at position t predicts code t from codes < t.
  • receptive_field returns 1 + sum((kernel_size - 1) * d) over the block dilations: 1024 codes with the defaults, which covers all 625 codes of a 5000-sample ECG.
  • sample(batch_size=1, latent_length=625, temperature=1.0, device="cuda") fills a zero tensor one position at a time, drawing each code from softmax(logits / temperature). Each step only feeds the last receptive_field codes to the network (indices[:, start:i+1]), which gives the same result as feeding the full context.

Training and sampling use the logits the same way: logit t is trained to predict code t (see PriorLightning.compute_loss below), and sampling draws code t from logit t.

docs.title: Shapes and downsampling factor
docs.text:
The encoder has len(channel_multipliers) stages, but only the first len - 1 stages downsample. Each stride-2 conv halves the length, so:

downsampling factor = 2 ** (len(channel_multipliers) - 1)

With the default (1, 2, 4, 4) the factor is 8, which gives these shapes:

Tensor Shape (defaults, seq_length=5000) Input ECG [B, 12, 5000] Continuous latent z [B, 64, 625] Quantized latent z_q [B, 64, 625] Code indices [B, 625] (values in [0, 512)) Prior logits [B, 512, 625] Reconstruction [B, 12, 5000]

seq_length should be divisible by the factor, or the reconstruction will be shorter than the input.

VQVAELightning.downsample_factor returns this factor, and VQVAELightning.latent_length(seq_length) returns seq_length // factor. It raises ValueError if seq_length is not a multiple of the factor. VQVAELightning.sample() and PriorLightning.sample() both use it, so samples always have the requested length.

With the default config, the stage-1 model has about 6.38 M parameters and the PixelCNN prior has about 1.14 M (1,136,256).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Both configs are dataclasses in src/ecgen/families/vqvae/config.py. The Lightning wrappers accept the dataclass, a plain dict (converted with Config(**dict)), or the fields as flat keyword arguments (VQVAELightning(num_embeddings=256)), which is what load_from_checkpoint uses.

docs.title: VQVAEConfig
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning in_channels int 12 Number of ECG leads (input and output channels) base_channels int 64 Channel width of the first encoder stage latent_channels int 64 Latent channels, which is also the codebook embedding dim channel_multipliers tuple[int, ...] (1, 2, 4, 4) Per-stage width multipliers. len - 1 sets the number of ×2 downsamplings num_res_blocks int 2 Residual blocks per stage num_embeddings int 512 Codebook size K commitment_cost float 0.25 Weight β in the VQ loss lr float 1e-4 Adam learning rate b1 float 0.9 Adam β1 b2 float 0.999 Adam β2

docs.title: PriorConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning num_embeddings int 512 Vocabulary size. Must equal the VQ-VAE's num_embeddings hidden_dim int 128 Embedding and conv width of the PixelCNN num_layers int 10 Number of CausalGatedBlock layers kernel_size int 2 Kernel size of the causal convolutions dilation_cycle int 10 Layer i uses dilation 2 ** (i % dilation_cycle). The defaults give dilations 1 … 512 and a receptive field of 1024 codes lr float 1e-3 Adam learning rate b1 float 0.9 Adam β1 b2 float 0.999 Adam β2 vqvae_checkpoint str "" Path to the stage-1 checkpoint. If non-empty (and vqvae_config is unset), it is loaded and frozen in __init__ vqvae_config dict \| None None The VQ-VAE's config fields. Filled in automatically when vqvae_checkpoint is loaded, so prior checkpoints can be restored without the stage-1 file. If set, __init__ builds the VQ-VAE from it instead of reading vqvae_checkpoint

configs/model/vqvae/vqvae_1d_base.yaml and configs/model/vqvae/prior_base.yaml list the same defaults as YAML fragments. See VQ-VAE Training for how the experiment YAMLs are wired.

docs.title: Losses
docs.text:
Both losses live in src/ecgen/families/vqvae/losses.py.

Function Signature Computes vqvae_loss (recon, x, vq_loss) -> (total, recon_loss, vq_loss) recon_loss = mse(recon, x) (mean). total = recon_loss + vq_loss. There is no KL term prior_loss (logits [B, K, L], targets [B, L]) -> loss Mean cross-entropy over all positions

vq_loss is the codebook + commitment loss returned by VectorQuantizer. The total loss has no extra weight on it.

docs.title: VQVAELightning (stage 1)
docs.text:
src/ecgen/families/vqvae/vqvae_lightning.py. Constructed as VQVAELightning(config) and wraps a VQVAE1D in self.vqvae.

Method Description forward(x) Returns (recon, vq_loss, indices) training_step / validation_step Read the signal with get_signal(batch): an ECGBatch (from ECGDataModule), a {"signal"} or legacy {"ecg_signals"} dict, or an (ecg, features) tuple reconstruct(x) no_grad. Returns the reconstruction [B, C, L] encode_to_indices(x) no_grad. Returns code indices [B, L_latent]. The prior uses this decode_from_indices(indices) no_grad. Returns an ECG [B, C, L_latent * factor] sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000) Decodes uniformly random code indices. Useful only as a sanity check. Use the prior for real generation configure_optimizers() Single Adam optimizer (lr, betas=(b1, b2))

reconstruct, encode_to_indices, decode_from_indices and sample put the inner model in eval() mode.

Logged metrics:

Key When train/total_loss, train/recon_loss, train/vq_loss Every step and epoch train/unique_codes, train/codebook_usage Every 100th training batch. codebook_usage = unique_codes / num_embeddings val/total_loss, val/recon_loss, val/vq_loss Per epoch val_loss Per epoch (same as val/total_loss). Monitored by checkpointing and early stopping val/unique_codes, val/codebook_usage Per epoch

Watch codebook usage

A low codebook_usage means codebook collapse: only a few codes are ever selected. That limits reconstruction quality and makes the prior's job trivial.

docs.title: PriorLightning (stage 2)
docs.text:
src/ecgen/families/vqvae/prior_lightning.py. Constructed as PriorLightning(config) and wraps a PixelCNNPrior in self.prior. The frozen VQ-VAE in self.vqvae is set up in one of two ways:

  • If config.vqvae_config is set (the case when restoring a prior checkpoint), __init__ builds an untrained VQVAELightning(config.vqvae_config), calls .eval() and .freeze(), and the weights are then filled in from the prior checkpoint's own state_dict.
  • Otherwise, if config.vqvae_checkpoint is non-empty, __init__ loads it with VQVAELightning.load_from_checkpoint(path, map_location="cpu"), calls .eval() and .freeze(), and records the VQ-VAE's config as vqvae_config in the prior's hyperparameters. It raises FileNotFoundError if the path does not exist.
Method Description forward(indices) Returns the prior logits [B, K, L] compute_loss(indices) Returns prior_loss(self.prior(indices), indices): cross-entropy of each code given the codes before it training_step / validation_step Encode the batch with the frozen VQ-VAE (encode_to_indices), then return compute_loss(indices). Raise RuntimeError if no VQ-VAE is loaded sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000, temperature=1.0) Samples indices from the prior and decodes them with the VQ-VAE. See the factor-16 warning above configure_optimizers() Adam over self.prior parameters only

Logged metrics: train/loss (per step and epoch), and val/loss and val_loss (per epoch).

Because self.vqvae is a registered submodule, the frozen VQ-VAE weights are saved inside every prior checkpoint, under keys vqvae.vqvae.*. Together with the recorded vqvae_config, this makes a prior checkpoint self-contained (see Loading checkpoints).

Retrain stage-2 checkpoints from before the prior rewrite

The prior used to be a stack of mask-A/B GatedMaskedConv1d layers. Prior checkpoints from that architecture have different state_dict keys and cannot be loaded into the current PriorLightning. Retrain stage 2 from your stage-1 checkpoint. Stage-1 VQ-VAE checkpoints are not affected.

docs.title: Loading checkpoints
docs.text:
Both wrappers accept either config= or the flat config fields as keyword arguments, which is how save_hyperparameters(config.__dict__) stores them. A plain load_from_checkpoint(path) therefore works, for checkpoints written before and after this was fixed:

from ecgen.families.vqvae import VQVAELightning, PriorLightning

vqvae = VQVAELightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu"
)
prior = PriorLightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/prior_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu"
)
  • Passing config=VQVAEConfig(...) / config=PriorConfig(...) explicitly still works and takes precedence over the stored hyperparameters.
  • Unknown keyword arguments raise TypeError: Unexpected VQVAEConfig fields: [...] (or PriorConfig).
  • A prior checkpoint stores vqvae_config, so PriorLightning.load_from_checkpoint rebuilds the frozen VQ-VAE from the prior checkpoint's own weights and does not read the stage-1 file. Prior checkpoints saved before vqvae_config was added lack this field and still load the VQ-VAE from the stored vqvae_checkpoint path, so that file must exist (pass vqvae_checkpoint=<path> to load_from_checkpoint if it has moved).

docs.title: Reconstruction and code extraction
docs.text:
import torch
from ecgen.families.vqvae import VQVAELightning

vqvae = VQVAELightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu"
).eval()

x = torch.randn(4, 12, 5000)                 # [B, leads, samples]
recon = vqvae.reconstruct(x)                 # [4, 12, 5000]
indices = vqvae.encode_to_indices(x)         # [4, 625], dtype long
x_hat = vqvae.decode_from_indices(indices)   # [4, 12, 5000]

docs.title: Sampling example
docs.text:
import torch
from ecgen.families.vqvae import PriorLightning

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# The prior checkpoint also contains the frozen VQ-VAE (weights + config)
prior = PriorLightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/prior_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location=device
).eval()

ecgs = prior.sample(
    n_samples=16,
    seq_length=5000,      # must be a multiple of the VQ-VAE downsampling factor (8)
    temperature=1.0,      # >1 more diverse, <1 more conservative
)                         # [16, 12, 5000]

# Or step by step: sample 625 codes, then decode them
indices = prior.prior.sample(
    batch_size=16, latent_length=prior.vqvae.latent_length(5000), device=device
)                                               # [16, 625]
ecgs = prior.vqvae.decode_from_indices(indices) # [16, 12, 5000]

Sampling is sequential over the 625 latent positions. Each step runs a forward pass of the prior over the last receptive_field codes (all of them with the defaults), so expect it to be slow on CPU.

docs.title: Standalone VQ-VAE (single_file/)
docs.text:
single_file/ holds a self-contained two-stage VQ-VAE for MIMIC-IV-ECG. All model, data, loss, callback and training code is in one Python file, so you can copy the directory to another machine and run it without installing ECGEN.

File Purpose train_vqvae_standalone.py Everything: models, dataset, Lightning modules, callback, CLI. --stage 1 trains the VQ-VAE and --stage 2 trains the PixelCNN prior. run_train_vqvae.sh Bash wrapper configured through environment variables. Runs stage 1, stage 2, or both in sequence. test_data_loading.py Pre-flight check of a MIMIC-IV-ECG directory. README.md, QUICK_START.md, SUMMARY.md, FIXES.md, WANDB_GUIDE.md Older notes that this page replaces. Parts of them are out of date (see Corrections).

Independent copy: changes do not propagate

The standalone file imports nothing from the ecgen package or the root models/, data/, training/ or utils/ packages. It re-implements the same architecture as the packaged VQ-VAE (ecgen.families.vqvae). A fix or change in one is not reflected in the other. Checkpoints are also not interchangeable without care, because the module class paths differ. See Differences from the packaged implementation.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
pip install torch pytorch-lightning matplotlib numpy pandas scikit-learn wfdb
pip install wandb   # optional; only used with --wandb

wandb is imported in a try/except. If it is missing, --wandb prints a warning and training continues with TensorBoard only.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
cd single_file

# 1. Check the data
python test_data_loading.py --data-dir /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg

# 2. Smoke test: 100 records/split, 10 epochs per stage, no W&B
DATA_DIR=/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg \
MAX_SAMPLES=100 MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE1=10 MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE2=10 \
WANDB_ENABLED=false \
./run_train_vqvae.sh both

# 3. Monitor
tensorboard --logdir runs

docs.title: Validating the data
docs.text:
python test_data_loading.py [--data-dir PATH]
Flag Default --data-dir $DATA_DIR if set, otherwise the hard-coded cluster path /work/vajira/DATA/SEARCH/MIMIC_IV_ECG_raw_v1/mimic-iv-ecg-diagnostic-electrocardiogram-matched-subset-1.0

The checks run in this order and stop at the first hard failure (exit code 1):

  1. The directory exists.
  2. machine_measurements.csv exists (its size is printed).
  3. The CSV loads with pandas (row count and columns are printed).
  4. The required columns subject_id, study_id, and the 9 measurement columns are present.
  5. files/ exists, and the .hea/.dat pair is present for the first 10 rows. If none are found, the check fails. If only some are, it prints a warning.
  6. wfdb.rdrecord loads the first readable record among the first 100 rows, and the script prints its shape and sampling frequency. If wfdb is not installed, this is only a warning.

On success it prints suggested run_train_vqvae.sh commands.

docs.title: Running with the shell wrapper
docs.text:
./run_train_vqvae.sh [1|2|both]     # default: both
  • 1: stage 1 only.
  • 2: stage 2 only. Requires VQVAE_CHECKPOINT to point to an existing file.
  • both: stage 1, then stage 2 using the checkpoint stage 1 just produced.

The wrapper calls train_vqvae_standalone.py by absolute path, so you can run it from any directory. However, RUNS_ROOT (default runs) is resolved relative to your current directory.

After stage 1, the wrapper picks the stage-2 input with find <ckpt_dir> -name "epoch*.ckpt" | sort | tail -n 1, falling back to last.ckpt. This gives the highest-epoch retained top-k checkpoint, which is not necessarily the one with the lowest val_loss. To choose explicitly, run stage 2 separately with VQVAE_CHECKPOINT=....

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
All variables are optional. The defaults below are copied from the script.

There are no variables for --kernel-size or --dilation-cycle; their script defaults (2 and 10) are used VQVAE_CHECKPOINT unset --vqvae-checkpoint; required for 2, set automatically by both Variable Default Maps to LR_STAGE1 0.0001 --lr (stage 1) LR_STAGE2 0.001 --lr (stage 2) MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE1 100 --max-epochs (stage 1) MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE2 100 --max-epochs (stage 2) ACCELERATOR gpu --accelerator DEVICES 0 --devices (space-separated IDs, e.g. "0 1") LOG_EVERY_N_STEPS 50 --log-every-n-steps CHECK_VAL_EVERY_N_EPOCH 1 --check-val-every-n-epoch GRADIENT_CLIP 1.0 --gradient-clip PATIENCE 10 --patience SAVE_TOP_K 3 --save-top-k VIZ_EVERY_N_EPOCHS 5 --viz-every-n-epochs (stage 1) VIZ_NUM_SAMPLES 4 --viz-num-samples (stage 1) Variable Default Effect WANDB_ENABLED true Adds --wandb. Only the exact string true enables it. WANDB_PROJECT ecg-vqvae --wandb-project WANDB_ENTITY empty --wandb-entity if non-empty WANDB_RUN_NAME empty --wandb-run-name; stage 2 gets <name>_stage2 WANDB_TAGS empty --wandb-tags (space-separated)

The wrapper has no variable for --skip-missing-check, --b1 or --b2. Call the Python script directly to use them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Full dataset, larger codebook
DATA_DIR=/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg MAX_SAMPLES=null \
MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE1=200 MAX_EPOCHS_STAGE2=200 BATCH_SIZE=64 NUM_EMBEDDINGS=1024 \
./run_train_vqvae.sh both

# Stage 2 from a chosen checkpoint
VQVAE_CHECKPOINT=runs/vqvae_mimic_standalone/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt \
./run_train_vqvae.sh 2

# Codebook-size sweep (stage 1 only)
for K in 256 512 1024 2048; do
  NUM_EMBEDDINGS=$K EXP_NAME_STAGE1="vqvae_emb${K}" ./run_train_vqvae.sh 1
done

docs.title: Running the Python script directly
docs.text:
# Stage 1
python train_vqvae_standalone.py --stage 1 \
    --data-dir /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg --exp-name vqvae_exp \
    --batch-size 32 --max-epochs 100 --num-embeddings 512

# Stage 2
python train_vqvae_standalone.py --stage 2 \
    --data-dir /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg --exp-name prior_exp \
    --vqvae-checkpoint runs/vqvae_exp/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt \
    --num-embeddings 512

docs.text:
Flag Type / default Notes --stage 1 or 2, required --exp-name vqvae_mimic Run dir: <runs-root>/<exp-name>/seed_<seed>/ --seed 42 Seeds Python, NumPy, torch, and the data split --runs-root runs --data-dir required Must contain machine_measurements.csv --batch-size 32 --num-workers 4 --max-samples None Per split (train and val) --skip-missing-check flag Skip the .hea/.dat existence scan --val-split / --test-split 0.1 / 0.1 Subject-level fractions --in-channels 12 Stage 1; also the dataset lead count. There is no --resume flag

The older README shows --resume ..., but the script does not define it, and argparse will reject it. trainer.fit is always called without ckpt_path.

CPU runs

--devices is always parsed as a list of ints. Lightning's CPU accelerator rejects a list (devices selected with CPUAccelerator should be an int > 0), so --accelerator cpu does not currently work with this script.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
The standalone file has its own MIMICIVECGDataset, similar to but not identical to the packaged ecgen.data.datasets.MIMICIVECG:

  • Splits by subject_id with two seeded train_test_split calls (test first, then val from the remainder). This gives the same subject sets as the packaged dataset only when the input rows are identical, and they are not, because the packaged dataset drops NaN feature rows before splitting (its default missing: drop).
  • Does not drop rows with NaN measurements. Feature statistics use nanmean/nanstd.
  • The missing-file check requires both .hea and .dat, and prints how many it found. If the split is empty after filtering and max_samples, the constructor raises ValueError: Dataset is empty after filtering! with hints.
  • If a record fails to load, it prints the error and returns an all-zero ECG instead of raising.
  • Extra leads are truncated, but fewer than num_leads leads are not padded. Time is zero-padded or truncated to seq_length.
  • Per-sample normalization (x - x.mean()) / (x.std() + 1e-6) over all leads.
  • Returns (ecg[num_leads, seq_length], features[9]).

VQVAEMIMICDataModule builds only train and val splits (no test), with shuffle=True for train and pin_memory=True.

docs.title: Stage 1: VQ-VAE
docs.text:
x [B, 12, 5000]
 └─ Encoder1D: conv7 → (2 ResBlocks per level, stride-2 conv between levels) × 4 levels, mults (1,2,4,4)
               → mid ResBlock ×2 → GroupNorm → SiLU → conv3 → 2·latent channels; first half kept
 z [B, 64, 625]          (3 downsamplings: 5000 / 8 = 625)
 └─ VectorQuantizer (K = 512 codes, dim 64, nearest neighbour, straight-through)
 z_q [B, 64, 625], indices [B, 625]
 └─ Decoder1D (mirror, ConvTranspose1d upsampling)
 x̂ [B, 12, 5000]

With default settings the model has about 6.4 M parameters.

Loss (vqvae_loss): MSE(x̂, x) + vq_loss. In the code,

codebook_loss   = F.mse_loss(quantized.detach(), z)      # gradient flows to the encoder
commitment_loss = F.mse_loss(quantized, z.detach())      # gradient flows to the codebook
vq_loss = codebook_loss + commitment_cost * commitment_loss

So commitment_cost (β) scales the term that updates the codebook, and the encoder-side term has weight 1. This is the reverse of the usual VQ-VAE convention (‖sg[z] − e‖² + β‖z − sg[e]‖²). Keep this in mind when tuning --commitment-cost. The packaged implementation has the same behaviour.

Optimizer: Adam(lr, (b1, b2)), with no scheduler.

docs.title: Stage 2: PixelCNN prior
docs.text:
indices [B, 625]  (from the frozen stage-1 encoder, computed on the fly each batch)
 └─ Embedding(K, hidden_dim) → shift right by one (zeros at t = 0)
 └─ CausalGatedBlock × num_layers   (left-padded causal conv, kernel 2, dilation 2^(i % dilation_cycle) = 1, 2, …, 512;
                                     tanh·sigmoid gate → 1×1 residual (+ input) and 1×1 skip)
 └─ Σ skips → ReLU → Conv1d 1×1 → ReLU → Conv1d 1×1
 logits [B, K, 625]   (logit t predicts code t from codes < t; receptive field 1024 codes)

With default settings the prior has about 1.14 M parameters. sample() draws the 625 codes one at a time and feeds each step only the last receptive_field codes.

Loss: prior_loss(logits, indices), the cross-entropy of each code given the codes before it (no target shift, so training matches sampling). The stage-1 model is frozen (eval() + freeze()).

Old stage-2 checkpoints

Prior checkpoints saved before the switch from mask-A/B GatedMaskedConv1d layers to CausalGatedBlock have different state_dict keys and cannot be loaded. Retrain stage 2. Stage-1 checkpoints are unaffected.

docs.title: Callbacks and logging
docs.text:
Stage 1 Stage 2 ModelCheckpoint epoch{epoch:03d}-step{step:06d}.ckpt, last.ckpt, top-k by val_loss same EarlyStopping val_loss, patience same LearningRateMonitor per step per step Reconstruction plots samples/epoch_XXXX.png every viz-every-n-epochs (real vs. recon of the first val example, up to 8 leads) — Trainer deterministic=True deterministic=True

Logged metrics:

  • Stage 1: train/total_loss, train/recon_loss, train/vq_loss, train/unique_codes and train/codebook_usage (every 100th batch), val/total_loss, val/recon_loss, val/vq_loss, val/unique_codes, val/codebook_usage, val_loss.
  • Stage 2: train/loss, val/loss, val_loss.

Useful signals: val/recon_loss should go down, and val/codebook_usage (unique codes / K per batch) shows codebook collapse when it stays very low.

docs.title: Weights & Biases
docs.text:
pip install wandb && wandb login           # once
WANDB_PROJECT=my-ecg WANDB_ENTITY=my-team WANDB_TAGS="sweep v2" ./run_train_vqvae.sh 1
WANDB_ENABLED=false ./run_train_vqvae.sh both   # disable (the wrapper enables W&B by default)
WANDB_MODE=offline ./run_train_vqvae.sh both    # offline; later: wandb sync runs/<exp>/seed_42/wandb/

When --wandb is set, the script creates a WandbLogger with save_dir=<run_dir> and a config dict containing the stage, the architecture, lr, batch_size, max_epochs, seed and, for stage 2, vqvae_checkpoint. If initialization raises an error, or wandb is not installed, it prints a warning and continues with TensorBoard. TensorBoard is always on.

Stage 1 metrics do not reach W&B

In train_stage1_vqvae the trainer is built with logger=tb_logger instead of logger=loggers_list. The WandbLogger is constructed but never attached, so stage-1 metrics go to TensorBoard only. Stage 2 passes loggers_list and logs to both.

docs.title: Loading checkpoints and sampling
docs.text:
VQVAELightning and PriorLightning rebuild their config from the flat hyperparameters stored in the checkpoint, so a plain load_from_checkpoint(path) works (passing config= explicitly is still accepted). When stage 2 loads the stage-1 checkpoint, it records the VQ-VAE's config as vqvae_config in the prior's hyperparameters; together with the vqvae.* weights already stored in the prior checkpoint, this makes the prior checkpoint self-contained, so loading it does not read the stage-1 file. (Prior checkpoints saved before vqvae_config was added still load the VQ-VAE from the stored vqvae_checkpoint path.)

PriorLightning.sample() derives the latent length from the VQ-VAE (VQVAELightning.latent_length(seq_length), a downsampling factor of 8 by default), so samples have the requested length. seq_length must be a multiple of that factor; otherwise it raises ValueError.

# run from inside single_file/
import torch
from train_vqvae_standalone import VQVAELightning, PriorLightning

# Stage 1 on its own (reconstruction, encode_to_indices, decode_from_indices)
vqvae = VQVAELightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/vqvae_mimic_standalone/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu"
).eval()

# Prior: also restores its frozen VQ-VAE from the prior checkpoint
prior = PriorLightning.load_from_checkpoint(
    "runs/prior_mimic_standalone/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cuda"
).eval()

samples = prior.sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000, temperature=1.0)  # [16, 12, 5000], per-sample normalized units
torch.save(samples.cpu(), "generated_ecgs.pt")

docs.title: Differences from the packaged implementation
docs.text:
Aspect single_file/ Packaged (ecgen.families.vqvae + ecgen train) Code location One file, no repo imports ecgen.families.vqvae, ecgen.data.datasets.MIMICIVECG, ecgen.training Installation none (plain pip deps) pip install -e . Configuration CLI flags / env vars only configs/experiments/{vqvae,prior}_mimic.yaml plus key=value overrides Entry point one script with --stage 1 or --stage 2; run_train_vqvae.sh with 1, 2 or both ecgen train <config> per stage; scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_mimic.sh, run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh Dataset own copy (keeps NaN-feature rows, zero ECG on read errors, no lead padding, train/val only) MIMICIVECG (drops NaN-feature rows by default, raises on read errors, pads or selects leads, train/val/test) Batch format tuple only ECGBatch from ECGDataModule; the wrappers also accept legacy tuples and dicts Visualization minimal built-in callback (1 example, PNG only) vae_visualization callback (VAEVisualizationCallback: num_samples, overlay/all-leads, TensorBoard/W&B logging) Resume not supported --resume <ckpt> W&B stage 1 logger not attached (bug) attached by the runner when wandb.enabled Default run names vqvae_mimic_standalone, prior_mimic_standalone (wrapper) vqvae_mimic, prior_mimic Shared behaviour same architecture, defaults, metric names, checkpoint naming, config-from-hyperparameters checkpoint loading (self-contained prior checkpoints), and sampling via VQVAELightning.latent_length()

The nn.Module attribute names match (vqvae.encoder, vqvae.vq, vqvae.decoder, prior.*), so state-dict weights can in principle be moved between the two by loading the state_dict into the other class. load_from_checkpoint across implementations is not supported. For the packaged workflow, see VQ-VAE and VQ-VAE training.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Data directory not found (wrapper) / ERROR: Data directory does not exist Set DATA_DIR / --data-dir to the folder containing machine_measurements.csv. Dataset is empty after filtering! Run test_data_loading.py. Check that files/p*/p*/s*/*.hea and .dat exist. Try --skip-missing-check (Python script only). TypeError: Unexpected VQVAEConfig fields: [...] (or PriorConfig) A keyword argument passed to the constructor or load_from_checkpoint is not a config field. Check its spelling. devices selected with CPUAccelerator should be an int > 0 CPU runs are not supported by the current --devices parsing. CUDA out of memory Lower BATCH_SIZE, or BASE_CHANNELS/LATENT_CHANNELS. Low codebook_usage Try a smaller NUM_EMBEDDINGS. Note the β convention before tuning COMMITMENT_COST. Slow start on the full dataset The file-existence scan touches every record. Use --skip-missing-check once the data is known to be complete. unrecognized arguments: --resume Not supported here. Use ecgen train ... --resume <ckpt>.

docs.title: Corrections to the older notes
docs.text:
The Markdown files in single_file/ predate several changes. Compared with the code:

  • WANDB_ENABLED: WANDB_GUIDE.md lists the default as false. The wrapper default is true.
  • W&B support: FIXES.md says W&B "was never included". It is included, but stage 1 does not attach the logger.
  • --resume: shown in README.md, but the flag does not exist.
  • Sampling snippet: works as written, returning [16, 12, 5000]. See above.
  • Low codebook usage → "increase commitment cost": with the β placement in this code, β scales the codebook update, not encoder commitment.
  • The README omits LOG_EVERY_N_STEPS and CHECK_VAL_EVERY_N_EPOCH, which the wrapper does support.

docs.title: Training Callbacks
docs.text:
Callbacks live in src/ecgen/training/callbacks/visualization.py and are exported from ecgen.training.callbacks:

from ecgen.training.callbacks import (
    VAEVisualizationCallback,
    ECGVisualizationCallback,
    GeneratedSamplesCallback,
)

ecgen.training.callbacks.checkpointing (CustomCheckpointCallback) and ecgen.training.callbacks.logging (CustomLoggingCallback) are empty placeholders.

docs.title: Registry names
docs.text:
The runner builds the callbacks: list of an experiment YAML in order. Each entry is {name: <registered name>, params: {...}} or {target: <import.path.Class>, params: {...}}:

Name Class vae_visualization VAEVisualizationCallback ecg_visualization ECGVisualizationCallback generated_samples GeneratedSamplesCallback early_stopping pytorch_lightning.callbacks.EarlyStopping lr_monitor pytorch_lightning.callbacks.LearningRateMonitor model_checkpoint pytorch_lightning.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint

A callback whose constructor takes save_dir gets ${run_dir}/samples if params does not set it. The main ModelCheckpoint is always added by the runner from the checkpoint: section, so model_checkpoint is only for an additional one.

All three visualization callbacks act in on_validation_epoch_end, so they only fire on epochs where validation runs (check_val_every_n_epoch). They save PNGs with matplotlib's Agg backend.

docs.title: VAEVisualizationCallback
docs.text:
Plots real vs reconstructed ECGs for autoencoders (used by vae_mimic.yaml and vqvae_mimic.yaml).

VAEVisualizationCallback(
    save_dir,                  # str | Path, created if missing
    log_every_n_epochs=5,
    num_samples=4,
    plot_all_leads=True,       # True: one subplot per lead; False: all leads overlaid
    log_to_tensorboard=True,
    log_to_wandb=False,
)

Behaviour:

  • Skipped during the sanity check and when current_epoch % log_every_n_epochs != 0.
  • Takes the first batch of trainer.val_dataloaders, reads the signal with ecgen.types.get_signal (an ECGBatch, a {"signal"} / legacy {"ecg_signals"} dict, or an (ecg, features) tuple), and keeps the first num_samples.
  • Reconstructs with pl_module.vae(ecg) if the module has a vae attribute, else pl_module.vqvae(ecg), else pl_module(ecg); the first element of the returned tuple is used.
  • Saves save_dir/epoch_{epoch:04d}.png (150 dpi), logs the figure to TensorBoard under the tag vae_reconstruction and, if enabled, to W&B under vae_reconstruction.

See Visualization for the plot layouts.

docs.title: ECGVisualizationCallback
docs.text:
Plots one real vs one generated ECG for GANs.

ECGVisualizationCallback(save_dir, every_n_epochs=10, n_samples=1)

Reads pl_module._val_real_sample and pl_module._val_fake_sample (set by Pulse2PulseGAN.validation_step) and does nothing if they are missing. Plots up to 8 leads in two columns and saves save_dir/sample_epoch_{epoch:04d}.png; also logs samples/real_vs_fake to any logger whose experiment has a log method (W&B). n_samples is stored but not used.

docs.title: GeneratedSamplesCallback
docs.text:
Periodically generates and saves samples.

GeneratedSamplesCallback(save_dir, every_n_epochs=25, n_samples=16)

Calls pl_module.generate_samples(n_samples) (does nothing if the module lacks that method — only Pulse2PulseGAN has it), saves the tensor to generated_epoch_{epoch:04d}.pt and a plot of the first sample (up to 8 leads) to generated_epoch_{epoch:04d}.png, and logs samples/generated to W&B.

Note

ECGVisualizationCallback and GeneratedSamplesCallback take every_n_epochs, whereas VAEVisualizationCallback takes log_every_n_epochs.

docs.title: Using callbacks
docs.text:
In an experiment YAML (from vae_mimic.yaml):

checkpoint:            # the runner's ModelCheckpoint
  monitor: val_loss
  mode: min
  save_top_k: 3

callbacks:
  - name: early_stopping
    params: {monitor: val_loss, patience: 10, mode: min, verbose: true}
  - name: lr_monitor
    params: {logging_interval: step}
  - name: vae_visualization          # save_dir defaults to ${run_dir}/samples
    params:
      log_every_n_epochs: 5
      num_samples: 4
      log_to_wandb: true

Individual values can be changed from the command line, e.g. ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml callbacks.2.params.log_every_n_epochs=1. The VAE, VQ-VAE and prior log val_loss; Pulse2Pulse checkpoints on val/d_wasserstein (mode: max).

docs.title: Custom callbacks
docs.text:
Subclass pytorch_lightning.Callback:

import pytorch_lightning as pl

class MyCallback(pl.Callback):
    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer, pl_module):
        ...

then reference it from the YAML with target: my_project.callbacks.MyCallback, or register a name for it:

from ecgen.registry import CALLBACKS

CALLBACKS.add("my_callback", MyCallback)   # or @CALLBACKS.register("my_callback") on the class

Shared callbacks belong in src/ecgen/training/callbacks/, registered in its __init__.py.

docs.title: Conditioning
docs.text: Conditional models generate ECGs given something: a label, patient data, ECG measurements, or part of an ECG. Conditioning in ECGEN is separate from the model families: a family that supports it takes a conditioning: block in its model.params, and the same block works for every conditional family.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: Piece Where What it does Condition fields the dataset Each sample carries cond[field] (and cond_missing[field]). MIMIC: measurements (9 machine measurements). Synthetic: measurements (heart rate, amplitude), rhythm (3 classes), labels (3 multi-hot). Field encoders ecgen.conditioning.encoders Turn one field into one slot: a global vector, a sequence of tokens, or a time-aligned dense signal. CompositeConditioner ecgen.conditioning.composite Runs all encoders, sums vectors, concatenates tokens and dense channels, and applies condition dropout. Output: ConditionOutput(vector, tokens, tokens_mask, dense). Injection layers ecgen.nn.injection How a backbone consumes the slots: FiLM, AdaGN, AdaLNZero, AddToTimeEmb (vector), CrossAttention1d (tokens), concat_dense (dense). All start as the identity (zero-initialised). Observation masks ecgen.data.masks For partial-ECG conditioning: data.masks adds an obs_mask to every batch, and the masked_signal encoder conditions on signal * obs_mask.

docs.title: Encoders
docs.text: name Field value Slot Notes categorical class index [B] vector Missing / negative index → learned "unknown" embedding multilabel multi-hot [B, L] vector (or tokens with as_tokens: true) SSSD-ECG-style linear projection; tokens = one per present label numeric normalized values [B, F] + missing mask vector (or tokens) Missingness is an explicit input fourier normalized values [B, F] vector Random Fourier features, for sharp dependence on scalars like heart rate masked_signal reads obs / obs_mask (field name obs) dense [x * mask, mask], optionally projected by a 1×1 conv text_hash strings list[str] tokens (or vector) Hashed bag-of-words embeddings, trained with the model; no dependencies text strings list[str] tokens (or vector) Frozen Hugging Face encoder (model_name, max_length); needs ecgen[text]; weights stay out of the checkpoint, embeddings are cached per distinct text

docs.title: Text conditions
docs.text: Report text is a string field: MIMIC (report: true joins the machine report lines), PTB-XL (report), and the synthetic data (a templated "sinus tachycardia, high voltage"). Strings are collated into lists and encoded into tokens that the backbone attends to (cross-attention in unet1d and dit1d). At sampling time pass one string for all samples or one per sample: sample(n, cond={"report": "Sinus bradycardia"}). An empty string or a missing field uses the null token.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
model:
  name: <a conditional family>
  params:
    conditioning:
      vector_dim: 256          # every vector encoder is projected to this and summed
      token_dim: 256
      encoders:
        - {field: measurements, name: numeric, params: {num_features: 9, dim: 256}}
        - {field: obs, name: masked_signal, params: {num_leads: 12}}
      dropout: {measurements: 0.1}   # per-field drop probability while training

data:
  masks:                        # only needed when an encoder reads `obs`
    name: mixture
    params:
      components:
        - {weight: 0.6, name: lead_subset, params: {keep: [[I], [I, II]]}}
        - {weight: 0.2, name: time_span, params: {min_frac: 0.1, max_frac: 0.5}}
        - {weight: 0.2, name: unobserved}

Mask generators: none (all observed), unobserved, lead_subset (keep lists of lead names, or a random min_leads..max_leads), time_span (imputation), forecast (observe a prefix), random_points, and mixture.

docs.title: Dropout, missing fields, and guidance
docs.text: While training, each field is replaced by a learned null embedding with its dropout probability. A field that is not given at all (at sampling time) uses the same null. So one model can be sampled with any subset of its conditions, and classifier-free guidance compares a pass with the conditions to a pass with drop="all".

docs.title: Checks before training
docs.text:
The runner refuses a config when:

  • the family does not support conditioning (Capabilities.conditional);
  • an encoder produces a slot the family cannot consume (accepts);
  • an encoder's field is not in the dataset's samples;
  • an encoder reads obs but data.masks is not set.

docs.title: Raw values at sampling time
docs.text:
Training data statistics travel with the checkpoint (data_info: lead names, sampling rate, length, and a normalizer per numeric field). At sampling time, pass numeric fields in their raw units and the model normalizes them:

model = SomeFamily.load_from_checkpoint("runs/.../last.ckpt")
x = model.sample(8, cond={"measurements": [75.0, 1.2]})   # heart rate, amplitude
x = model.sample(8, cond={})                               # unconditional (null embeddings)

Use NaN (or None) for an unknown value inside a numeric field.

docs.title: Conditional families
docs.text:
Family accepts How conditions enter Extras vae (CVAE) vector, dense FiLM after every encoder/decoder residual block; dense concatenated to the encoder input and (pooled) to the decoder input learned_prior: true → p(z \| c); latent_type: global → one latent vector per ECG, whose prior samples decode to coherent ECGs (spatial latents reconstruct well but their prior samples do not); recon_on: unobserved for imputation pulse2pulse (cGAN) vector, dense Generator: FiLM on every decoder stage, dense concatenated to the input noise. Critic: projection head for vectors, dense concatenated to its input (paired / pix2pix critic) l1_weight (e.g. 100) + l1_on: unobserved for lead reconstruction; the critic has its own conditioner copy (no dropout) vqvae_prior (conditional PixelCNN) vector, dense Condition added to both gate pre-activations of every causal block (V_f h, V_g h); dense pooled to code resolution sample(..., guidance=w) = classifier-free guidance on the logits; the stage-1 VQ-VAE stays unconditional diffusion (and flow_matching) vector, tokens, dense Vector added to the time embedding (→ AdaGN in every block), tokens by cross-attention at the attention levels, dense concatenated to the input sample(guidance=w) = CFG; loss_on: unobserved + clean_observed for SSSD-style imputation; training-free inpaint="replace" or "repaint"

All three keep their original parameters when conditioning is absent, so unconditional checkpoints load unchanged. Conditional models paste_observed the given part of obs into their output by default.

Example configs: configs/experiments/cvae_mimic.yaml, pulse2pulse_lead_reconstruction.yaml, prior_mimic_conditional.yaml.

docs.title: Checking condition adherence
docs.text:
scripts/evaluate/condition_adherence.py samples a model at a grid of requested heart rates and measures the heart rate of the output (ecgen.evaluation.measure.heart_rate, R-peak detection; method="neurokit" uses NeuroKit2):

python scripts/evaluate/condition_adherence.py runs/cvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt \
    --family vae --target rr_interval --rates 50,70,90,110,130

It reports MAE and Pearson r between requested and measured rates; an unconditional checkpoint gives the baseline (r ≈ 0).

docs.title: Training Guide
docs.text: General workflow for training models in ECGEN. Model-specific pages: VAE, VQ-VAE, Pulse2Pulse.

docs.title: 1. Get the data
docs.text:
Training reads raw MIMIC-IV-ECG directly (WFDB records + machine_measurements.csv); there is no preprocessing step. See MIMIC-IV-ECG.

Note

scripts/data/prepare_mimic.py and scripts/data/validate_dataset.py are placeholders that only print a message.

docs.title: 2. Configure an experiment
docs.text:
Copy and edit an experiment file in configs/experiments/:

# configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml (excerpt)
experiment:
  name: my_vae
  seed: 42
  runs_root: runs

model:
  name: vae
  params:
    in_channels: 12
    base_channels: 64
    latent_channels: 8
    kl_weight: 0.0001

data:
  dataset:
    name: mimic_iv_ecg
    params:
      root: /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg
      max_samples: 1000      # null for the full dataset
  batch_size: 32

trainer:
  max_epochs: 100
  accelerator: gpu
  devices: [0]

Every section is read by the same runner; see Training with ecgen train for the full schema and Configuration for the per-family params.

docs.title: 3. Train
docs.text:
ecgen train configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml trainer.max_epochs=5     # overrides win over the YAML
ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml                     # VQ-VAE stage 1
ecgen train configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=<vqvae.ckpt>   # stage 2

The scripts/shell/run_train_*.sh wrappers call the same command; see Training entry points.

docs.title: Callbacks — ecgen.training.callbacks
docs.text:
• visualization.py: VAEVisualizationCallback, ECGVisualizationCallback, GeneratedSamplesCallback
  • checkpointing.py, logging.py: empty placeholder classes (CustomCheckpointCallback, CustomLoggingCallback)

The runner always adds a ModelCheckpoint built from the checkpoint: section; the other callbacks, including Lightning's early_stopping and lr_monitor, are listed by name in callbacks:. See Callbacks.

docs.title: Losses
docs.text:
Each family keeps its loss next to its model:

Module Functions ecgen.families.vae.losses vae_loss ecgen.families.vqvae.losses vqvae_loss, prior_loss ecgen.families.gan.losses wgan_discriminator_loss, wgan_generator_loss, adversarial_loss, least_squares_discriminator_loss, least_squares_generator_loss training/losses/common.py mse_loss, l1_loss

The old training/losses/{vae,vqvae,gan}_losses.py re-exports were removed in 1.2.

docs.title: Metrics — training/metrics/
docs.text:
File Functions reconstruction.py reconstruction_mse, reconstruction_mae generation.py signal_to_noise_ratio clinical.py wasserstein_distance, gradient_penalty_loss

Evaluation metrics for generated samples live in the separate evaluation/ package; see Evaluation metrics.

docs.title: TensorBoard
docs.text:
Every run logs to runs/<exp_name>/seed_<seed>/tb/:

tensorboard --logdir runs/                          # all runs
tensorboard --logdir runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/tb      # one run

docs.title: Weights & Biases
docs.text:
Enable it in the experiment YAML (the runner creates the WandbLogger for you):

wandb:
  enabled: true
  project: ecg-vae
  entity: null
  run_name: null   # defaults to <exp_name>_seed<seed>
  tags: [vae]

or on the command line with wandb.enabled=true wandb.project=<name>.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The runner calls ecgen.utils.seed.set_global_seed(experiment.seed); the shipped configs also set trainer.deterministic: true. The MIMIC-IV-ECG split is done at the subject level and seeded by the dataset's own seed parameter (default 42). Each run writes config_resolved.yaml and metadata.json (command, package versions, git info) next to its checkpoints.

docs.title: Practical advice
docs.text:
1. Start small: set data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000 and a few epochs to check the pipeline, or use data.dataset.name=synthetic with no data at all (see Smoke runs).
  2. Watch the plots: the reconstruction images in samples/ reveal problems before the loss does.
  3. Mind check_val_every_n_epoch: checkpointing, early stopping and visualization all run after validation. Validation runs on 0-based epochs 4, 9, 14, ... when it is set to 5; with log_every_n_epochs: 5 on vae_visualization as well (the vae_mimic.yaml defaults) no reconstruction plot is ever produced — see Visualization.

docs.title: Out of memory
docs.text:
• Reduce batch_size
  • Reduce model width/depth (base_channels, num_res_blocks)

docs.title: Slow training
docs.text:
• Increase num_workers
  • Use data.dataset.params.skip_missing_check: true once the dataset is known to be complete

docs.title: Pulse2Pulse Training
docs.text:
This page covers training the Pulse2Pulse GAN on MIMIC-IV-ECG and generating samples from a trained checkpoint. Training runs through the shared runner, ecgen train (see Training with ecgen train).

File Role configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml Experiment config (model.name: pulse2pulse) scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_mimic.sh python -m ecgen train <config> [overrides] scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_standalone.sh Same, with settings from environment variables scripts/generate/generate_pulse2pulse.py Sample generation and plotting from a checkpoint configs/model/gan/pulse2pulse.yaml Model fragment (not read by anything)

docs.title: Option A: ecgen train (or its wrapper)
docs.text:
ecgen train configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml \
    data.dataset.params.root=/data/mimic-iv-ecg data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000 \
    trainer.max_epochs=5 wandb.enabled=false

./scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_mimic.sh [config] [overrides]   # default configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml

docs.title: Option B: environment-variable wrapper
docs.text:
DATA_DIR=/data/mimic-iv-ecg BATCH_SIZE=64 GPU_ID=1 \
    ./scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_standalone.sh

The wrapper cds to the repo root and runs pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml with these overrides:

Variable Default Override DATA_DIR /work/vajira/DATA/SEARCH/MIMIC_IV_ECG_raw_v1/mimic-iv-ecg-diagnostic-electrocardiogram-matched-subset-1.0 data.dataset.params.root EXP_NAME pulse2pulse_mimic experiment.name BATCH_SIZE 128 data.batch_size MAX_EPOCHS 300 trainer.max_epochs GPU_ID 0 trainer.devices=[GPU_ID] NUM_WORKERS 4 data.num_workers

It also always sets data.dataset.params.max_samples=null (full dataset), data.dataset.params.skip_missing_check=true and wandb.enabled=false; further key=value arguments are appended and win.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml:

Section Values model name: pulse2pulse; Pulse2PulseConfig fields model_size: 50, num_channels: 8, seq_length: 5000 (multiple of 2500), lr: 1e-4, b1: 0.5, b2: 0.9, lmbda: 10.0 (gradient-penalty weight), n_critic: 5 data.dataset mimic_iv_ecg with leads: independent8 (I, II, V1–V6), seq_length: 5000, scale: zscore, max_samples: 10000 data batch_size: 128, num_workers: 4, split_params: {val: {max_samples: 1000}} (caps validation at 1000 records) checkpoint monitor: val/d_wasserstein, mode: max, save_top_k: 3 callbacks ecg_visualization (every_n_epochs: 10), generated_samples (every_n_epochs: 25, n_samples: 16) trainer max_epochs: 300, devices: [0], check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, log_every_n_steps: 50 wandb enabled: true, project: ecg-pulse2pulse

model.params.num_channels must equal the number of selected leads; the runner's compatibility check stops the run otherwise.

configs/model/gan/pulse2pulse.yaml (latent_dim: 100, base_channels: 64, lr_g/lr_d: 0.0002, b2: 0.999) does not match Pulse2PulseConfig and nothing reads it.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Batches come from the generic ECGDataModule over MIMICIVECG (see MIMIC-IV-ECG): train and val splits from the dataset's seeded, subject-level split, each record (8, 5000), z-scored per record over the selected leads. Pulse2PulseGAN reads batch.signal and ignores the measurement conditions.

Changed lead set

The leads are now I, II, V1–V6 (leads: independent8), which match the CSV columns that ecgen.generate writes. The removed scripts/train/train_pulse2pulse.py fed the first 8 leads in file order (I, II, III, aVR, aVF, aVL, V1, V2) and z-scored all 12 leads before dropping 4. Models trained that way have a different lead layout from new ones.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
runs/<exp-name>/seed_<seed>/
├── checkpoints/
│   ├── epoch{EEE}-step{SSSSSS}.ckpt   # top-3 by val/d_wasserstein (mode="max")
│   └── last.ckpt
├── samples/
│   ├── sample_epoch_NNNN.png          # ECGVisualizationCallback: real vs fake, first sample
│   ├── generated_epoch_NNNN.pt        # GeneratedSamplesCallback: (16, C, L) tensor
│   └── generated_epoch_NNNN.png
├── metrics/train_val_metrics.json
├── tb/                                # TensorBoard logs
├── config_resolved.yaml
├── metadata.json
└── wandb/                             # only with wandb.enabled

Sample callbacks rarely fire with the default schedule

Both callbacks run in on_validation_epoch_end and only act when trainer.current_epoch % every_n_epochs == 0. With check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, validation runs at current_epoch 4, 9, 14, … These values are never multiples of 10 or 25, so in practice the callbacks only write files during the sanity-check validation at epoch 0 (verified with Lightning 2.0). To get periodic plots, use values that line up, e.g. trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch=1, or pick every_n_epochs so that current_epoch + 1 is a multiple of the validation interval.

For the meaning of the logged train/* and val/* metrics, see Pulse2Pulse GAN → Logged metrics.

docs.title: Generating samples
docs.text:
python scripts/generate/generate_pulse2pulse.py \
    --checkpoint runs/pulse2pulse_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt \
    --output-dir generated_samples \
    --n-samples 16 \
    --save-tensors
Flag Default Description --checkpoint required Lightning checkpoint --output-dir generated_samples Created if missing --n-samples 16 Number of ECGs to generate --device cuda:0 Falls back to CPU if CUDA is unavailable --seed 42 torch.manual_seed --save-tensors off Also save generated_samples.pt

The script writes:

  • generated_grid.png: a 4-column grid with all leads overlaid per sample
  • generated_sample_0_detailed.png: one subplot per lead for sample 0
  • generated_sample_{0..3}.png: per-lead plots for the first min(n_samples, 4) samples
  • generated_samples.pt: a (n_samples, C, L) CPU tensor, only with --save-tensors

The script loads the model with Pulse2PulseGAN.load_from_checkpoint(args.checkpoint, map_location=device) and needs no extra arguments; see Pulse2Pulse GAN → Loading a checkpoint.

docs.title: Setup check
docs.text:
scripts/utils/test_pulse2pulse_setup.py instantiates the model, the legacy data config (ecgen.data.pulse2pulse_mimic), callbacks, losses and metrics from the ecgen package as a quick smoke test:

python scripts/utils/test_pulse2pulse_setup.py

For an end-to-end check without data, train for one epoch on synthetic ECGs:

ecgen train configs/experiments/pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml data.dataset.name=synthetic \
    'data.dataset.params={num_samples: 64, leads: independent8}' data.split_params={} \
    trainer.max_epochs=1 trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch=1 \
    trainer.accelerator=cpu trainer.devices=1 wandb.enabled=false
