docs.title: Training with ecgen train
docs.text: Every model family is trained by one YAML-driven runner, ecgen.training.runner, exposed as the ecgen command. There are no per-model training scripts: the experiment YAML says which family, dataset and callbacks to build.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
pip install -e .        # installs the `ecgen` console script

ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml trainer.max_epochs=5 data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml --resume runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml --print-config     # show the resolved config, do not train
ecgen list                                                         # registered families, datasets, callbacks

python -m ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml          # same as `ecgen train`
Argument Meaning config Experiment YAML (configs/experiments/*.yaml). dotted.key=value ... Overrides, applied after the YAML, so they always win. --resume <ckpt> Resume from a checkpoint (same as the override resume=<ckpt>). --print-config Print the resolved config (defaults filled, ${...} interpolated) and exit.

The shell wrappers in scripts/shell/ are thin conveniences around the same command; extra arguments are passed through as overrides:

Wrapper Runs run_train_vae_mimic_config.sh [config] [overrides] python -m ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml ... run_train_vqvae_mimic.sh [config] [overrides] VQ-VAE stage 1 (vqvae_mimic.yaml) run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh <stage1.ckpt> [config] [overrides] prior (prior_mimic.yaml) with model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=<stage1.ckpt> run_train_pulse2pulse_mimic.sh [config] [overrides] Pulse2Pulse (pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml) run_train_pulse2pulse_standalone.sh Pulse2Pulse with settings from env vars (DATA_DIR, EXP_NAME, BATCH_SIZE, MAX_EPOCHS, GPU_ID, NUM_WORKERS) run_sweep.sh [overrides] every config in configs/experiments/, then the prior on runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt if it exists

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Each override is dotted.key=value; the value is parsed as YAML (1e-3 is read as a float). Integer path components index into lists.

ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml \
    model.params.lr=1e-3 \
    trainer.devices=[1] \
    wandb.enabled=false \
    callbacks.2.params.num_samples=2 \
    data.dataset.params.max_samples=null

docs.title: Config schema
docs.text:
The runner accepts exactly these top-level sections; any other key (for example the old visualization: section) is rejected with an error.

experiment:
  name: vae_mimic            # run directory: <runs_root>/<name>/seed_<seed>/
  seed: 42                   # global seed (default 42)
  runs_root: runs            # default "runs"

model:
  name: vae                  # registry name: vae | vqvae | vqvae_prior | pulse2pulse
  # target: my_pkg.models.MyModel   # ...or an import path instead of `name`
  params:                    # the family's config dataclass fields, flat
    in_channels: 12          # must match the dataset's lead count
    base_channels: 64
    latent_channels: 8
    channel_multipliers: [1, 2, 4, 4]
    num_res_blocks: 2
    lr: 0.0001
    kl_weight: 0.0001
    # legacy form `params: {config: {...}}` is still accepted

data:                        # -> ecgen.data.datamodule.ECGDataModule
  dataset:
    name: mimic_iv_ecg       # registry name: mimic_iv_ecg | synthetic (or `target:`)
    params:                  # dataset constructor args; `split` is filled in per split
      root: /path/to/mimic-iv-ecg
      max_samples: 1000      # null = full split
      leads: null            # null = 12 leads in file order; "independent8"; or a list of names
      seq_length: 5000
      scale: zscore          # per-record z-score; "none" = mV; or a number
  batch_size: 32
  num_workers: 4
  pin_memory: null           # default: torch.cuda.is_available()
  split_params:              # per-split overrides of dataset.params
    val: {max_samples: 1000}

checkpoint:                  # -> ModelCheckpoint (defaults shown)
  monitor: val_loss
  mode: min
  save_top_k: 1
  save_last: true
  filename: "epoch{epoch:03d}-step{step:06d}"

callbacks:                   # built in order, after the checkpoint callback
  - name: early_stopping
    params: {monitor: val_loss, patience: 10, mode: min}
  - name: lr_monitor
    params: {logging_interval: step}
  - name: vae_visualization  # save_dir defaults to ${run_dir}/samples
    params: {log_every_n_epochs: 5, num_samples: 4}

trainer:                     # passed to pl.Trainer as keyword arguments
  max_epochs: 100
  accelerator: gpu
  devices: [0]
  check_val_every_n_epoch: 5
  gradient_clip_val: 1.0

wandb:                       # optional; TensorBoard is always on
  enabled: false
  project: ecg-vae
  entity: null
  run_name: null             # default <name>_seed<seed>
  tags: []
  notes: ""
  log_model: false

resume: null                 # checkpoint to resume from (or --resume)

model and data are required; everything else has defaults. String values anywhere in the config may use ${run_dir}, ${name} and ${seed}, for example callbacks: [{name: generated_samples, params: {save_dir: "${run_dir}/gen"}}].

The shipped configs are the reference examples: vae_mimic.yaml, vqvae_mimic.yaml, prior_mimic.yaml, pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml.

docs.title: Registry names
docs.text:
ecgen list prints the current registries. Built in:

Kind Name Class family vae ecgen.families.vae.VAELightning family vqvae ecgen.families.vqvae.VQVAELightning family vqvae_prior ecgen.families.vqvae.PriorLightning family pulse2pulse ecgen.families.gan.Pulse2PulseGAN dataset mimic_iv_ecg ecgen.data.datasets.MIMICIVECG dataset synthetic ecgen.data.datasets.SyntheticECG callback vae_visualization VAEVisualizationCallback (reconstruction plots; VAE and VQ-VAE) callback ecg_visualization ECGVisualizationCallback (real vs generated; Pulse2Pulse) callback generated_samples GeneratedSamplesCallback (periodic sample grids; Pulse2Pulse) callback early_stopping pytorch_lightning.callbacks.EarlyStopping callback lr_monitor pytorch_lightning.callbacks.LearningRateMonitor callback model_checkpoint pytorch_lightning.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint (an extra one; the runner always adds its own from checkpoint:)

A callback whose constructor takes save_dir and does not get one writes to ${run_dir}/samples. See Callbacks for their parameters.

docs.title: Run directory
docs.text:
runs/<experiment.name>/seed_<seed>/
├── config_resolved.yaml         # config after overrides, defaults and ${...} interpolation
├── metadata.json                # command, config path, Python/package versions, git info
├── checkpoints/
│   ├── epoch###-step######.ckpt # top-k by checkpoint.monitor
│   └── last.ckpt
├── samples/                     # visualization callback output
├── metrics/
│   └── train_val_metrics.json   # final callback/logged metrics and best_model_path
├── tb/version_N/                # TensorBoard logs
└── wandb/                       # only when wandb.enabled

There is no best.ckpt; the best path is recorded in metrics/train_val_metrics.json. Each checkpoint also stores the datamodule state under the ECGDataModule key: lead_names, fs, seq_length and the train split's feature_normalizer.

docs.title: Compatibility check
docs.text:
After building the model and the train/val datasets, and before training starts, the runner compares the model's channel count (in_channels / num_channels) and seq_length (where the config declares one) with the dataset's leads and length. A mismatch fails immediately, e.g.:

ValueError: Model expects 12 channels but the dataset yields 8 leads ['I', 'II', 'V1', ...];
set data.dataset.params.leads or the model's channel count

For the prior, the check uses the frozen stage-1 VQ-VAE's input.

docs.title: Two-stage VQ-VAE
docs.text:
# Stage 1: VQ-VAE
ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml

# Stage 2: PixelCNN prior over the frozen stage-1 codes
ecgen train configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml \
    model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt
# or
./scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt

model.params.num_embeddings and the dataset's leads / seq_length in prior_mimic.yaml must match the stage-1 run. See VQ-VAE training.

docs.title: Smoke runs without data
docs.text:
The synthetic dataset generates deterministic ECG-like signals, so a config can be tested without MIMIC-IV-ECG:

ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml \
    data.dataset.name=synthetic \
    'data.dataset.params={num_samples: 64, seq_length: 5000}' \
    data.batch_size=8 data.num_workers=0 \
    trainer.max_epochs=1 trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch=1 \
    trainer.accelerator=cpu trainer.devices=1 \
    wandb.enabled=false experiment.name=smoke

Keep trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch no larger than trainer.max_epochs: checkpoints monitor val_loss, so a run that never validates writes no checkpoint at all.

SyntheticECG takes split, num_samples, leads, seq_length, fs, scale and seed, so the MIMIC-specific params (e.g. root) must be replaced rather than merged, as above.

docs.title: Extending: new families, datasets and callbacks
docs.text:
Components are looked up in three registries in ecgen.registry: FAMILIES, DATASETS and CALLBACKS. A spec is either {name: <registered>, params: {...}} or {target: <import.path.Class>, params: {...}}.

Without registering — point target at any importable class:

model:
  target: my_project.models.MyModel
  params: {in_channels: 12, lr: 1e-4}
data:
  dataset:
    target: my_project.data.MyDataset
    params: {root: /data/mine}
callbacks:
  - target: my_project.callbacks.MyCallback
    params: {every_n_epochs: 5}

Registering a name (in library code, or in a module that is imported before training):

from ecgen.families.base import GenerativeModule
from ecgen.registry import FAMILIES

@FAMILIES.register("my_model")
class MyModel(GenerativeModule):
    def __init__(self, config=None, **kwargs):
        ...

Built-in names come from ecgen.registry.load_builtins(), which imports ecgen.families, ecgen.data.datasets and ecgen.training.callbacks. A family should:

  • subclass GenerativeModule, take config=None, **kwargs and resolve them with ecgen.utils.config.resolve_config, so load_from_checkpoint(path) works;
  • read batches with self.get_signal(batch) — batches are ECGBatch objects (signal [B, C, T], lead_names, fs, cond, cond_missing, meta); get_signal also accepts the legacy dict and tuple formats;
  • expose config.in_channels (or num_channels) and, if fixed, config.seq_length so the compatibility check can run;
  • implement sample(n_samples, ...) returning [n, C, T].

For datasets see Adding a Dataset.

docs.title: Sampling with ecgen sample
docs.text:
Every checkpoint written by ecgen train records its family and the training data contract (lead names, sampling rate, length, scaling, condition normalizers), so one call samples any model:

import ecgen

x = ecgen.sample("runs/diffusion_mimic_conditional/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", 16,
                 cond={"measurements": [800, 40, 128, 170, 258, 520, 60, 30, 40]},  # raw units
                 guidance=2.0, steps=50, seed=0,
                 output_dir="samples/", format="csv", plot=2)
# x: [16, 12, 5000] float32

ecgen sample runs/.../last.ckpt -n 16 -o samples/ --format csv \
    --cond measurements=800,40,128,170,258,520,60,30,40 --guidance 2 --steps 50 --seed 0 --plot 2
ecgen sample runs/.../last.ckpt -n 8 --cond report="Sinus tachycardia" --format wfdb
Argument Meaning cond Raw condition values: numeric fields in their original units (NaN = unknown), class indices, multi-hot vectors, strings for text fields. A value with a leading dimension of n (an [n, F] array, n class indices, n strings) gives one condition per sample; anything else is used for all samples. Fields left out use the model's null embedding. obs, obs_mask Partially observed ECGs and masks (1 = observed), e.g. only lead I, for lead reconstruction / imputation guidance Classifier-free guidance scale (conditional diffusion, flow matching, PixelCNN prior) steps Sampling steps (diffusion / flow) seed Reproducible sampling derive_12 Complete the 8 independent leads (I, II, V1–V6) to the standard 12 (Einthoven / Goldberger) output_dir, format npy (one array), csv (one file per ECG, lead-name header), wfdb (.hea/.dat), or None; samples.json records leads, fs, units, conditions plot Render the first N samples as interactive HTML (ecgen.plot_ecg) family Registry name, only for checkpoints that predate family recording

Other keyword arguments go to the model's sample() (e.g. eta, solver, inpaint="repaint", temperature). Units are mV for data trained with scale: none; z-scored models output normalized units (NU).

ecgen.load_model(checkpoint) returns the model itself, and hf://<repo>/<path> checkpoints are downloaded as for ecgen.generate. ecgen.generate (the original Pulse2Pulse .pt loader) is unchanged.

docs.title: Training Entry Points
docs.text:
All families are trained by one runner, ecgen train <config.yaml> (see Training with ecgen train). The per-model scripts scripts/train/train_{vae_mimic,vqvae_mimic,prior_mimic,pulse2pulse}.py and their script-local DataModules were removed.

Entry point What it runs ecgen train <config> [key=value ...] / python -m ecgen train ... The runner, for any family scripts/shell/run_train_vae_mimic_config.sh [config] [overrides] VAE (vae_mimic.yaml) scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_mimic.sh [config] [overrides] VQ-VAE stage 1 (vqvae_mimic.yaml) scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh <vqvae_ckpt> [config] [overrides] PixelCNN prior (prior_mimic.yaml, model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=<vqvae_ckpt>) scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_mimic.sh [config] [overrides] Pulse2Pulse (pulse2pulse_mimic.yaml) scripts/shell/run_train_pulse2pulse_standalone.sh Pulse2Pulse, settings from env vars DATA_DIR, EXP_NAME, BATCH_SIZE, MAX_EPOCHS, GPU_ID, NUM_WORKERS scripts/shell/run_sweep.sh [overrides] Every configs/experiments/*.yaml except the prior, then the prior on runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt if it exists python -m ecgen.training.train --config <yaml> Deprecated wrapper that calls the runner single_file/run_train_vqvae.sh → single_file/train_vqvae_standalone.py --stage {1,2} Self-contained VQ-VAE (both stages), flags/env vars only, no package imports

All wrappers in scripts/shell/ first cd to the repository root, so they can be run from anywhere, and pass extra arguments through to ecgen train as overrides. Overrides are applied after the YAML, so the command line always wins.

scripts/train/train_template.py now only points at the runner: to add a model, register a family and write a config instead of a new script (see Extending).

docs.title: Standalone VQ-VAE
docs.text: single_file/train_vqvae_standalone.py re-implements the VQ-VAE, prior, dataset and training loop in one file and is independent of ecgen.families.vqvae. See Standalone VQ-VAE.

docs.title: VAE Training
docs.text: The VAE is trained on MIMIC-IV-ECG by the shared runner, ecgen train, with configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml. See Training with ecgen train for the config schema and overrides.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• pip install -e . (see Installation)
  • MIMIC-IV-ECG on disk, laid out as described in MIMIC-IV-ECG (machine_measurements.csv plus files/p<XXXX>/p<subject_id>/s<study_id>/<study_id>.hea/.dat), with data.dataset.params.root pointing at it

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
CLIShell wrapperPython 
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml \
    data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000 trainer.max_epochs=10 wandb.enabled=false

./scripts/shell/run_train_vae_mimic_config.sh                         # configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml
./scripts/shell/run_train_vae_mimic_config.sh configs/experiments/my_vae.yaml trainer.max_epochs=10

The wrapper cds to the repo root and runs python -m ecgen train <config> [overrides].

from ecgen.training.runner import train_from_file

train_from_file("configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml", ["trainer.max_epochs=10"])

Overrides are applied after the YAML, so they always win.

docs.title: What the runner builds
docs.text:
• Model: model.name: vae → ecgen.families.vae.VAELightning, with model.params as the flat VAEConfig fields (in_channels, base_channels, latent_channels, channel_multipliers, num_res_blocks, lr, kl_weight, b1, b2). Adam (lr, b1, b2), no scheduler.
  • Data: ECGDataModule over MIMICIVECG (data.dataset.name: mimic_iv_ecg) for the train / val splits; subject-level split with val_split, test_split, seed; max_samples caps each split. Batches are ECGBatch objects; the VAE reads batch.signal [B, 12, 5000].
  • Callbacks: ModelCheckpoint from checkpoint: (top-3 on val_loss, plus last.ckpt), then the YAML list: early_stopping (patience 10), lr_monitor, vae_visualization.
  • Loggers: TensorBoard always; W&B when wandb.enabled (the shipped config enables it).

Logged metrics: train/{total,recon,kl}_loss, val/{total,recon,kl}_loss, val_loss.

docs.title: Common settings
docs.text:
Setting Key (override form) vae_mimic.yaml Data directory data.dataset.params.root cluster path Records per split data.dataset.params.max_samples 10000 (null = all) Skip file check data.dataset.params.skip_missing_check false Leads data.dataset.params.leads null (12, file order) Batch size / workers data.batch_size / data.num_workers 32 / 4 Width / latent model.params.base_channels / model.params.latent_channels 64 / 8 KL weight model.params.kl_weight 0.0001 Learning rate model.params.lr 0.0001 Epochs trainer.max_epochs 100 GPUs trainer.devices [0] Validation interval trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch 5 Early stopping patience callbacks.0.params.patience 10 Top-k checkpoints checkpoint.save_top_k 3 Plot interval callbacks.2.params.log_every_n_epochs 5 W&B wandb.enabled / wandb.project true / ecg-vae Resume --resume <ckpt> or resume=<ckpt> null

No reconstruction plots with the shipped config

Lightning validates on 0-based epochs 4, 9, 14, ... when check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, while VAEVisualizationCallback only plots when epoch % log_every_n_epochs == 0. With both set to 5 (as in vae_mimic.yaml) the callback never fires. Set callbacks.2.params.log_every_n_epochs=1.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Smaller, faster model
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml \
    model.params.base_channels=32 data.batch_size=64 trainer.max_epochs=50

# Multiple GPUs
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml 'trainer.devices=[0, 1]'

# Resume
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml --resume runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt

# No data: smoke-test the pipeline on synthetic ECGs
ecgen train configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml data.dataset.name=synthetic \
    'data.dataset.params={num_samples: 64}' trainer.max_epochs=1 trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch=1 \
    trainer.accelerator=cpu trainer.devices=1 wandb.enabled=false

├── config_resolved.yaml

│   └── last.ckpt

docs.title: Using a trained model
docs.text:
from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning

model = VAELightning.load_from_checkpoint("runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu")
model.eval()

samples = model.sample(n_samples=16, seq_length=5000)   # generate
recon = model.reconstruct(ecg_batch)                     # (B, 12, 5000) -> (B, 12, 5000)
latent = model.vae.encode_to_latent(ecg_batch)           # (B, 8, 625)

Note

scripts/generate/generate_vae.py is a stub that only prints a message; use the snippet above to generate samples.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ecgen' / ecgen: command not found pip install -e . FileNotFoundError: machine_measurements.csv not found at ... data.dataset.params.root must point at the directory containing machine_measurements.csv and files/ ValueError: Unknown config sections: ['visualization'] Old-style config; move the plot settings to a vae_visualization entry under callbacks: ValueError: Model expects 12 channels but the dataset yields ... model.params.in_channels must equal the number of selected leads wandb not installed; continuing without it The run continues with TensorBoard only; pip install wandb and log in, or set wandb.enabled=false CUDA out of memory Lower batch_size, base_channels or num_res_blocks Slow start-up The missing-file check stats every record; set data.dataset.params.skip_missing_check=true once the data is known to be complete Blurry reconstructions Lower kl_weight, or increase model capacity KL collapses to ~0 / samples are poor Raise kl_weight

docs.title: VQ-VAE Training
docs.text:
The VQ-VAE is trained in two separate runs:

Stage What is trained model.name Shell wrapper Experiment config 1 VQVAELightning (encoder, codebook, decoder) vqvae scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_mimic.sh configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml 2 PriorLightning (PixelCNN over code indices; VQ-VAE frozen) vqvae_prior scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml

Both stages run through ecgen train (see Training with ecgen train). Stage 2 needs a stage-1 checkpoint. Both stages train on MIMIC-IV-ECG. See MIMIC-IV-ECG for the dataset.

PriorLightning loads the stage-1 model with a plain VQVAELightning.load_from_checkpoint(path) and records its config in the prior's hyperparameters, so a finished prior checkpoint can be restored on its own with PriorLightning.load_from_checkpoint(path). See Loading checkpoints.

Old stage-2 checkpoints must be retrained

The PixelCNN prior was rewritten as a stack of causal dilated CausalGatedBlocks (default receptive field 1024 codes). Prior checkpoints from the earlier mask-A/B architecture have different state_dict keys and do not load into the current PriorLightning, so rerun stage 2. Stage-1 VQ-## Quick start

# Stage 1: VQ-VAE
ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml
#   or: ./scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_mimic.sh [config] [overrides]

# Find a real checkpoint (there is no best.ckpt, see "Checkpoint names" below)
ls runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/

# Stage 2: PixelCNN prior on the frozen stage-1 model
ecgen train configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml \
    model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt
#   or: ./scripts/shell/run_train_vqvae_prior_mimic.sh runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt [config] [overrides]

The wrappers cd to the repository root first, so relative paths resolve against the repo root, and pass any extra key=value arguments to ecgen train. The stage-2 wrapper exits early if the checkpoint file does not exist, and otherwise adds model.params.vqvae_checkpoint=<checkpoint>.

Command-line overrides are applied after the YAML, so they always win, e.g. ecgen train configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml trainer.max_epochs=5 data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000.

docs.title: configs/experiments/vqvae_mimic.yaml (stage 1)
docs.text:
Section Notable values experiment name: vqvae_mimic, seed: 42, runs_root: runs wandb enabled: true, project: ecg-vqvae model name: vqvae; params = the VQVAEConfig defaults: 64/64 channels, channel_multipliers: [1, 2, 4, 4], 2 res blocks, 512 codes, β = 0.25, lr 1e-4 data dataset: mimic_iv_ecg with root (hard-coded cluster path), max_samples: 1000, leads: null (12), seq_length: 5000, scale: zscore; batch_size: 32, num_workers: 4 checkpoint monitor: val_loss, save_top_k: 3 callbacks early_stopping (patience 10), lr_monitor, vae_visualization (log_every_n_epochs: 1, num_samples: 4, log_to_wandb: true) trainer max_epochs: 100, devices: [0], check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, gradient_clip_val: 1.0

Note

The checked-in stage-1 config has max_samples: 1000, a smoke-test setting. For a full run, pass data.dataset.params.max_samples=null.

docs.title: configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml (stage 2)
docs.text:
Section Notable values experiment name: prior_mimic, seed: 42 wandb enabled: false, project: ecg-vqvae-prior model name: vqvae_prior; num_embeddings: 512, hidden_dim: 128, num_layers: 10, kernel_size: 2, dilation_cycle: 10, lr: 0.001, vqvae_checkpoint: runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt data Same dataset path and leads/seq_length/scale; max_samples: 10000 callbacks early_stopping, lr_monitor (no visualization) trainer Same as stage 1

Keep the dataset params (path, splits, seed, leads, seq_length, scale) the same in both stages, so the prior trains on codes from the same train split and the input matches what the VQ-VAE was trained on. The runner's compatibility check compares the dataset with the frozen VQ-VAE's in_channels.

docs.title: configs/model/vqvae/
docs.text: vqvae_1d_base.yaml and prior_base.yaml are reference fragments that list the VQVAEConfig / PriorConfig defaults under a top-level model: key. The runner does not load them. Change hyperparameters in model.params of the experiment YAML or with overrides such as model.params.num_embeddings=1024.

docs.title: Choosing the VQ-VAE checkpoint
docs.text:
The stage-1 checkpoint is model.params.vqvae_checkpoint: the value in prior_mimic.yaml, unless an override (or the stage-2 wrapper's argument) replaces it. PriorLightning raises FileNotFoundError: VQ-VAE checkpoint not found: <path> if the file does not exist. With the default YAML you can run ecgen train configs/experiments/prior_mimic.yaml without an override once stage 1 has written last.ckpt.

Stage 1 never writes a best.ckpt (see below), so point at last.ckpt or one of the epoch###-step######.ckpt files. The best path is recorded in runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/metrics/train_val_metrics.json (best_model_path).

docs.title: Checkpoint names
docs.text:
The runner builds ModelCheckpoint from the checkpoint: section:

ModelCheckpoint(
    dirpath=runs/<exp_name>/seed_<seed>/checkpoints,
    filename="epoch{epoch:03d}-step{step:06d}",
    save_last=True, save_top_k=3, monitor="val_loss", mode="min",
    auto_insert_metric_name=False,
)

This produces files such as epoch049-step001600.ckpt and last.ckpt. If you rerun into the same directory, Lightning keeps the existing files and adds a version suffix to the new ones, e.g. last-v1.ckpt or epoch014-step000480-v2.ckpt. In that case last.ckpt may come from an older run, so check timestamps, change experiment.seed/name, or clear the directory.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Each run writes to <runs_root>/<exp_name>/seed_<seed>/:

runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/
├── config_resolved.yaml
├── metadata.json
├── checkpoints/        # epoch###-step######.ckpt (top-k by val_loss) + last.ckpt
├── samples/            # stage 1: epoch_XXXX.png real-vs-reconstruction plots
├── metrics/train_val_metrics.json
├── tb/version_N/       # TensorBoard logs (always on)
└── wandb/              # W&B run files (if enabled)

The stage-2 run directory (runs/prior_mimic/seed_42/) has the same layout; its samples/ stays empty.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
TensorBoard is always enabled:

tensorboard --logdir runs/vqvae_mimic/seed_42/tb

Weights & Biases is enabled by wandb.enabled: true (stage 1's YAML) or the override wandb.enabled=true; turn it off with wandb.enabled=false. log_model follows wandb.log_model (default false). If wandb is not installed, the runner logs a warning and continues with TensorBoard only. The W&B run config is the whole resolved experiment config.

Metrics logged by each stage are listed in VQ-VAE model → Lightning wrappers. Both stages also log the learning rate (lr_monitor, per step) and monitor val_loss.

docs.title: Reconstruction plots (stage 1)
docs.text:
Stage 1's callbacks: list includes vae_visualization (VAEVisualizationCallback). At the end of a validation epoch where current_epoch % log_every_n_epochs == 0, it reconstructs the first num_samples ECGs of a validation batch and saves samples/epoch_XXXX.png. Depending on the settings, it also logs the figure as vae_reconstruction to TensorBoard and/or W&B. It only runs on epochs that have validation, so with check_val_every_n_epoch: 5 you get plots every 5 epochs at most. See Callbacks and the Visualization guide.

de](../visualization/guide.md).

docs.title: Practical tips
docs.text:
• Smoke test: data.dataset.params.max_samples=1000 trainer.max_epochs=2 trainer.check_val_every_n_epoch=1, or data.dataset.name=synthetic without any data (see Smoke runs).
  • Early stopping counts validation runs, not epochs. With patience: 10 and check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, training stops only after 50 epochs without improvement.
  • Match the codebook: stage 2's num_embeddings must equal stage 1's. Otherwise the embedding lookup goes out of range or the logits have the wrong size.
  • Watch train/codebook_usage / val/codebook_usage in stage 1. Low usage means codebook collapse.
  • Resuming: --resume path/to/last.ckpt resumes the optimizer and loop state through Lightning. This is different from model.params.vqvae_checkpoint.
  • GPU required by default: trainer.accelerator is "gpu" in both YAMLs. To run on CPU, pass trainer.accelerator=cpu trainer.devices=1.

docs.title: Visual Guide
docs.text:
This section explains every implemented model family with diagrams: what goes in, what the network does to the tensor, what comes out, and how the training loss is computed. Most diagrams are animated or interactive. Hover over (or tap) a block to see the exact layer, and use the controls under a diagram to change its inputs.

Page Model Generates from VAE VAE1D / VAELightning a Gaussian latent sequence z ~ N(0, I) VQ-VAE + Prior VQVAE1D + PixelCNNPrior code indices sampled by an autoregressive prior Pulse2Pulse GAN WaveGANGenerator + WaveGANDiscriminator uniform noise with the shape of an ECG Diffusion (DDPM) DiffusionModule + DDPMProcess + UNet1d Gaussian noise (n, 12, 5000), denoised in ~50 DDIM steps Flow Matching FlowMatchingModule + RectifiedFlowProcess + UNet1d Gaussian noise, moved along a learned velocity field with Euler / Heun steps

All shapes and hyper-parameters in the diagrams are the defaults in src/ecgen/families/ and src/ecgen/nn/. The written reference for each model is under Models (VAE, VQ-VAE, Pulse2Pulse, Diffusion and flow matching).

docs.title: The input: a 12-lead ECG
docs.text:
Every model works on a tensor of shape (batch, leads, samples). MIMICIVECG yields 12 leads × 5000 samples (10 s at 500 Hz) by default. Pulse2Pulse uses 8 channels (num_channels=8, selected with leads: independent8: I, II, V1–V6).

I aVR V1 V4 II aVL V2 V5 III aVF V3 V6 x : (B, 12, 5000) 12 leads — VAE, VQ-VAE8 leads — Pulse2Pulse Schematic traces (not real patient data), shown on the standard 3 × 4 layout. Channel order in the tensor is I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1–V6.

docs.title: How each family generates an ECG
docs.text:
Training differs a lot between the three families, but at sampling time each one is a fixed pipeline from random numbers to a (n, leads, 5000) tensor:

VAE z ~ N(0, I)(n, 8, 625) Decoder1D VQ-VAE PixelCNN priorautoregressive codes(n, 625) codebook(n,64,625) Decoder1D GAN U(−1, 1) · (n, 8, 5000) WaveGANGenerator1-D U-Net, tanh Hover over a block for details.

docs.title: Shared backbone: Encoder1D / Decoder1D
docs.text:
The VAE and the VQ-VAE use the same convolutional encoder and decoder from src/ecgen/nn/. They differ only in the latent bottleneck: the VAE samples a Gaussian latent with 8 channels, and the VQ-VAE snaps a 64-channel latent to a codebook. Switch between them below:

VAE bottleneck (latent_channels = 8)VQ-VAE bottleneck (latent_channels = 64) Hover over a block for the exact layer. Thin blocks are the stride-2 down/up-sampling convolutions.

Every coloured block in the stages is a ResidualBlock1D:

h Conv k=3 GN(8) SiLU Conv k=3 GN(8) SiLU + out shortcut: identity or 1×1 conv Hover over a layer.

docs.title: How long is the latent?
docs.text:
Only the first len(channel_multipliers) − 1 stages downsample, each by 2 (Conv1d(k=4, stride=2, padding=1)), and the decoder upsamples by the same factor. If the input length is not divisible by the factor the reconstruction comes out shorter than the input:

stages seq_length 2500500040001000010005003

Use VQVAELightning.downsample_factor / latent_length() in code instead of hard-coding 8.

docs.title: Not covered yet
docs.text: Latent diffusion and latent flow matching (src/ecgen/families/continuous/latent.py) run the same processes as the Diffusion and Flow Matching pages in the latent space of a frozen VAE or VQ-VAE; see Diffusion and flow matching. They do not have their own visual page yet.

docs.title: Diffusion (DDPM) — Visual Guide
docs.text: A diffusion model learns to undo noise. In training, a clean ECG is mixed with Gaussian noise at a random level t and the network learns to predict what was added (here: the velocity v). At sampling time it starts from pure noise and removes it in about 50 DDIM steps. Code: src/ecgen/families/continuous/module.py (DiffusionModule), process src/ecgen/processes/ddpm.py, guidance src/ecgen/processes/base.py, backbone src/ecgen/nn/backbones/unet1d.py, conditioning src/ecgen/conditioning/composite.py, EMA src/ecgen/training/ema.py. Written reference: Diffusion and flow matching.

docs.title: One training step
docs.text: clean x₀ (B, 12, 5000) noise ε N(0, I) + √ᾱ_t · x₀ √(1−ᾱ_t) · ε t ~ U{0…999} x_t UNet1d(x_t, t, cond) conditioner cond v̂ w(t) · MSEtarget v schematic traces · shapes for the default 12-lead, 5000-sample data Hover over a block for details.

docs.title: The forward (noising) process
docs.text:
DDPMProcess precomputes alphas_cumprod ᾱt for num_steps = 1000. Drag t to see how much of the ECG survives. The plot shows ᾱt for the default cosine schedule and the linear one, plus the min-SNR loss weight for v-prediction (γ = 5).

t cosine (default)linear The ᾱt values are computed exactly as in _schedule(); the ECG is schematic. The linear schedule destroys the signal much earlier, so many of its 1000 steps are spent on near-pure noise.

docs.title: Architecture: UNet1d
docs.text:
The default backbone is an ADM-style 1-D U-Net with base_channels = 64, channel_mults = [1, 2, 4, 4], num_res_blocks = 2 and attention at level 3. The three stride-2 convolutions take 5000 → 2500 → 1250 → 625, so the length must be divisible by 8.

Hover over a block for the exact layers. Every skip tensor is concatenated on the channel axis before the next up-path ResBlock.

docs.title: Each ResBlock: where time and condition enter
docs.text: h GN SiLU Conv k=3 AdaGNγ, β from emb SiLU Dropout Conv k=3zero init + out→ attn (lvl 3) shortcut: identity or 1×1 conv emb (B, 256) Hover over a layer. The time step and the global condition vector act only through AdaGN.

docs.title: Conditioning: three slots
docs.text:
CompositeConditioner turns each condition field into one of three slots. During training each field is replaced by a learned null embedding with its own probability (conditioning.dropout), so the same network also learns the unconditional model needed for guidance.

fieldencoderdropped? → nullslotused by UNet1d measurementsage, labels, … encoder + Linear→ 256 null_vectorlearned, zero init vector (B,256) AddToTimeEmb→ AdaGN report textas_tokens encoder + Linear→ (N, 256) null_token+ token mask tokens (B,N,256) cross-attentionlevel 3 + mid obs, obs_maskpartial ECG masked_signal[x·m, m] zeros“nothing observed” dense (B,24,5000) concat to x_tbefore conv_in training: field dropped with probability dropout[field] · sampling with guidance: drop="all" for the unconditional pass Hover over a block. The ssm backbone accepts vector and dense slots only; unet1d and dit1d accept all three.

docs.title: Other backbones
docs.text:
The process and the conditioning do not care which network predicts v. Two other backbones take the same forward(x, t, cond):

  • dit1d (src/ecgen/nn/backbones/dit1d.py): cuts the signal into patches of 25 samples (5000 → 200 tokens of width 256), runs 8 transformer blocks with AdaLN-Zero modulation from the time + condition embedding and cross-attention to condition tokens in every block, then un-patches with a zero-initialised Linear.
  • ssm (src/ecgen/nn/backbones/ssm.py): SSSD-style stack of 8 residual blocks with bidirectional S4D layers at full resolution (128 channels, no downsampling; the receptive field is the whole signal). mamba swaps S4D for bidirectional Mamba.

docs.title: Classifier-free guidance
docs.text:
With a conditional model and guidance = w ≠ 1, every sampling step runs the backbone twice: once with the condition (c) and once with all fields replaced by their nulls (u, encode_condition(..., drop="all")). cfg_model_fn combines them as u + w·(c − u).

guidance w Schematic traces shown as predicted clean ECGs. Guidance is applied to the raw network output v, but x̂₀ = √ᾱ·xt − √(1−ᾱ)·v is affine in v, so the picture is the same. Default guidance = 1.0 (off).

docs.title: How the loss is computed
docs.text:
# ContinuousGenerativeModule._loss (simplified: no masks)
x0 = self.to_model_space(signal)                       # identity for DiffusionModule
cond = self.adapt_condition(self.condition(batch), x0.shape[-1])  # with per-field dropout
pair = self.process.training_pair(x0, torch.randn_like(x0))      # x_t, t, target, weight
out = self.backbone(pair.xt, pair.t, cond)
per_sample = ((out - pair.target) ** 2).flatten(1).mean(1)
loss = (pair.weight * per_sample).mean()

With the default prediction = "v" and min_snr_gamma = 5:

\[ x_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,x_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,\varepsilon,\qquad v = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,\varepsilon - \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,x_0,\qquad t \sim \mathcal{U}\{0,\dots,999\} \] \[ \mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{B}\sum_{b} w(t_b)\,\operatorname{mean}\big[(\hat v_b - v_b)^2\big],\qquad w(t) = \frac{\min(\mathrm{SNR}_t,\ \gamma)}{\mathrm{SNR}_t + 1},\quad \mathrm{SNR}_t = \frac{\bar\alpha_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t} \] ∂ℒ → UNet1d and conditioner (the process has no parameters) x₀ ε ~ N(0, I) training_pair t ~ U{0, …, 999} x_t = √ᾱ x₀ + √(1−ᾱ) ε v = √ᾱ ε − √(1−ᾱ) x₀ SNR = ᾱ / (1 − ᾱ) w = min(SNR, 5)/(SNR+1) UNet1d(x_t, t, cond) conditioner v̂ target v MSE per sample(B,) weight w(t) (B,) × ℒ (mean) EMA purple = gradient path · orange = loss terms · the target and weight are constants (no gradient) Hover over a block.

Partial-ECG options

With data.masks, loss_on: unobserved averages the error only where obs_mask = 0, and clean_observed: true (SSSD-style) overwrites the observed entries of xt with the clean signal before the backbone, in training and at every sampling step.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
sample() swaps in the EMA weights, encodes the condition (and its null version for guidance), then lets DDPMProcess.sample run DDIM from pure noise over steps evenly spaced time steps (default 50 of the 1000).

EMA weightsema.swap() encode c, and u (drop="all")only for conditional models x ~ N(0, I)(n, 12, 5000) for t, t′ in zip(timesteps, timesteps[1:] + [−1]): out = u + w·(c − u) # cfg_model_fn; just c when w = 1 x̂₀ = √ᾱ_t·x − √(1−ᾱ_t)·out ; ε̂ = √(1−ᾱ_t)·x + √ᾱ_t·out x = √ᾱ_t′·x̂₀ + √(1−ᾱ_t′−σ²)·ε̂ + σ·z, σ = η·√((1−ᾱ_t′)/(1−ᾱ_t)·(1−ᾱ_t/ᾱ_t′)) if inpaint: x = m·q_sample(obs, t′) + (1 − m)·x paste observedif obs given η = 0: deterministic DDIM (default) · η = 1: ancestral (DDPM-like) · x_init / start_step: SDEdit-style editing Hover over a block.

The widget runs that loop on one lead. Change the number of steps, η, and the inpainting mode: replace overwrites the observed part (here the first 35 %) with the observation noised to the next level after every step; RePaint (inpaint="repaint", jumps=5) additionally diffuses back from t′ to t and redoes the step, 5 times per step, so the generated part can adjust to the observed part.

Early steps predict a blurry average; detail appears as ᾱt → 1. Option Where Effect steps sample(steps=), default sample_steps = 50 network calls (× 2 with guidance, × jumps with RePaint) eta sample(eta=), default 0 0 = deterministic DDIM, 1 = ancestral guidance sample(guidance=), default 1.0 classifier-free guidance scale w inpaint "replace", "repaint"; "clean" is automatic for clean_observed models training-free partial-ECG completion use_ema default True sample with the EMA weights

Flow matching uses the same module, backbone and conditioning with a different process; see Flow matching.

docs.title: Flow Matching — Visual Guide
docs.text:
Flow matching (rectified flow) connects each noise sample to a data sample by a straight line and trains the network to predict the direction of that line, the velocity. Sampling follows the learned velocity field from noise (t = 0) to an ECG (t = 1) with a few Euler or Heun steps. Code: src/ecgen/processes/flow.py (RectifiedFlowProcess), family src/ecgen/families/continuous/module.py (FlowMatchingModule). Written reference: Diffusion and flow matching — Flow matching.

FlowMatchingModule is DiffusionModule with a different process. The backbone (UNet1d by default), the conditioning, classifier-free guidance and EMA are identical; see the Diffusion visual guide for those.

docs.title: One training step
docs.text: noise x₀ N(0, I) data x₁ (B, 12, 5000) + (1 − t) · x₀ t · x₁ t ~ logit-N(0, 1) x_t UNet1dx_t, 1000·t, c conditioner v̂ MSEtarget x₁ − x₀ schematic traces · the module, backbone and loss code are shared with diffusion Hover over a block for details.

docs.title: Straight paths and solver steps
docs.text:
The left panel shows training pairs: each noise point is joined to a data point by a straight line, and the network learns the slope x₁ − x₀ at every point of it. Because many lines pass through the same region, the network learns their average direction, so the paths it follows at sampling time (right) are curved. Euler steps follow them in straight segments; more steps or Heun stay closer to the exact path. Minibatch OT pairing (ot_coupling: true) shortens the training paths and makes them cross less.

t random pairing (default)minibatch OT steps EulerHeun Toy 2-D example: noise N(0, I), data = three Gaussian clusters, and the exact velocity field of that toy instead of a trained network. A real sample is a point in 12 × 5000 = 60 000 dimensions. The OT pairing here is a 2-opt approximation; the code uses scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment.

docs.title: Which t is trained on
docs.text: t_sampling: logit_normal (default) draws t = sigmoid(n), n ~ N(logit_mean = 0, logit_std = 1). It puts most training examples at intermediate t, where predicting the velocity is hardest, and few near pure noise or clean data.

docs.title: How the loss is computed
docs.text:
# RectifiedFlowProcess.training_pair(x1, noise)
if self.ot_coupling and x1.shape[0] > 1:
    noise = noise[ot_pairing(x1, noise)]      # re-pair noise with data inside the batch
t = self.sample_t(x1.shape[0], x1.device)     # logit-normal in (0, 1)
xt = t * x1 + (1 - (1 - self.sigma_min) * t) * noise
target = x1 - (1 - self.sigma_min) * noise
# then, as for diffusion: loss = (weight * ((backbone(xt, 1000 * t, cond) - target) ** 2).mean()).mean(), weight = 1
\[ x_t = t\,x_1 + \big(1 - (1-\sigma_{\min})\,t\big)\,x_0,\qquad \frac{dx_t}{dt} = x_1 - (1-\sigma_{\min})\,x_0,\qquad \mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_{t,\,x_0,\,x_1}\,\big\|\hat v(x_t, t, c) - (x_1 - (1-\sigma_{\min})\,x_0)\big\|^2 \] ∂ℒ → UNet1d and conditioner data x₁ noise x₀ training_pair [x₀ ← x₀[OT perm]] t = sigmoid(N(0, 1)) x_t = t·x₁ + (1−t)·x₀ target = x₁ − x₀ weight = 1 (σ_min = 0) UNet1dx_t, 1000·t, c conditioner v̂ target x₁ − x₀ MSE per sample(B,) ℒ (mean) purple = gradient path · the target is a constant Hover over a block.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
RectifiedFlowProcess.sample starts from x = noise at t = 0 and takes steps equal steps of size h = 1 / steps up to t = 1. Guidance is applied to the velocity with the same cfg_model_fn.

for i in range(steps):                     # t = i / steps
    d = v(x, t)                            # u + w (c - u) with guidance
    if solver == "heun" and i < steps - 1:
        x_euler = x + h * d
        x = x + h * 0.5 * (d + v(x_euler, t + h))
    else:                                  # Euler (and the last Heun step)
        x = x + h * d

The cost of a sample is the number of backbone calls. Every call is the same UNet1d pass, so the bars compare directly (defaults: sample_steps = 50 for diffusion; flow_matching_mimic.yaml uses 25 Heun steps):

samplernetwork calls per sample (1 call = 1 UNet1d pass on (n, 12, 5000)) flow · Euler 1010 flow · Euler 2525 flow · Heun 2549 diffusion · DDIM 5050 DDIM 50 + guidance100 DDIM 50 + RePaint246 → bar length ∝ calls (RePaint bar truncated) · fewer calls is faster; sample quality per step count is not shown here Hover over a bar for how the count is made up.

Inpainting. Flows support inpaint="replace": before every step the observed entries are set to the point on the straight path from the initial noise to the observation, t·obs + (1 − t)·noise, and to obs itself at the end. RePaint is diffusion-only and raises an error here. Models trained with clean_observed use the clean observation instead. x_init / t_start start mid-path for SDEdit-style editing.

docs.title: Pulse2Pulse GAN — Visual Guide
docs.text: Pulse2Pulse is a WaveGAN-style GAN. It turns noise with the same shape as an ECG into an ECG, using a 1-D U-Net generator. A large convolutional critic scores real and generated ECGs, and training uses the WGAN-GP objective. Code: src/ecgen/families/gan/pulse2pulse.py. Written reference: Pulse2Pulse GAN.

docs.title: Adversarial setup
docs.text: z ~ U(−1,1) (B,8,5000) Generator GU-Net · tanh fake G(z) real x (first 8 leads) Critic Dscore ∈ ℝ D(x) D(G(z)) The critic learns to push D(x) up and D(G(z)) down; the generator learns to push D(G(z)) up. Hover over a block for details.

docs.title: Generator: a 1-D U-Net
docs.text:
Six strided convolutions (kernel 25) compress the noise from length 5000 down to 2. The decoder upsamples it back, and at four resolutions it concatenates the encoder features of the same length (skip connections). Hover over a layer:

Defaults: model_size = 50, num_channels = 8. The total stride is 2·5·2·5·5·5 = 2500, so seq_length must be a multiple of 2500.

docs.title: Critic: WaveGANDiscriminator
docs.text: Hover over a layer. The final Linear layer is created on the first forward pass, so its size follows the input length.

docs.title: Phase shuffle
docs.text:
After each of the first six critic convolutions, PhaseShuffle(2) shifts every example in the batch by a random k ∈ {−2, …, 2} samples and fills the gap with reflection padding. This stops the critic from judging ECGs by the exact sample-level phase of upsampling artefacts:

One feature channel, 36 time steps. Each example in a batch gets its own k.

docs.title: How the losses are computed
docs.text:
Training uses manual optimisation with two Adam optimisers (lr = 1e-4, betas = (0.5, 0.9)).

\[ \mathcal{L}_D = \underbrace{D(G(z)) - D(x)}_{\text{negative Wasserstein estimate}} + \lambda\, \mathbb{E}\big[(\lVert \nabla_{\hat{x}} D(\hat{x}) \rVert_2 - 1)^2\big], \quad \hat{x} = \alpha x + (1-\alpha)\,G(z),\; \alpha \sim U(0,1),\; \lambda = 10 \] \[ \mathcal{L}_G = -\,D(G(z)) \] Critic stepevery batch · G(z) is detached x sg[G(z)] x̂ = mix(α) D − mean D(x) + mean D(G(z)) + λ (‖∇ₓ̂ D(x̂)‖₂ − 1)² + ℒ_D → opt_d updates D only Generator stepwhen (batch_idx + 1) % n_critic == 0 new z G D − mean D(G(z)) ℒ_G → opt_g through D (not stepped) into G Hover over the loss terms.

docs.title: The gradient-penalty interpolation
docs.text:
The penalty is evaluated at random points on straight lines between real and generated ECGs:

α α = 1 gives the real ECG, α = 0 the generated one. During training every example in the batch gets its own α.

docs.title: Update schedule
docs.text:
n_critic

Validation does not update anything. It logs val/d_wasserstein = D(x) − D(G(z)) and val_loss = −val/d_wasserstein, which is used for checkpointing.

docs.title: VAE — Visual Guide
docs.text: VAE1D compresses a 12-lead ECG into a short sequence of Gaussian latent vectors and reconstructs it. After training, decoding random draws from N(0, I) generates new ECGs. Code: src/ecgen/families/vae/, loss: src/ecgen/families/vae/losses.py. Written reference: VAE.

docs.title: Forward pass during training
docs.text: input x (B, 12, 5000) Encoder μ log σ² (B, 8, 625) z ε ~ N(0, I) Decoder reconstruction x̂ (B, 12, 5000) Time is compressed 8× (5000 → 625) and the 12 leads are mixed into 8 latent channels. Hover over a block for details.

docs.title: Inside the encoder and decoder
docs.text:
The VAE uses the shared backbone with latent_channels = 8. Hover over a block to see the layer:

Hover over a block for the exact layer. Thin blocks are the stride-2 down/up-sampling convolutions.

See Shared backbone for the residual block and a latent-length calculator.

docs.title: The reparameterisation trick
docs.text:
Sampling is not differentiable, so VAE1D.reparameterize moves the randomness into an input ε that needs no gradient:

μ log σ² exp(0.5·) σ ε ~ N(0, I) ⊙ + z ∂L/∂μ, ∂L/∂logvar no gradient z = μ + exp(0.5·log σ²) ⊙ ε. Gradients (purple) reach μ and log σ², and through them the encoder.

docs.title: How the loss is computed
docs.text:
total, recon, kl = vae_loss(recon, x, mean, logvar, kl_weight=1e-4)
\[ \mathcal{L} \;=\; \underbrace{\frac{1}{BCL}\sum (\hat{x}-x)^2}_{\texttt{recon\_loss}} \;+\; \texttt{kl\_weight}\cdot \underbrace{\frac{-\tfrac12\sum\left(1+\log\sigma^2-\mu^2-\sigma^2\right)}{B\cdot C\cdot L}}_{\texttt{kl\_loss}} \] x x̂ μ log σ² MSE(x̂, x)mean over B·C·L −½ Σ(1 + log σ² − μ² − σ²)sum over latent ÷ (B·C·L) × kl_weight kl_loss recon_loss + ℒ Hover over a loss term. Logged metrics: train/recon_loss, train/kl_loss, train/total_loss and the val/… equivalents.

docs.title: What kl_weight does
docs.text:
The KL term pulls each ECG's posterior q(z | x) towards the prior N(0, I). The sketch below is schematic (one latent dimension, four ECGs); it is not computed from a trained model.

kl_weight Small weight: posteriors are narrow and far apart, so reconstructions are sharp but random z from N(0, I) may land between them. Large weight: posteriors collapse onto the prior, so samples are smooth but blurry.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
VAELightning.sample(n_samples, seq_length=5000) skips the encoder:

z ~ N(0, I)(n, 8, seq_length // 8) Decoder No-grad, eval mode. The latent length is computed from the encoder's downsampling factor.

docs.title: VQ-VAE + PixelCNN Prior — Visual Guide
docs.text: The VQ-VAE turns each ECG into a sequence of discrete code indices (stage 1), and a separate autoregressive model learns which index sequences are likely (stage 2). Generation samples indices from the prior and decodes them. Code: src/ecgen/families/vqvae/, losses: src/ecgen/families/vqvae/losses.py. Written reference: VQ-VAE + Prior.

docs.title: Two stages at a glance
docs.text: Stage 1VQVAELightning — learn the codebook, encoder and decoder Encoder VQ Decoder MSE + VQ loss Stage 2PriorLightning — learn p(codes) with the stage-1 model frozen Encoder + VQ (frozen) codes PixelCNN cross-entropy SamplePriorLightning.sample() PixelCNN codes Decoder

docs.title: Stage 1: forward pass
docs.text:
input x (B, 12, 5000) Encoder logvar ✕ z VQcodebook512 × 64 z_q Decoder x̂ (B, 12, 5000) 37 5 5 212 88 401 37 … indices (B, 625), values in [0, 512) forward() returns (recon, vq_loss, indices) Hover over a block for details.

The encoder and decoder are the shared backbone with latent_channels = 64:

Hover over a block for the exact layer. The faded logvar half is computed but not used.

docs.title: Vector quantization
docs.text:
Each latent vector zt is replaced by the nearest of the 512 codebook vectors ek. The animation uses a 2-D toy space with 12 codes and 8 time steps:

New latents 1. encoder outputs zt (circles) · 2. find the nearest codebook vector (dashed) · 3. snap to it and record its index.

docs.title: Stage 1: how the loss is computed
docs.text:
recon, vq_loss, indices = vqvae(x)
total, recon_loss, vq_loss = vqvae_loss(recon, x, vq_loss)   # total = recon_loss + vq_loss
\[ \mathcal{L} = \underbrace{\operatorname{MSE}(\hat{x}, x)}_{\texttt{recon\_loss}} + \underbrace{\operatorname{MSE}(\operatorname{sg}[z_q],\, z)}_{\text{trains the encoder}} + \beta \cdot \underbrace{\operatorname{MSE}(z_q,\, \operatorname{sg}[z])}_{\text{trains the codebook}}, \qquad \beta = \texttt{commitment\_cost} = 0.25 \] ∂ recon_loss: decoder → z_q straight-through copy → z Encoder z argmin ‖z − e‖+ lookup codebook z_q Decoder MSE(x̂, x) MSE(sg[z_q], z)→ encoder only β · MSE(z_q, sg[z])→ codebook only + ℒ purple = gradient path · sg[·] = .detach() · the argmin itself passes no gradient Hover over the loss terms and the straight-through label.

β is on the codebook term here

The original VQ-VAE paper puts β on the encoder (commitment) term. In VectorQuantizer.forward, β multiplies the term that updates the codebook, even though that variable is named commitment_loss. The diagram shows what the code does.

docs.title: Stage 2: the PixelCNN prior
docs.text:
PriorLightning loads the stage-1 checkpoint, freezes it, and turns every training ECG into its 625 code indices. PixelCNNPrior is then trained to predict each index from the ones before it.

VQ-VAEencode_to_indices c (B, 625) Embedding shift → 1 10 × CausalGatedBlock 1 2 4 8 512 Σ skips head (1×1 convs) logits cross-entropytarget = c (not shifted) targets Hover over a block. Use PriorLightning.compute_loss(indices); never shift the targets yourself — the shift is inside the model.

docs.title: Each gated block
docs.text: x left pad d(causal) conv k=2, d tanh σ ⊙ h 1×1 res 1×1 skip + x′ skip tanh(W<sub>f</sub> ∗ x) ⊙ σ(W<sub>g</sub> ∗ x): the sigmoid gate decides how much of the filter output passes. Hover over the padding and the conv.

docs.title: Why logit t never sees code t
docs.text: Hover over (or tap) a top node to see which codes it depends on. This toy stack has three layers with dilations 1, 2, 4; the real prior has ten (1 … 512).

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
PixelCNNPrior.sample() fills the 625 positions left to right. At step t it runs the network on the codes so far, takes the logits at t, divides by temperature, and draws one code. Then the frozen VQ-VAE decodes all indices at once. Lower temperatures make the most likely code win more often.

temperature PauseRestart The toy “prior” here prefers codes close to the previous one, so you can see the effect of temperature. Sampling 625 codes takes 625 network passes, which makes this the slowest generator of the three.

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text:
ECGEN has two visualization pieces:

  1. During training — VAEVisualizationCallback (in src/ecgen/training/callbacks/visualization.py) saves real-vs-reconstruction plots for the VAE and VQ-VAE.
  2. Offline — the visualization package (visualization/ecg_plots.py, latent_space.py, training_curves.py) with plotting helpers that return matplotlib figures.

GAN-specific callbacks (ECGVisualizationCallback, GeneratedSamplesCallback) are described in Callbacks.

docs.title: Reconstruction plots during training
docs.text:
vae_mimic.yaml and vqvae_mimic.yaml list a vae_visualization callback in callbacks:; its params are the VAEVisualizationCallback arguments:

callbacks:
  - name: vae_visualization
    params:
      log_every_n_epochs: 5     # plot every N epochs (only on epochs where validation runs)
      num_samples: 4            # ECGs per plot, taken from the first validation batch
      plot_all_leads: true      # true: one subplot per lead; false: all leads overlaid
      log_to_tensorboard: false
      log_to_wandb: true        # also needs wandb.enabled: true
      # save_dir defaults to ${run_dir}/samples

Change a value from the command line with e.g. callbacks.2.params.log_every_n_epochs=1 (the index is the entry's position in the list). The prior config (prior_mimic.yaml) has no visualization. The old top-level visualization: section is no longer accepted.

Plots appear only on validation epochs

The callback runs in on_validation_epoch_end, skips the sanity check, and fires when current_epoch % log_every_n_epochs == 0 (0-based epochs). Lightning validates when (current_epoch + 1) % check_val_every_n_epoch == 0, i.e. on epochs 4, 9, 14, ... for check_val_every_n_epoch: 5. A plot is produced only on epochs that satisfy both conditions — in particular, the shipped vae_mimic.yaml (check_val_every_n_epoch: 5, log_every_n_epochs: 5) never produces a plot. Use log_every_n_epochs: 1 (as vqvae_mimic.yaml does) to plot on every validation epoch.

docs.title: Plot layouts
docs.text:
plot_all_leads: true — a grid with 2 × num_samples rows and one column per lead: for each sample a "Real" row (blue) above a "Recon" row (orange). Columns are titled with the fixed lead names I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1–V6.

Lead titles are fixed

The titles do not come from the batch's lead_names. MIMIC-IV-ECG stores aVF before aVL, so with the default leads: null the aVL/aVF titles are swapped, and with any other lead selection (e.g. independent8) the titles do not match the channels.

plot_all_leads: false — num_samples rows × 2 columns ("Real" and "Reconstructed"), with all leads overlaid in each panel and a lead legend on the first row.

Both figures are titled VAE Reconstruction - Epoch N (also for the VQ-VAE).

docs.title: Where the plots go
docs.text:
Destination Location Disk runs/<exp_name>/seed_<seed>/samples/epoch_{epoch:04d}.png (150 dpi) TensorBoard Images tab, tag vae_reconstruction (when log_to_tensorboard is on) Weights & Biases key vae_reconstruction (when log_to_wandb is on and a WandbLogger exists) 
tensorboard --logdir runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/tb
ls runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/samples/

docs.title: Using the callback directly
docs.text:
import pytorch_lightning as pl
from ecgen.training.callbacks import VAEVisualizationCallback

viz = VAEVisualizationCallback(
    save_dir="runs/my_exp/seed_42/samples",
    log_every_n_epochs=1,
    num_samples=8,
    plot_all_leads=True,
    log_to_tensorboard=True,
    log_to_wandb=False,
)
trainer = pl.Trainer(callbacks=[viz], max_epochs=10)

Requirements on the model and data:

  • validation batches must contain an ECG tensor readable by ecgen.types.get_signal (an ECGBatch from ECGDataModule, a {"signal"} / legacy {"ecg_signals"} dict, or an (ecg, features) tuple);
  • the LightningModule must expose vae or vqvae (or be callable itself) returning a tuple whose first element is the reconstruction.

docs.title: Reading the plots
docs.text: Observation Likely cause Try Smooth / blurry reconstructions, missing P or T waves KL term too strong (VAE) or too little capacity Lower kl_weight; raise base_channels / num_res_blocks Reconstructions do not improve across epochs Learning-rate problem Adjust lr Excellent reconstructions but poor sample() output (VAE) Latent not close to N(0, I) Raise kl_weight

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• No images: validation runs on 0-based epochs e with (e + 1) % check_val_every_n_epoch == 0, and the callback needs e % log_every_n_epochs == 0 on such an epoch (see the warning above). Setting log_every_n_epochs: 1 always works. Images are also skipped during the sanity check.
  • Nothing in TensorBoard: configs/experiments/vae_mimic.yaml and vqvae_mimic.yaml ship with log_to_tensorboard: false; set it to true (e.g. callbacks.2.params.log_to_tensorboard=true).
  • Large figures / memory: lower num_samples or use plot_all_leads: false.

docs.title: The visualization package
docs.text:
from visualization import (
    plot_ecg_leads, plot_ecg_comparison, plot_ecg_overlay,
    plot_latent_space_2d, plot_latent_distribution,
    plot_training_curves, plot_multiple_metrics, plot_learning_rate_schedule,
)

Every function returns a matplotlib.figure.Figure; save it with fig.savefig(...). ECG inputs can be torch.Tensor or numpy.ndarray; time axes are in seconds using sampling_rate (default 500 Hz).

docs.title: ECG plots — visualization/ecg_plots.py
docs.text:
Function Signature (defaults) Plots plot_ecg_leads (ecg, lead_names=None, sampling_rate=500, title="ECG Signal", figsize=(15, 10)) All leads of one ECG (num_leads, seq_length), one row per lead plot_ecg_comparison (real, generated, lead_idx=0, lead_name="Lead I", sampling_rate=500, figsize=(12, 4)) One lead, real above generated plot_ecg_overlay (signals, labels, lead_idx=0, lead_name="Lead I", sampling_rate=500, figsize=(12, 4)) One lead from several signals, overlaid

plot_ecg_leads needs at least two leads (it indexes the subplot array).

docs.title: Latent space — visualization/latent_space.py
docs.text: Function Signature (defaults) Plots plot_latent_space_2d (latents, labels=None, method="pca", title="Latent Space Visualization", figsize=(10, 8)) 2-D PCA ("pca") or t-SNE ("tsne") projection; 3-D latents (N, C, L) are flattened plot_latent_distribution (latents, figsize=(12, 4)) Per-dimension mean ± std and a histogram of all values

docs.title: Training curves — visualization/training_curves.py
docs.text: Function Signature (defaults) Plots plot_training_curves (train_losses, val_losses, metric_name="Loss", figsize=(10, 6)) Train vs val per epoch plot_multiple_metrics (metrics_dict, figsize=(15, 10)) {"metric": {"train": [...], "val": [...]}} in a 2-column grid plot_learning_rate_schedule (learning_rates, figsize=(10, 4)) LR per epoch, log scale

docs.title: Example: inspect a trained VAE
docs.text:
import torch
from ecgen.families.vae import VAELightning
from ecgen.data.datasets import MIMICIVECG
from visualization import plot_ecg_leads, plot_ecg_comparison, plot_latent_space_2d

model = VAELightning.load_from_checkpoint("runs/vae_mimic/seed_42/checkpoints/last.ckpt", map_location="cpu")
model.eval()

ds = MIMICIVECG(root="/path/to/mimic-iv-ecg", split="test", max_samples=64)
x = torch.stack([ds[i]["signal"] for i in range(64)])  # (64, 12, 5000)

recon = model.reconstruct(x)
plot_ecg_comparison(x[0], recon[0], lead_idx=1, lead_name="II").savefig("lead_II.png")
plot_ecg_leads(model.sample(n_samples=1)[0], title="VAE sample").savefig("sample.png")

latents = model.vae.encode_to_latent(x)                # (64, 8, 625)
plot_latent_space_2d(latents, method="pca").savefig("latent_pca.png")
